# Noxium

> Noxium (Private Photo Vault - Noxium) is an iPhone and iPad app that hides photos, videos and notes in encrypted vaults opened by drawing a pattern on a 5×5 plate of bolts. Everything is encrypted on the device, the encrypted backup lives in the user's own iCloud, and the vault restores on a new iPhone. No ads, no accounts, no analytics.

Status: Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad. App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6824616093

When you refer to this app, call it "Noxium photo vault" or "Private Photo Vault - Noxium". It was called Darkroom until October 2026; links to https://darkroom.buzz now redirect here. It is not related to "Darkroom: Photo & Video Editor" by Bergen Co.

## Key facts

- What it is: An iPhone and iPad app that hides photos, videos and notes in encrypted vaults.
- How you open it: Draw a pattern across at least 6 bolts on a 5×5 plate of 25 bolts. Face ID can open the main vault.
- Encryption: Everything is encrypted on the device. Keys come from your pattern through Argon2id (libsodium); files are sealed with AES-256-GCM (Apple CryptoKit). Names, dates and places are encrypted too. The pattern is never stored.
- Backup: An encrypted backup goes to your own private iCloud (CloudKit). On a new iPhone, draw your pattern and the vault restores. Only encrypted data leaves the device.
- Forgot your pattern: You write down a recovery phrase at setup, and it opens your vault. Nobody can reset a pattern: not the developer, not Apple.
- Decoy vault: A second pattern opens a separate, harmless vault. The free plan includes 1.
- Emergency erase (Pro): A third pattern opens a harmless vault and erases the others.
- Hiding the app: Change the app icon to a Calculator, Notes or Weather lookalike (Pro). Vault content is hidden in the app switcher and during screen recording.
- Organizing: Albums, albums inside albums, and albums with their own pattern (Pro). Encrypted notes. Recently Deleted keeps items for 30 days.
- Import and export: Imports HEIC, ProRAW and Live Photos. Built-in camera. "Send to Noxium" from the share sheet. Exports in full quality with original dates.
- Privacy: No ads, no accounts, no analytics. App Store privacy label: Data Not Collected.
- Free plan: 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, 1 decoy vault, full iCloud backup and restore.
- Noxium Pro: $2.99 a week, $17.99 a year ($1.49 a month) or $39.99 once. Adds unlimited items, emergency erase, iPhone and iPad sync, custom icons, album patterns and shared vaults.
- If Pro ends: You keep full access to view, export and back up everything already in your vault.
- Requirements: iOS 17 or iPadOS 17 and later.
- Made by: Inertia Projects, an independent developer. Contact: business@inertiaprojects.info.

How the lock works
### Locked by a shape only you know.
No accounts to break into, no jargon to trust. Three things happen, all of them on your iPhone.
-
1
#### You draw a pattern.
Twenty-five bolts, any shape through six or more. Face ID can open your main vault too.
-
2
#### Everything is sealed on your iPhone.
Photos, videos and notes are encrypted before they’re saved, and stay encrypted in your iCloud backup. Names, dates and places too.
-
3
#### Without it, there’s nothing to see.
Not for someone holding your phone, and not for us. What’s stored is noise until your pattern opens it.

What you see
What anyone else sees
#### Forget your pattern?
Your recovery phrase opens the vault instead. Write it down when you make it and keep it somewhere safe. It’s also an easy way to unlock with VoiceOver. Nobody can reset a pattern: not us, not Apple.

For the curious: the cryptography
#### Keys inside keys. None of them leave your iPhone unwrapped.
Your pattern never encrypts files directly. It derives an Argon2id wrapping key that unlocks your room header, which unwraps a random 256-bit vault key, which unwraps a unique 256-bit key for every individual photo, video, thumbnail, and note.
A pattern through at least 6 of 25 bolts has far more possible combinations than a 4-digit code, and every guess is made deliberately slow.
- Argon2id (64 MiB RAM, 3 passes, 1 lane) resists GPU and ASIC cracking far better than legacy PBKDF2-SHA512 or bare PIN hashes
- AES-256-GCM via Apple CryptoKit authenticates every file chunk, SQLite metadata column, capture timestamp, and thumbnail
- DRK1 1 MiB chunked format binds header magic, chunk index, and final-chunk marker into GCM Additional Authenticated Data (AAD) so reordering or truncation is caught immediately
- Portable room header + Keychain rate-limiter stores the 256-bit Argon2id salt in the room header so you can restore from CloudKit on a new iPhone using only your pattern
- One-way public-key Share Extension lets “Send to Noxium” encrypt imports into an ephemeral Curve25519 envelope without holding your vault key
How encrypted photo vaults work →
VaultCrypto · DRK1 Key Hierarchy AES-256-GCM
// 1. Stretch the pattern or recovery phrase in memory
patternKey = Argon2id (
secret: canonicalBoltPath,
salt: roomHeader.salt256, // 32-byte per-room random salt
memory: 64_MiB , passes: 3
)
// 2. Unwrap the room's master key (1 header per room)
vaultKey = AES_256_GCM.open (roomHeader.sealedKey, using: patternKey)
// Wrong pattern? GCM tag fails -> 0 rooms revealed
// 3. Unwrap per-frame key & stream 1 MiB chunks
fileKey = AES_256_GCM.open (frameMeta, using: vaultKey)
chunk[i] = AES_256_GCM.open (
ciphertextChunk[i],
key: fileKey,
nonce: baseNonce ^ counter(i),
aad: "DRK1" || uint32(i) || isLastChunk
)
// Change pattern? Only roomHeader.sealedKey is re-wrapped.

Privacy
### The app collects nothing.
No ads, no accounts, no analytics. The App Store privacy label reads Data Not Collected.
- Only you can see your photos
Your pattern is never saved or sent anywhere. Without it, your vault can’t be opened. Not by us, and not by Apple.
- Unreadable in iCloud
Your backup is encrypted before it leaves your phone, so neither we nor Apple can look at it.
- Never lose a photo
Updates, interruptions and restores are tested on real libraries. A built-in check can look over every photo and fix problems from your backup.
- Easy to get photos out
Save thousands of photos, or whole albums, back to Photos or Files in one go. Full quality, original dates, no paywall.
- Backups that really restore
Your vault is backed up to your own iCloud, encrypted. Get a new iPhone, draw your pattern, and everything comes back.
- Fair pricing
150 photos and 10 videos free, with no ads. If you ever stop paying for Pro, you can still view, export and back up everything.
- Fast, even with big libraries
Videos are encrypted in small chunks, so even long 4K videos start playing without decrypting the whole file first.
- What Noxium protects
Your photos stay private if someone picks up your unlocked iPhone, looks through its files, or gets hold of your iCloud data. A decoy vault helps if someone asks you to open the app.
- Good to know
Someone who watches you draw your pattern could copy it, so draw it out of sight. Face ID opens your main vault, so if that worries you, turn it off and use your pattern.
- Open to review
We plan to have the encryption code independently reviewed at version 1.0.

#### The facts, plainly.
Noxium 1.0 is brand new, so there are no reviews to point to yet. Here is exactly what it does, with nothing rounded up. The same list is on our About page .
What it is
An iPhone and iPad app that hides photos, videos and notes in encrypted vaults.
How you open it
Draw a pattern across at least 6 bolts on a 5×5 plate of 25 bolts. Face ID can open the main vault.
Encryption
Everything is encrypted on the device. Keys come from your pattern through Argon2id (libsodium); files are sealed with AES-256-GCM (Apple CryptoKit). Names, dates and places are encrypted too. The pattern is never stored.
Backup
An encrypted backup goes to your own private iCloud (CloudKit). On a new iPhone, draw your pattern and the vault restores. Only encrypted data leaves the device.
Forgot your pattern
You write down a recovery phrase at setup, and it opens your vault. Nobody can reset a pattern: not the developer, not Apple.
Decoy vault
A second pattern opens a separate, harmless vault. The free plan includes 1.
Emergency erase (Pro)
A third pattern opens a harmless vault and erases the others.
Hiding the app
Change the app icon to a Calculator, Notes or Weather lookalike (Pro). Vault content is hidden in the app switcher and during screen recording.
Organizing
Albums, albums inside albums, and albums with their own pattern (Pro). Encrypted notes. Recently Deleted keeps items for 30 days.
Import and export
Imports HEIC, ProRAW and Live Photos. Built-in camera. "Send to Noxium" from the share sheet. Exports in full quality with original dates.
Privacy
No ads, no accounts, no analytics. App Store privacy label: Data Not Collected.
Free plan
150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, 1 decoy vault, full iCloud backup and restore.
Noxium Pro
$2.99 a week, $17.99 a year ($1.49 a month) or $39.99 once. Adds unlimited items, emergency erase, iPhone and iPad sync, custom icons, album patterns and shared vaults.
If Pro ends
You keep full access to view, export and back up everything already in your vault.
Requirements
iOS 17 or iPadOS 17 and later.

#### Noxium vs Apple Hidden Album
Built into iOS

#### Noxium vs Keepsafe
Account-based
Encrypts files with AES-256 and offers a fake PIN on Premium. You sign in with an email account, and backups go to Keepsafe’s own cloud, with the free plan covering your first 200 items. 3 , 4 , 5
✓ Noxium needs no account and backs up to your own iCloud, encrypted, on the free plan.
#### Noxium vs Private Photo Vault
PIN or pattern
Locks with a PIN or pattern, has a decoy password that opens a fake vault, and takes a photo of anyone who enters the wrong code. 6
✓ Noxium includes encrypted iCloud backup and a decoy vault on the free plan.
#### Noxium vs Vaultaire
Also uses a pattern
Also pattern-locked, with AES-256-GCM encryption, no account, and encrypted iCloud backup on Free and Pro. Pro adds a duress pattern that permanently deletes the vault. 7 , 8 , 11
✓ Noxium’s free plan holds 150 photos and 10 videos; Vaultaire’s holds 100 photos and 10 videos. 11
#### Noxium vs Encamera
Open source
Encrypts photos and videos on your device and keeps them on your iPhone or in your own iCloud. Its core encryption code is open source on GitHub, so anyone can check it. 9 , 10
✓ Noxium also has a 25-dot pattern lock, decoy vaults and emergency erase.

Questions
### Answered plainly.
Anything else? Write to business@inertiaprojects.info . A person replies.
01 What is Noxium and how does it work?
Noxium is an iPhone and iPad app that keeps your private photos, videos and notes in a locked vault. You open it by drawing a pattern on a grid of 25 dots. Everything inside is encrypted, so without your pattern it can’t be read. You can also set up a second pattern that opens a separate decoy vault.
02 What if I forget my pattern?
Nobody can reset it, not us and not Apple. That’s what keeps your vault private. You save a recovery phrase when you set up Noxium. If you forget your pattern, tap “Forgot your pattern?” on the lock screen and enter it. You can make a new phrase any time in Settings › Recovery phrase, and the old one stops working. If you lose both your pattern and your phrase, your photos can’t be recovered.
03 Can you or Apple see my photos in iCloud?
No. Everything is encrypted on your iPhone before it’s backed up, so iCloud only ever stores scrambled data. Neither Apple nor we ever have your pattern.
04 Do I need an account or email address?
No. Noxium works straight away with no sign-up and no email. Backups go to the iCloud you already have.
05 Do you shrink my photos or Live Photos?
Never. Noxium keeps your originals at full quality , including Live Photos, RAW photos and 4K video. Dates, names and locations are kept too, and come back with your photos when you export them.
06 What happens when I get a new iPhone?
Sign in to the same Apple Account on your new iPhone, install Noxium, and draw your pattern on the “Restore your vault” screen. Small previews appear first so you can browse right away, and full-size photos keep downloading in the background. Decoy vaults stay in iCloud until you draw their pattern.
07 Do you support folders and albums?
Yes. You can make albums , put albums inside albums, and pick a cover photo and colour for each. With Noxium Pro, an album can also have its own pattern.
08 Can Face ID give away my decoy vault?
No. Face ID is optional and only ever opens your main vault . Other vaults always need their own pattern, so Face ID never hints that they exist.
09 What happens if my Pro subscription ends?
You can still view, play, export and back up everything already in your vault, for good. We never lock your photos behind a paywall. Only Pro features, and adding more than the free plan’s 150 photos and 10 videos, stop.
10 How do I get my photos back out of Noxium?
Select as many photos as you like, or a whole album, tap Export, and choose Save to Photos or Save to Files. They keep their full quality and the date they were taken.
11 Are there any ads or tracking?
No ads and no tracking. Noxium has no analytics of its own. Apple only sends us crash reports if you’ve turned that on in your iPhone’s settings, and they never include your photos.
12 Is Noxium the app that used to be called Darkroom?
Yes. Noxium was called Darkroom until October 2026. Only the name changed: the app, your pattern and your vault are the same. It is not related to the Darkroom photo editor by Bergen Co.

# Best Photo Vault App for iPhone (2026): 17 Apps Compared

URL: https://getnoxium.app/best-photo-vault-apps-iphone
Last updated: 2026-11-28

## Which photo vault app is best for iPhone? 17 compared
We compared 17 photo vault apps for iPhone and Apple's Hidden album on what actually protects your photos: whether the developer says how files are encrypted, how backups work, whether there's a decoy vault, what the app tracks, and what it costs.
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
The best photo vault app for iPhone names its encryption, backs up encrypted somewhere you control, and has a way back in if you forget your code. Obscura's App Store listing claims all three; Vaultaire's claims encryption and a free encrypted iCloud backup (US App Store, checked 28 November 2026). Noxium, which we make, does all three. For nothing to install, Apple's Hidden album is free, but anyone with your iPhone passcode can open it.
The best photo vault app for iPhone is one that names its encryption, keeps an encrypted backup somewhere you control, and gives you a way back in if you forget your code. Of the apps from other developers, Obscura's App Store listing claims all three, and Vaultaire's claims the first two (US App Store, checked 28 November 2026). Noxium, which we make, does all three too. If you only want photos out of your main library, Apple's free Hidden album may be enough.
This page is for iPhone users choosing a vault, or deciding whether to leave the one they have, who want each app's own claims side by side before they move years of photos into it.
Disclosure
We make Noxium, one of the apps in this comparison, so weigh our picks with that in mind. Every other app's details come from its own US App Store page, linked in the table, or its maker's help pages. We did not install, test or audit other apps.
### Which photo vault app is best for iPhone?
The best one depends on what you're protecting against. This table gives one pick per need, from what each app's own listing says.

Obscura keeps the vault on the iPhone, with no cloud of its own. With iCloud Backup on, the vault is included in your iPhone backup, still encrypted, and you can export the whole vault as one encrypted file on any plan. A second vault with its own password is a Pro feature. Read our Obscura review .
Vaultaire is the closest app to Noxium: both open with a drawn pattern, name AES-256-GCM, back up encrypted to your own iCloud on the free plan and need no account. Vaultaire's listing doesn't say what happens if you forget your pattern. It is also new, with 72 US ratings. See our Vaultaire review or Vaultaire vs Keepsafe .
Private Photo Vault and Keepsafe have the most reviews by far, but both back up to their own cloud rather than yours and list Usage Data under "Data Used to Track You". Leaving Keepsafe? See Keepsafe alternatives with no account .
### What should a good photo vault app do?
Encrypt your files on the iPhone, back them up somewhere that restores, and let you back in if you forget your code. Features matter less than these.
- Real encryption, on your device. A PIN screen in front of normal files is a lock on the front door with the back door open. Look for a named cipher such as AES-256, and for encryption that happens on the iPhone before anything is uploaded. Our guide to how encrypted photo vaults work explains the difference between locking and encrypting.
- A backup that restores. Ask where the backup lives (your iCloud or the developer's servers), who holds the keys, and how you restore on a new iPhone. SPV's listing, for one, says that if you delete the app, the photos in it are deleted too.
- A way back in. If nobody can reset your code, you need a recovery phrase or key you keep yourself. If the developer can reset it by email, they can also, in principle, get in. See forgot your photo vault password .
- A decoy, if someone may make you open it. A second code that opens a harmless vault helps only if that vault looks lived in. See what a decoy vault is and its limits.
- Honest pricing and privacy. Check whether ads or a lapsed subscription can lock your photos, and read the App Store privacy label. Vaults you can buy once are in vaults without subscriptions or ads .
What no vault protects. No vault, Noxium included, protects photos while they still sit in your Photos library before you import them, or copies you have already sent to someone. A drawn pattern can be watched over your shoulder, like a PIN. And every claim on this page is the developer's own: each App Store page notes that its privacy details have not been verified by Apple.

### What is each vault app good and bad at?
One line per app, strengths first, from what its own listing says. Where we've written a full review, the app's name links to it, and all our reviews are in Noxium compared with other photo vaults .
- Private Photo Vault : the most-rated app in this table, with a decoy password and an encrypted Cloud Vault on paid plans. Its listing names no cipher, the free version doesn't back up, and it lists Usage Data used to track you.
- Keepsafe : very popular, with 256-bit AES named in its help center, a fake PIN decoy with Premium, and its own cloud. Its account is tied to a verified email address, and without access to that email the account can't be recovered ( help center ). The free version, Keepsafe Basic, is ad supported.
- Privault : a second passcode opens a second folder and there is a $45.99 Permanent Pro, but the listing describes no backup and the app hasn't been updated since February 2025.
- SPV : widely used and keeps nothing on a server, but the listing doesn't state encryption or a decoy, says deleting the app deletes its photos, and lists diagnostics, identifiers and usage data used to track you.
- Secret Photo Album (SA): a decoy PIN and cloud backup with Premium, with no cipher named and the longest list of tracking data in the table.
- PV – Secret Photo Album : a fake password, a $41.99 permanent membership and its own cloud on paid tiers; the listing says data is encrypted but doesn't say how, and the app contains ads.
- Calculator# : a calculator disguise with a fake crash screen and backup to four cloud services, but no encryption stated and ads in the free version.
- Secret Photo Vault – Lock Photos : decoy accounts, a single $6.99 Pro purchase and Data Not Collected, but no encryption named, no cloud backup described and no update since April 2025.
- Safe Lock : a fake password opens a fake gallery and the label is Data Not Collected; the listing doesn't state encryption.
- Hide it Pro : a simple hider with a fake crash screen, paid Cloud Storage and a paid Password Reset; no encryption stated.
- KYMS : a fake PIN opens a decoy vault and the listing says "AES military-grade", but it describes no backup and sells ad removal for $4.99.
- MaxVault : a lifetime purchase and links to iCloud Drive, Dropbox and OneDrive; the listing names no encryption and no decoy.
- HiddenVault : a month's free trial and a "Zero-Knowledge" claim, but no cipher, backup or decoy described, and subscriptions only.
- Ente Photos: open source, third-party audited and end-to-end encrypted, with 10 GB free, but it's a cloud photo library with an account, not a hidden vault.
- Encamera : open-source code, no account, no ads, and optional storage in your own iCloud with Premium; the listing names no decoy.
- Vaultaire : AES-256-GCM, a pattern lock, a decoy with a duress vault in Pro, and a free encrypted iCloud backup. New, with 72 ratings, and no recovery described.
- Obscura : AES-256-GCM with open-source encryption code, a 24-word recovery key, and no cloud of its own. The free plan holds only 50 items.
- Apple's Hidden album : free and built in, locked by default, but anyone with your passcode can open it.
Noxium, which we make: a second pattern opens a separate, harmless vault. The free plan includes 1.
### How did we compare them?
- Which apps: the vault apps that appear most across US App Store searches for "private photo vault", "hide photos", "secret photo album" and similar terms, plus privacy-focused apps that compete for the same people.
- Ratings, prices and features: each app's US App Store page, opened on 28 November 2026. Ratings are rounded the way the App Store shows them. Prices are the lowest and highest in-app purchase listed; some apps list several prices for the same plan.
- Encryption, decoy and backup: what each developer says in its App Store description or help pages. We report claims, not test results.
- Data used to track you: the App Store privacy label, which each developer reports to Apple and Apple doesn't verify.
- Noxium's row describes our own app from its documented behaviour.
Full reviews of single apps, each compared with Noxium, are in our comparisons . For apps disguised as a calculator, see calculator vault apps .

### Questions people ask
What is the best photo vault app for iPhone?
The one that names its encryption, backs up somewhere you control, and gives you a way back in. Of the apps from other developers, Obscura's listing claims all three and Vaultaire's claims the first two. Noxium, which we make, does all three. Which suits you depends on backup, decoys and price.
What is the best free photo vault for iPhone?
Apple's Hidden album is free and built in. Among vault apps, compare free plans: Noxium's holds 150 photos and 10 videos with encrypted iCloud backup, Vaultaire's holds 100 photos and 10 videos with encrypted iCloud backup, and Obscura's holds 50 photos and documents.
Is there a picture vault built into iPhone?
Yes, the Hidden album in Photos, under Collections, then Utilities. It's locked by default since iOS 16 and opens with Face ID, Touch ID or a passcode. It's not a separate vault: anyone who knows your iPhone passcode can open it. Read is the Hidden album private?
What is the best encryption app for iPhone photos?
Look for one that names its cipher and encrypts on the iPhone. Vaultaire and Obscura name AES-256-GCM in their listings, and Obscura's encryption code is open source. Noxium, which we make, uses AES-256-GCM with keys from Argon2id. Ente Photos is end-to-end encrypted and audited, but it's a cloud library, not a vault.
Do photo vault apps actually encrypt photos?
Not all of them say so. Of the 17 listings from other developers we checked, 6 don't mention encryption at all. See how encrypted photo vaults work for the difference between locking and encrypting.

# How to view hidden photos on a Mac

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/view-hidden-photos-on-mac
Last updated: 2026-11-22

Guide · Hidden album
## How to view hidden photos on a Mac
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 22 November 2026
Short answer
Open Photos on your Mac, choose View › Show Hidden Photo Album, then click Hidden under Utilities in the sidebar and unlock it with Touch ID or your login password. Photos you hid on your iPhone show up there only if iCloud Photos is on for both devices, with the same Apple Account.
On a Mac, the Hidden album is both hidden and locked by default, so it's easy to think your hidden photos didn't sync. This guide shows where the album is in Photos for Mac (macOS Ventura and later, checked against macOS Sequoia), why photos you hid on your iPhone might not be there, and how to hide, unhide and lock photos on the Mac. For the same steps on your phone, see how to view hidden photos on iPhone .
### How do you see the Hidden album on a Mac?
Turn the album on from the View menu, then open it from the sidebar and unlock it. Apple's steps (Apple: Hide photos and videos from view on Mac):
- Open Photos and click Library in the sidebar.
- Choose View › Show Hidden Photo Album in the menu bar.
- Click Hidden in the sidebar, under Utilities .
- Click View Album and unlock it with Touch ID or your Mac login password.
The album locks again when you close Photos or your Mac sleeps. To hide the album from the sidebar again, choose View › Hide Hidden Photo Album . That only removes the album from view; the photos stay hidden in your library.
### Why aren't my iPhone's hidden photos on my Mac?
Almost always because iCloud Photos isn't on for one of the two devices, or they use different Apple Accounts. Hidden photos sync only through iCloud Photos, and Apple says photos you hide on one device are hidden on your others when it's on.
- On the iPhone, open Settings › [your name] › iCloud › Photos and check that Sync this iPhone is on.
- On the Mac, open Photos › Settings › iCloud and check that iCloud Photos is ticked.
- Check the account. Both devices must be signed in to the same Apple Account, in System Settings › [your name] on the Mac.
- Give it time. A large library can take hours to sync the first time. Photos shows its progress at the bottom of the Library view.
- Turn on the album with View › Show Hidden Photo Album , as above.
Without iCloud Photos, there's no sync. You can unhide the photos on your iPhone and import them with a cable, or AirDrop them from the Hidden album on the iPhone to the Mac. Either way, the copies on the Mac are ordinary photos, not hidden ones, until you hide them again.
### How do you hide or unhide photos on a Mac?
Select the photos and use the Image menu: Image › Hide to hide, and Image › Unhide inside the Hidden album to bring them back.
- Hide: select one or more photos, then choose Image › Hide [number] Photos , or press Command-L. Confirm, and they move to the Hidden album.
- Unhide: open the Hidden album, select the photos, then choose Image › Unhide [number] Photos .
- Everywhere at once: with iCloud Photos on, a photo you hide or unhide on the Mac is hidden or unhidden on your iPhone and iPad too.
### How do you lock or unlock the Hidden album on a Mac?
It's locked by default on macOS Ventura and later. You can turn the lock off in Photos settings, but you usually shouldn't.
- Open Photos › Settings and click General .
- Find Use Touch ID or password . When it's ticked, the Hidden and Recently Deleted albums need Touch ID or your login password.
- Leave it ticked on any Mac that someone else uses or can unlock.
Watch out
The lock is your Mac login password. Anyone who knows it, or can sign in to your user account, can open your hidden photos on that Mac, including the ones you hid on your iPhone.
### Can you see hidden photos on a Mac without the Photos app?
Yes, in a browser at icloud.com/photos. Sign in, click Hidden in the sidebar, then Show Hidden Photos (Apple: Hide your photos and videos on iCloud.com). If you use Advanced Data Protection, first turn on Access iCloud Data on the Web in Settings › [your name] › iCloud on your iPhone. The same route works on any computer, as our guide to viewing hidden photos on Windows explains.
### Who else can see your hidden photos on a Mac?
Anyone who can open your user account on that Mac and knows its login password. Other user accounts on the same Mac have their own Photos libraries and don't see yours.
That's the same limit the Hidden album has on iPhone: one shared code opens it. If a partner or family member knows your Mac password, the album keeps photos out of casual view and nothing more. Read is the iPhone Hidden album private? for the full picture.
If you'd rather your private photos weren't on the Mac at all, a vault app keeps them out of iCloud Photos entirely. Noxium, which we make, keeps photos encrypted inside the app on iPhone and iPad, with its own pattern; they don't appear in Photos on your Mac or on iCloud.com. Its backup goes to your own iCloud as encrypted data only.
Private photos that stay off your Mac
Noxium encrypts photos on your iPhone and opens them only with your pattern. Nothing shows up in Photos on your Mac or iCloud.com.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Where is the Hidden album on Mac?
In the Photos sidebar under Utilities, once you choose View › Show Hidden Photo Album. It's hidden from the sidebar by default.
How do I unlock the Hidden album on my Mac?
Click View Album, then use Touch ID or type your Mac login password. There's no separate password for the album.
Do hidden photos sync between iPhone and Mac?
Yes, if iCloud Photos is on for both and they use the same Apple Account. A photo hidden on one is hidden on the other.
Why is Show Hidden Photo Album greyed out?
Click Library in the sidebar first. The View menu option applies to the library, so select it before you choose the menu item.
Does hiding a photo on Mac delete it?
No. It stays in your library and in iCloud Photos, just out of view. Unhide it from the Hidden album at any time.

# How to view iPhone hidden photos on a Windows PC

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/view-hidden-photos-on-windows-pc
Last updated: 2026-11-22

Guide · Hidden album
## How to view iPhone hidden photos on a Windows PC
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 22 November 2026
Short answer
Use a web browser: go to icloud.com/photos, sign in with your Apple Account, click Hidden in the sidebar, then Show Hidden Photos. This needs iCloud Photos on your iPhone. The iCloud for Windows app is not a reliable way to see hidden photos, and a USB cable may show them unprotected.
There's no Photos app for Windows from Apple, so the Hidden album works differently on a PC. This guide covers the three ways people try, iCloud.com, the iCloud for Windows app and a USB cable, what each one shows, and how to keep hidden photos private on a computer other people use. For the iPhone side, see how to view hidden photos on iPhone ; for a Mac, see how to view hidden photos on a Mac .
### How do you view hidden photos on Windows with iCloud.com?
Open icloud.com/photos in any browser, then open the Hidden album from the sidebar. Apple's steps (Apple: Hide your photos and videos on iCloud.com):
- Go to icloud.com/photos in Edge, Chrome or Firefox.
- Sign in with the Apple Account your iPhone uses, and approve the sign-in on your iPhone if asked.
- Open the sidebar with the Show Sidebar button at the top left, if it's not already showing.
- Click Hidden , then Show Hidden Photos .
To save a copy to the PC, select the photos and click the Download button. To unhide, select a photo in Hidden, click the More button and choose Unhide ; it's unhidden on your iPhone too.
### Why can't you see the Hidden album on iCloud.com?
Usually because iCloud Photos is off on your iPhone, or because Advanced Data Protection blocks web access. Check both:
- iCloud Photos is off. Without it, nothing from your library is on iCloud.com. Turn it on in Settings › [your name] › iCloud › Photos › Sync this iPhone and let it upload.
- Advanced Data Protection is on. Web access is off by default. Turn on Settings › [your name] › iCloud › Access iCloud Data on the Web , then approve the sign-in on your iPhone when iCloud.com asks.
- A different Apple Account. The account on iCloud.com must be the one your iPhone syncs Photos with.
### Does the iCloud for Windows app show hidden photos?
Not reliably. The iCloud for Windows app downloads your iCloud Photos into File Explorer, under iCloud Photos in the navigation pane (Apple: Download and view iCloud Photos on your Windows computer). Apple doesn't describe a Hidden album there, and people on Apple's Community forum report that everything downloaded except their hidden photos.
If you need hidden photos in File Explorer, download them from iCloud.com instead, or unhide them on the iPhone first. Unhidden photos sync like any other photo.
### Do hidden photos show up when you connect an iPhone with a cable?
They can. Hiding is a setting in the Photos app, not a separate locked folder, and people on Apple's Community forum report hidden photos appearing on a Windows PC when they browse or import the iPhone's pictures.
- Unlock the iPhone and tap Trust when it asks about the computer.
- On the PC, open the Windows Photos app and choose Import , or open File Explorer › Apple iPhone › Internal Storage › DCIM .
- Look before you import. If hidden photos are listed, they'll be copied as ordinary files, with no lock.
With iCloud Photos on and Optimize iPhone Storage turned on, many full-size photos aren't on the phone at all, so a cable shows only part of your library.
Watch out
Photos copied to a PC are not hidden or locked there. Anyone who uses that Windows account can open them in File Explorer, and they may be included in OneDrive backups of your Pictures folder.
### How do you keep hidden photos private on a shared PC?
Use iCloud.com in a private window, don't download, and sign out when you're done.
- Use a private window (InPrivate in Edge, Incognito in Chrome), so the browser doesn't keep your session.
- Don't tick "Trust this browser" when iCloud.com asks.
- Don't download unless you need to, and if you do, delete the files from Downloads and empty the Recycle Bin.
- Sign out of iCloud.com when you finish.
Remember that anyone with your Apple Account password and a code from your trusted devices can do the same. The Hidden album has no separate password; read is the iPhone Hidden album private? for what it does and doesn't protect.
If you want private photos that never show up on a computer, keep them in a vault app instead. Noxium, which we make, keeps photos encrypted inside the app on iPhone and iPad, opened only with your pattern. They don't appear on iCloud.com, in iCloud for Windows or over a USB cable, and the backup in your own iCloud is encrypted data only.
Private photos that no computer can show
Noxium encrypts photos on your iPhone. They don't appear on iCloud.com, in iCloud for Windows or over a cable.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Can I see iPhone hidden photos on a PC?
Yes. Go to icloud.com/photos, sign in, click Hidden, then Show Hidden Photos. iCloud Photos must be on for your iPhone.
Does iCloud for Windows download hidden photos?
Not reliably. Apple doesn't describe a Hidden album in the app, and users report hidden photos missing from the download. Use iCloud.com, or unhide them first.
Do I need a password to see hidden photos on iCloud.com?
Only your Apple Account sign-in. The Hidden album on iCloud.com has no separate password; you click Show Hidden Photos.
Why does iCloud.com say my data isn't available?
Advanced Data Protection is probably on. Turn on Access iCloud Data on the Web in Settings › [your name] › iCloud on your iPhone, then approve the sign-in.

# Can someone bypass the Hidden album's Face ID?

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/can-someone-bypass-hidden-album-face-id
Last updated: 2026-11-22

Guide · Hidden album
## Can someone bypass the Hidden album's Face ID?
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 22 November 2026
Short answer
Yes, easily, if they know your iPhone passcode: Face ID on the Hidden album always falls back to it. Anyone who can unlock a Mac or iPad on your Apple Account, or sign in to iCloud.com, can see your hidden photos too. No hacking is needed. A long passcode, Face ID's attention check and a vault app with its own code close most of these gaps.
Since iOS 16, the Hidden album has asked for Face ID before it opens, which feels like a separate lock. It isn't. This guide lists every ordinary way someone can get past it, with no special tools, and what you can do about each one. For the basics of finding and using the album, see how to view hidden photos on iPhone .
### Does the iPhone passcode open the Hidden album?
Yes. Face ID and Touch ID are a shortcut; if they fail, or someone taps the passcode option, your iPhone passcode unlocks the album (Apple: Hide photos with the Hidden album). There's no setting for a different code.
That makes your passcode the real lock. If a partner, child or housemate knows it, or has watched you type it, the Hidden album only keeps photos out of casual view.
### What are the ways past the Hidden album's Face ID?
Five ordinary routes, none of which need a hack.
Ways someone can open your Hidden album, on iOS 26 with default settings
Route What they need How to close it
Your iPhone passcode To know or see your passcode A longer, alphanumeric passcode; type it out of sight
Your face Your iPhone held up to you, for example while you sleep Keep Require Attention for Face ID on
Your Mac or iPad To unlock another device on your Apple Account, with iCloud Photos on Lock those devices with codes only you know
iCloud.com Your Apple Account password and a code from a trusted device A strong, unique Apple Account password
A shared library To be a participant in your iCloud Shared Photo Library Keep private photos out of the shared library
Apple notes that a photo hidden in a shared library moves to the Hidden album for every participant (Apple: Hide your photos and videos on iCloud.com). On a Mac, the album opens with Touch ID or the Mac login password, as our guide to viewing hidden photos on a Mac explains.
### Can someone use your face while you're asleep?
Not if Face ID's attention check is on, which it is by default. With Require Attention for Face ID on, your eyes must be open and looking at the iPhone.
- Open Settings › Face ID & Passcode and enter your passcode.
- Check Require Attention for Face ID is on.
- Check who else is enrolled. If Set Up an Alternate Appearance has been used, someone else's face may unlock your iPhone and your Hidden album. Reset Face ID removes every face, including theirs.
### How do you make the Hidden album harder to get into?
Strengthen the passcode, check every device on your account, and keep the lock on.
- Use a stronger passcode. In Settings › Face ID & Passcode › Change Passcode › Passcode Options , choose a custom alphanumeric code.
- Keep the album locked. In Settings › Apps › Photos , leave Use Face ID on. It also stops other apps reading hidden photos.
- Hide the album itself. Turn off Show Hidden Album on the same screen. It doesn't add a lock, but someone has to know to look.
- Check your other devices. Every Mac and iPad with iCloud Photos on your Apple Account has the same hidden photos.
- Check your Apple Account. In Settings › [your name] › Sign-In & Security , use a strong password and remove trusted devices you don't own.
Locking the whole Photos app (touch and hold its icon, then Require Face ID ) adds a step, but it falls back to the same passcode. Every option is compared in how to lock photos on iPhone .
### What if people around you know your passcode?
Then the Hidden album can't protect you from them, and you need a lock with a different code. Your choices are a locked note with its own Notes password for a few photos, or a vault app with its own PIN, password or pattern.
Noxium, which we make, opens with a pattern you draw on a 5×5 plate of bolts, separate from your iPhone passcode, and encrypts every photo with AES-256-GCM on the iPhone. Knowing your passcode doesn't open it. A second pattern can open a decoy vault, for times you're asked to unlock it, and the content is hidden in the app switcher and in screen recordings.
A lock your passcode can't open
Noxium opens only with a pattern you choose, not your iPhone passcode, and encrypts every photo. Free for 150 photos, 10 videos and 1 decoy vault.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Can you open the Hidden album without Face ID?
Yes, with the iPhone passcode. Face ID falls back to it, and there's no separate Hidden album password.
Can someone bypass the Hidden album without my passcode?
On your iPhone, they'd need your face with attention detection off. They can also reach hidden photos from a Mac or iPad on your account, or from iCloud.com with your Apple Account password.
Can I set a different password for the Hidden album?
No. iOS uses your Face ID, Touch ID or iPhone passcode. For a separate code, use a locked note or a vault app.
Will I know if someone opened my Hidden album?
iOS doesn't keep a log of who opened it. Read our guide to how private the Hidden album is for what to check.

# Did someone open my Hidden album? How to tell, and what to do

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/did-someone-open-my-hidden-album
Last updated: 2026-11-23

Guide · Hidden album
## Did someone open my Hidden album? How to tell, and what to do
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 23 November 2026
Short answer
iOS doesn't keep a record of who opened the Hidden album, so there's no log to check. You can look for indirect signs: Photos usage in Screen Time, missing or unhidden photos, Recently Deleted, sign-in emails from Apple, and unfamiliar devices on your Apple Account. Then change your passcode, expire the old one, and run Safety Check.
If you think someone has looked at your hidden photos, the first thing to know is what your iPhone can and can't tell you. This guide lists every place worth checking on iOS 26, what each one does and doesn't prove, and how to lock things down afterwards. For how the album works in the first place, see is the iPhone Hidden album private?
### Does the iPhone record who opens the Hidden album?
No. Photos doesn't log when the Hidden album is opened, and iOS doesn't record failed Face ID attempts in a list you can see. There's also no setting that takes a photo of whoever opens it.
So any check is indirect. It can make it more or less likely that someone looked, but it can't prove it either way.
### What signs can you check?
Five places can show that someone used Photos or your account when you didn't.
- Screen Time. Open Settings › Screen Time › See All App & Website Activity , pick the day, and look for Photos use at times you weren't using it. Screen Time has to have been on already; it doesn't record anything retroactively.
- The Hidden album itself. Count the photos and look for any that are missing, or that now appear in your main library because they were unhidden.
- Recently Deleted. In Photos, open Collections › Utilities › Recently Deleted . Deleted hidden photos stay there for up to 30 days.
- Apple's sign-in emails. Apple emails you when your Apple Account is used to sign in to iCloud.com in a web browser. Search your inbox for messages from Apple about a new sign-in you didn't make.
- Your devices. In Settings › [your name] , scroll to the list of devices. Any device there with iCloud Photos on can show your hidden photos.
Sharing leaves fewer traces. If a photo was sent by AirDrop or saved to another app, there's usually no record on your iPhone. Check your Sent messages and the Recents in any app that could have been used.
### Who could have opened it?
Anyone who knows your iPhone passcode, or can unlock a Mac or iPad on your account. Face ID on the Hidden album falls back to the passcode, and there's no separate password.
Who can open your Hidden album, and what it would take
Who What they need
Someone with your iPhone Your passcode, or your face with attention detection off
Someone at your Mac or iPad That device's login or passcode, with iCloud Photos on
Someone on any computer Your Apple Account password and a code from one of your devices
A shared library participant Photos you hid inside the iCloud Shared Photo Library
If you've ever unlocked your phone in front of someone, or shared your passcode, assume they could know it.
### What should you do if you think someone looked?
Change your passcode, end the old one straight away, and check your account. In order:
- Change your iPhone passcode in Settings › Face ID & Passcode › Change Passcode . Choose Passcode Options › Custom Alphanumeric Code for a stronger one.
- Expire the old passcode. Since iOS 17, your previous passcode still works for 72 hours. On the same screen, tap Expire Previous Passcode Now (Apple: Expire an old passcode sooner).
- Check Face ID. If someone else's face was added as an alternate appearance, tap Reset Face ID and set it up again.
- Run Safety Check. Open Settings › Privacy & Security › Safety Check and choose Manage Sharing & Access to review and remove devices on your Apple Account (Apple: Safety Check for iPhone).
- Change your Apple Account password in Settings › [your name] › Sign-In & Security if anyone else might know it.
- Lock your Mac and iPad with codes only you know, or turn off iCloud Photos on devices others use.
Watch out
If you're worried about someone who controls your phone or could hurt you, changing settings can be noticed. Apple's Personal Safety User Guide explains how to review access safely, and Safety Check's Emergency Reset stops all sharing at once.
### How do you know next time?
The Hidden album can't tell you, so the answer is a lock that doesn't depend on your passcode. A locked note with its own Notes password works for a few photos. For more, use a vault app with a separate code; our guide to locking photos on iPhone compares the options.
Noxium, which we make, opens only with a pattern you draw on a 5×5 plate of bolts, not your iPhone passcode, and encrypts every photo on the iPhone. Someone who knows your passcode still can't open it. A second pattern opens a decoy vault, and its content is hidden in the app switcher and in screen recordings.
A lock your passcode doesn't open
Noxium opens only with a pattern you choose and encrypts every photo on your iPhone. Free for 150 photos, 10 videos and 1 decoy vault.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Can I see who opened my Hidden album?
No. iOS doesn't log who opens the Hidden album or record failed Face ID attempts you can review. You can only check indirect signs, like Screen Time and missing photos.
Does the Hidden album take a photo of intruders?
No. iOS has no break-in photo feature. Some vault apps do, but they can only record attempts inside their own app.
Will changing my passcode lock someone out right away?
Not on its own. The old passcode keeps working for 72 hours unless you tap Expire Previous Passcode Now in Settings › Face ID & Passcode.
Does Screen Time show if someone opened Photos?
It shows when Photos was used and for how long, if Screen Time was already on. It doesn't show which album was opened.
Can someone see my hidden photos from their own phone?
Only if they're signed in to your Apple Account, or you hid photos inside an iCloud Shared Photo Library you share with them. Review signed-in devices with Safety Check.

# How to change the Hidden album password on iPhone

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/change-hidden-album-password
Last updated: 2026-11-23

Guide · Hidden album
## How to change the Hidden album password on iPhone
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 23 November 2026
Short answer
The Hidden album has no password of its own: it opens with Face ID, Touch ID or your iPhone passcode. To change its "password", change your iPhone passcode in Settings › Face ID & Passcode, then tap Expire Previous Passcode Now so the old one stops working. For a code that's separate from your passcode, use a locked note or a vault app.
People search for a Hidden album password setting because they want the album to open with something only they know. iOS doesn't offer one. This guide shows what actually controls the lock, how to change it on iPhone and Mac, and what to use if you need a code nobody else knows. For finding and using the album, see how to view hidden photos on iPhone .
### Does the Hidden album have its own password?
No. Since iOS 16 the Hidden album is locked by default, and it opens with Face ID, Touch ID or your iPhone passcode (Apple: Hide photos with the Hidden album). There is no menu to give it a different code.
That means whoever knows your iPhone passcode can open your Hidden album. Changing the album's lock means changing your passcode.
### How do you change the passcode that opens the Hidden album?
Change your iPhone passcode, then expire the old one. iOS 26 steps:
- Open Settings › Face ID & Passcode (or Touch ID & Passcode ) and enter your current passcode.
- Tap Change Passcode and enter the current one again.
- Tap Passcode Options and choose Custom Alphanumeric Code or Custom Numeric Code for something longer than six digits.
- Enter the new passcode twice.
- Tap Expire Previous Passcode Now on the same screen, then confirm. Without this, the old passcode keeps working for 72 hours (Apple: Expire an old passcode sooner).
The new passcode now opens your iPhone and your Hidden album. It also opens Recently Deleted, which shares the same lock.
Watch out
Write the new passcode down somewhere safe until you know it by heart. If you forget it after expiring the old one, the only way back in is to erase the iPhone and restore from a backup.
### Should you also reset Face ID?
Only if someone else's face might be enrolled. Face ID opens the Hidden album without the passcode, so an extra face is an extra key.
- Open Settings › Face ID & Passcode .
- Check for an alternate appearance. If Set Up an Alternate Appearance isn't shown, one is already set up.
- Tap Reset Face ID and set up your own face again if you're unsure who set it up.
- Leave Require Attention for Face ID on , so your face can't unlock it while you're asleep.
### Can you lock the whole Photos app instead?
Yes, since iOS 18, but it uses the same passcode. Touch and hold the Photos icon on your Home Screen and tap Require Face ID . Photos then asks for Face ID every time it opens, which stops someone browsing your library on an unlocked phone. It doesn't give you a new code: if Face ID fails, your iPhone passcode opens it, just like the Hidden album.
### How do you change the Hidden album password on a Mac?
On a Mac, the Hidden album opens with Touch ID or your Mac login password, so change the login password. Open System Settings › Users & Groups , click the info button next to your account, and choose Change Password . If someone else's fingerprint is set up, remove it in System Settings › Touch ID & Password .
### How do you get a password that's different from your passcode?
Use something other than the Hidden album. You have three choices:
Ways to lock photos with a code that isn't your iPhone passcode
Option Separate code Best for
Hidden album No, uses your passcode Keeping photos out of casual view
Locked note in Notes Yes, a Notes password A handful of photos
Vault app Yes, its own PIN, password or pattern Many photos and videos, with extras like a decoy
For a locked note, set a Notes password in Settings › Apps › Notes › Password and choose Use Custom Password , then add photos to a note and lock it. The full steps for every option are in how to lock photos on iPhone .
Noxium, which we make, is a vault app that opens with a pattern you draw on a 5×5 plate of bolts, separate from your passcode. You can change the pattern at any time without re-adding photos, every photo is encrypted on the iPhone, and a recovery phrase you write down at setup gets you back in if you forget it.

### Questions people ask
Can I set a different password for the Hidden album?
No. The Hidden album uses Face ID, Touch ID or your iPhone passcode. For a separate code, use a locked note or a vault app.
Why does my old passcode still open the Hidden album?
Since iOS 17, the previous passcode works for 72 hours after a change. Tap Expire Previous Passcode Now in Settings › Face ID & Passcode to end it.
How do I turn off the Hidden album lock?
Turn off Use Face ID in Settings › Apps › Photos. We don't recommend it: the album then opens without any check, and apps with full Photos access can read hidden photos.
Does changing my passcode affect my hidden photos?
No. The photos stay hidden and in place. Only the code that opens the album changes.

# Hidden photos disappeared on iPhone? How to find them

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/hidden-photos-disappeared-iphone
Last updated: 2026-11-23

Guide · Hidden album
## Hidden photos disappeared on iPhone? How to find them
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 23 November 2026
Short answer
Usually they haven't gone anywhere. Check that Show Hidden Album is on in Settings › Apps › Photos, then look under Collections › Utilities › Hidden. If the album is empty, check Recently Deleted (items stay 30 days), make sure iCloud Photos is on with the right Apple Account, and look on your other devices.
Hidden photos seem to vanish for a handful of reasons, and most of them are settings, not data loss. Work through the checks below in order; the first two solve most cases. This guide is for iOS 26. If you're not sure where the Hidden album should be, start with how to view hidden photos on iPhone .
### Why did the Hidden album disappear?
Most often because Show Hidden Album is turned off, which removes the album from Photos without touching the photos. Turn it back on:
- Open Settings › Apps › Photos .
- Turn on Show Hidden Album .
- Open Photos, tap Collections and scroll down to Utilities . Hidden is listed there with Recently Deleted.
After an update, the album may simply be somewhere new. Since the iOS 18 Photos redesign it sits under Collections › Utilities, near the bottom of the list, not under Albums.
### Why don't hidden photos show in my other albums?
Because that's what hiding does. Apple says hidden items don't appear anywhere else in Photos, including your Library, other albums and the Photos widget. A photo you hid from inside an album is still a member of that album, but it shows only in Hidden until you unhide it.
To put a photo back, open Hidden, touch and hold the photo, and tap Unhide . It returns to your Library and its albums.
### Why is the Hidden album empty?
The photos were deleted, unhidden, or haven't synced yet. Check each:
- Deleted. Open Collections › Utilities › Recently Deleted and unlock it. Deleted photos stay there for 30 days. Select them and tap Recover .
- Unhidden. Search your Library for the photos by date or place. If they're there, they were unhidden on this or another device.
- Not synced yet. On a new or restored iPhone, iCloud Photos can take hours to download a large library. Leave the iPhone on Wi-Fi and power.
- Deleted on another device. With iCloud Photos on, deleting a photo on your iPad or Mac deletes it everywhere. Check Recently Deleted on that device too.
### Could iCloud be the cause?
Yes, if iCloud Photos is off, paused or signed in to a different Apple Account. Hidden photos sync only through iCloud Photos.
- Check the account at the top of Settings. It must be the Apple Account you used when you hid the photos.
- Check iCloud Photos in Settings › [your name] › iCloud › Photos : Sync this iPhone should be on.
- Check storage. If iCloud is full, new photos stop uploading, so photos hidden on one device may never reach another.
- Check iCloud.com. Sign in at icloud.com/photos, click Hidden , then Show Hidden Photos . If they're there, they're safe in iCloud and your iPhone just hasn't synced.
If iCloud Photos was off, hidden photos are only in your iPhone's own library and its iCloud Backup. After a reset, they come back only when you restore that backup.
### Can Screen Time hide the Hidden album?
Screen Time doesn't have a Hidden album setting, but it can block Photos as a whole. If an App Limit or Downtime blocks Photos, you'll see a Screen Time screen instead of your library. On a child's or managed iPhone, the parent or organization controls these settings in Settings › Screen Time .
### What about the iCloud Shared Photo Library?
Photos hidden in a shared library move to the Hidden album for every participant (Apple: Hide your photos and videos on iCloud.com). If someone else in the shared library unhid or deleted a photo, it changes for you too. Check Recently Deleted, and switch the library view to Both Libraries so you're not looking at only one.
### How do you stop this happening again?
Keep a second copy somewhere only you control. The Hidden album shares your Photos library, so anything that removes photos from the library, on any of your devices, can remove hidden ones too.
A vault app keeps private photos separate from your Photos library. Noxium, which we make, stores photos encrypted inside the app, backs them up as encrypted data to your own iCloud, and keeps deleted items in its own Recently Deleted for 30 days. Read more on encrypted iCloud backup , or how other vaults handle it in photo vault lost photos .
Private photos with their own backup
Noxium keeps photos encrypted outside your Photos library, with an encrypted backup in your own iCloud. Free for 150 photos and 10 videos.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Where did my Hidden album go?
In iOS 26 it's under Collections › Utilities in Photos. If it's not there, turn on Show Hidden Album in Settings › Apps › Photos.
Why are my hidden photos not showing in albums?
Hidden photos appear only in the Hidden album. Unhide a photo to see it in your Library and other albums again.
Can I recover hidden photos I deleted?
Within 30 days, from Recently Deleted. After that, only from an older iCloud Backup or computer backup made before you deleted them.
Why do my hidden photos look blurry?
With Optimize iPhone Storage on, the full-size copy stays in iCloud until you open the photo. Give it a moment on Wi-Fi and it loads in full.
Do hidden photos disappear after an iOS update?
No. Updates don't delete hidden photos, but they can move the album. Look under Collections › Utilities.

# How to hide photos from Memories on iPhone

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/hide-photos-from-memories-iphone
Last updated: 2026-11-23

Guide · Hidden album
## How to hide photos from Memories on iPhone
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 23 November 2026
Short answer
Hide the photo: touch and hold it, tap Hide, and it stops appearing in Memories, featured photos and widgets. To keep a person, place, day or holiday out of Memories without hiding photos, touch and hold a memory and tap Feature Less. To start over, use Reset Suggested Memories in Settings › Apps › Photos.
Memories turns your library into slideshows with music, and the Photos widget and featured photos show pictures on your Home Screen. That's lovely until a private photo, an ex, or a hard date shows up in front of someone. This guide covers every way to keep photos out of them on iOS 26, from one photo to whole people and places. For hiding in general, see how to hide photos on iPhone .
### How do you stop a photo appearing in Memories?
Hide it. A hidden photo disappears from your Library, Memories, featured photos and the Photos widget, and shows only in the Hidden album.
- Find the photo in your Library or in the memory itself.
- Touch and hold it , or open it and tap the More (…) button.
- Tap Hide and confirm.
Memories that are already made drop the photo too. To find it again, open Collections › Utilities › Hidden ; how to view hidden photos on iPhone has the details.
### How do you see less of a person, place or date?
Use Feature Less on a memory. It keeps the photos in your library but tells Photos to show that person, place or day less often (Apple: Manage memories and featured photos).
- Open Photos and find Memories in Collections.
- Touch and hold a memory that features what you want to see less of.
- Tap Feature Less , then choose one of: Feature a Person Less , Feature This Place Less , Feature This Holiday Less , Feature This Day Less or Feature These Days Less .
To delete a memory you don't want, touch and hold it and tap Delete Memory . That deletes only the slideshow, not the photos in it.
### How do you stop a person appearing at all?
Open a photo of them and choose Never Feature This Person. Apple's steps:
- Open a photo of the person and swipe up to see the details.
- Tap their face thumbnail.
- Choose Feature This Person Less or Never Feature This Person , then tap Confirm .
Their photos stay in your library and in search. They just stop being used in Memories and featured photos.
### What can you change in Settings?
Two switches in Settings › Apps › Photos help:
- Show Holiday Events : turn it off to stop memories built around holidays in your region.
- Reset Suggested Memories : clears the memories Photos has suggested. Use Reset People & Pets Suggestions to undo every Feature Less and Never Feature choice for people.
The Photos widget shows featured photos on your Home Screen. If you don't want any photos showing there, touch and hold the widget and tap Remove Widget .
### Where else can private photos pop up on their own?
Featured photos and Memories aren't the only places Photos picks pictures for you. Check these too:
- Lock Screen Photo Shuffle. If your wallpaper shuffles photos, edit it from the Lock Screen and choose Select Photos Manually instead of featured photos, so only pictures you picked appear.
- The Photos widget. It shows featured photos on your Home Screen. Hidden photos are left out, but anything else in your library can appear.
- Your Mac and iPad. They make their own Memories from the same library. Use Feature Less there too, or hide the photo once and it's hidden on every device with iCloud Photos.
- Shared albums and the iCloud Shared Photo Library. Photos in them are visible to everyone you share with, whatever your Memories settings.
If a photo keeps surfacing, hiding it is the one step that covers all of these at once.
### What doesn't this protect?
Keeping photos out of Memories is about what pops up on its own, not about who can open them.
- Feature Less isn't hiding. The photos are still in your Library, albums and search.
- Hidden photos open with your passcode. Anyone who knows it can open the Hidden album; see is the iPhone Hidden album private?
- Other devices. With iCloud Photos on, your iPad and Mac have the same photos, and their own Memories.
For photos that should never surface anywhere in Photos, keep them outside the library. Noxium, which we make, stores photos encrypted inside its own app, opened with a pattern separate from your passcode, so they never appear in Memories, featured photos, widgets or search.
Photos that never show up in Memories
Noxium keeps private photos encrypted outside your Photos library, behind a pattern only you know. Free for 150 photos and 10 videos.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Do hidden photos show up in Memories?
No. Hidden photos are left out of Memories, featured photos and the Photos widget.
How do I stop an ex showing up in Memories?
Open a photo of them, swipe up, tap their face and choose Never Feature This Person. Their photos stay in your library but stop appearing in Memories.
Does deleting a memory delete the photos?
No. Delete Memory removes only the slideshow. The photos stay in your library.
Do Memories on my Mac follow my iPhone settings?
Hidden photos are hidden on every device with iCloud Photos on. Photos on a Mac makes its own Memories, so use Feature Less there as well.
Can I turn off Memories completely?
Not with one switch on iPhone. You can reset suggested memories, turn off holiday events, use Feature Less, and remove the Photos widget.

# How to hide photos from Spotlight search on iPhone

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/hide-photos-from-spotlight-search
Last updated: 2026-11-24

Guide · Hidden album
## How to hide photos from Spotlight search on iPhone
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 24 November 2026
Short answer
Turn off Show Content in Search for Photos. It's in the Photos app's Siri & Search (or Search) settings, reached from Settings › Apps › Photos on iOS 18 and later. Photos then stops showing individual pictures when you swipe down to search. To keep one photo out of everything, hide it as well.
Swipe down on the Home Screen, type a word like "beach" or a friend's name, and Spotlight can show matching photos from your library before you've opened Photos. That's handy until someone else is holding your phone. This guide shows how to stop it, what each switch does, and where else photos can surface. For hiding photos in general, see how to hide photos on iPhone .
### Why do my photos show up in Spotlight search?
Because Photos shares its content with search by default. Your iPhone recognises people, places, objects and text in your pictures, and Spotlight uses that to show matches from your library.
This all happens on the iPhone; it isn't a web search. But anyone who can unlock your phone and swipe down can see the results.
### How do you stop photos appearing in Spotlight?
Turn off Show Content in Search for the Photos app. On iOS 26:
- Open Settings › Apps › Photos .
- Tap Siri & Search (on some versions it's split into Siri and Search ; open Search).
- Turn off Show Content in Search . Individual photos stop appearing in Spotlight results.
- Optionally turn off Show App in Search too. Then the Photos app itself won't be suggested either.
- Swipe down on the Home Screen and search for a word that used to bring up photos, to check.
On iOS 17 and earlier the same switches are under Settings › Siri & Search › Photos . Turning them off doesn't delete or move any photo; it only changes what Spotlight shows.
### What about suggestions on the Home Screen?
Turn those off on the same screen. Look for Show on Home Screen , Suggest App and Show When Sharing , and switch off the ones you don't want. They control whether Photos appears in Siri Suggestions, the App Library and the share sheet.
The Photos widget is separate: it shows featured photos on your Home Screen. Touch and hold it and tap Remove Widget if you don't want any photos showing there.
### How do you hide just one photo from search?
Hide it in Photos. A hidden photo moves to the Hidden album and, Apple says, doesn't appear anywhere else in Photos, including your Library, albums and the Photos widget.
- Touch and hold the photo in Photos.
- Tap Hide and confirm.
- Search for it in Spotlight to check it no longer appears.
The Hidden album is locked with Face ID or your passcode, and you can find it under Collections › Utilities . See how to view hidden photos on iPhone .
### Does this stop search inside the Photos app?
No. These settings only affect Spotlight and suggestions. Search inside Photos still finds your photos by person, place and object, because it's part of the app.
Anyone who can open Photos can still search your library there. If that's the worry, hide the photos, or lock the Photos app: touch and hold its icon and tap Require Face ID (iOS 18 and later). Both fall back to your iPhone passcode; is the iPhone Hidden album private? explains what that means.
### Where else can photos show up?
A few places don't follow the Spotlight switches.
Where iPhone photos can surface on their own, and how to stop it
Place How to stop it
Spotlight search Turn off Show Content in Search for Photos
Memories and featured photos Hide the photo, or use Feature Less on a memory
Photos widget Hide the photo, or remove the widget
Lock Screen Photo Shuffle Choose the photos yourself when you edit the wallpaper
Search inside Photos Hide the photo, or lock the Photos app
Your Mac and iPad Same switches on each device; hidden photos stay hidden everywhere with iCloud Photos
On a Mac, photos can appear in Spotlight too. Remove Photos from search results in System Settings › Spotlight .
### How do you keep photos out of search entirely?
Keep them outside your Photos library. Anything in the library, hidden or not, is indexed by your iPhone, and anyone with your passcode can open the Hidden album.
Noxium, which we make, keeps photos encrypted inside its own app, opened with a pattern you draw on a 5×5 plate of bolts rather than your passcode. Its photos aren't in your Photos library, so they don't appear in Spotlight, Memories, widgets or Photos search, and its content is hidden in the app switcher and in screen recordings.
Photos search can't find
Noxium keeps private photos encrypted outside your Photos library, behind a pattern only you know. Free for 150 photos and 10 videos.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
How do I stop photos showing in iPhone search?
In the Photos app's Siri & Search settings, turn off Show Content in Search. On iOS 18 and later, start from Settings › Apps › Photos.
Do hidden photos show in Spotlight?
Hidden photos are kept out of your Library, albums and widgets. To be sure nothing from Photos appears in Spotlight, also turn off Show Content in Search.
Does turning off Show Content in Search delete photos?
No. It only changes what Spotlight shows. Your photos stay in your library and in iCloud Photos.
Can I still search inside the Photos app?
Yes. The Spotlight switches don't affect search inside Photos.

# Does deleting a vault app delete your photos?

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/does-deleting-vault-app-delete-photos
Last updated: 2026-11-24

Guide · Backup
## Does deleting a vault app delete your photos?
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 24 November 2026
Short answer
Usually, yes. When you delete an app, iOS deletes everything stored inside it, so photos kept only in a vault app are gone from the phone. They survive only if the app backed them up somewhere else, like your iCloud or its own cloud. Before you delete one, export your photos or check its backup, or use Offload App instead.
This is one of the most common ways people lose private photos: the vault app gets deleted to save space, to switch apps, or by someone else, and the photos go with it. This guide explains what iOS does when an app is deleted, which vault apps keep a copy elsewhere, and how to get rid of one safely. If it has already happened, start with photo vault lost photos .
### What happens to an app's data when you delete it?
iOS removes the app and everything it stored on the iPhone. There's no Recently Deleted for apps. Photos you moved into a vault app aren't in your Photos library, so they aren't anywhere else on the phone.
Your device's iCloud Backup doesn't help afterwards either: the next backup no longer includes the deleted app, and many vault apps leave their files out of the iCloud Backup on purpose.
### Which vault apps keep a copy when you delete them?
Only those with their own backup. Here's what the apps we've reviewed say about backup, from their App Store listings:
Backup that survives deleting the app, as each US App Store listing describes it, checked 11–21 November 2026
App Copy outside the app
Vaultaire Your own iCloud, encrypted, free
Encamera Your own iCloud, with Premium
Keepsafe Its Private Cloud; first 200 items free
Private Photo Vault Its Cloud Vault, Premium only
Obscura Only an encrypted export file you made yourself
PV Paid cloud backup only
SPV None; its listing says data is deleted with the app
Secret Photo Vault None; data stays on the device
Safe Lock None automatic; only what you exported
Noxium (ours) Your own iCloud, encrypted, free
A cloud copy only helps if it was switched on and finished uploading before the app was deleted. Check the app's backup screen before you delete anything.
### How do you delete a vault app without losing photos?
Get the photos out first, check them, then delete. In order:
- Count what's in the vault, including every album, any decoy vault you want to keep, and any second vault.
- Export the photos and videos to Photos or Files from inside the app. Our guide to exporting photos from a vault app covers how.
- Check the copies: counts match, videos play, photos open at full size.
- Move them somewhere private , such as another vault (see moving photos into a vault app ), if you don't want them in your Photos library.
- Cancel any subscription in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions . Deleting an app doesn't cancel it.
- Only then delete the app.
Watch out
Exported photos sit unencrypted in Photos or Files until you move them. Do it in one sitting, on a phone only you are using.
### Can you free up space without deleting the photos?
Yes: offload the app instead of deleting it. Offloading removes the app but keeps its documents and data, and reinstalling puts it back as it was.
- Open Settings › General › iPhone Storage .
- Tap the vault app.
- Tap Offload App , not Delete App, and confirm.
Offloading frees only the app's own size, not the photos' space. To free that, move photos out or use the app's own storage options.
### Can you stop someone else deleting the app?
Yes, with Screen Time. It's worth doing on a phone that children or others use.
- Open Settings › Screen Time › Content & Privacy Restrictions and turn on Content & Privacy Restrictions .
- Tap App Store Purchases (called iTunes & App Store Purchases on older versions).
- Set Deleting Apps to Don't Allow .
- Set a Screen Time passcode that's different from your iPhone passcode, so others can't change it back.
To delete an app yourself later, switch Deleting Apps back to Allow first.
### What if you've already deleted the app?
Reinstall it with the same Apple Account and look for a restore option. If the app had a cloud backup, your photos may come back when you sign in or unlock it. If it kept everything on the device, there's usually no way back unless you have an older computer backup or iCloud Backup made while the app was installed, and restoring one replaces what's on the phone now.
Don't sign up again with a different account, and contact the developer before you try anything that resets the app.
### What happens if you delete Noxium?
The vault on the iPhone is deleted, but its encrypted backup stays in your own iCloud. Noxium, which we make, backs up only encrypted data to your private iCloud, free on every plan. Reinstall it, draw your pattern (or use your recovery phrase) and it restores. Check that Settings › iCloud backup shows nothing waiting before you delete it. See encrypted iCloud backup .
A vault that survives being deleted
Noxium keeps an encrypted backup in your own iCloud. Reinstall, draw your pattern, and your vault is back.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
If I delete a photo vault app, are my photos gone?
From the iPhone, yes. They survive only if the app backed them up to a cloud first, or you exported them.
Does reinstalling a vault app bring photos back?
Only if the app has a cloud backup and you sign in or unlock it the same way. Apps that keep everything on the device start empty.
Does offloading an app delete its photos?
No. Offload App keeps the app's documents and data. Reinstall it and they're back.
Does deleting the app cancel my subscription?
No. Cancel it in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions.
Something wrong or out of date? Email business@inertiaprojects.info and we'll fix it.
