# How to export photos from a vault app on iPhone

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/export-photos-from-vault-app
Last updated: 2026-11-24

Guide · Backup
## How to export photos from a vault app on iPhone
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 24 November 2026
Short answer
Open the vault, select the photos, and use its Export, Share or Save option to send them to Photos or Files. Then check the count, that videos play, and that photos are full size before you delete anything. Exported copies are no longer protected by the vault, so move them on quickly.
You might want photos out of a vault to switch apps, to back them up, to print them, or before you delete the app. Every vault does it a little differently, and some quietly lose quality or dates on the way out. This guide gives the general steps, the routes each popular app offers, and the checks that tell you nothing was lost. Switching to a new phone instead? See moving a photo vault to a new iPhone .
### How do you export photos from a vault app?
Select, export, check. The buttons have different names in each app, but the steps are the same:
- Open the vault and the album you want.
- Tap Select (or touch and hold) and choose the photos and videos. Many apps have a Select All.
- Tap Export, Share or the share icon , and choose where they go: the Photos library, Files, or a computer.
- Wait for it to finish. Large videos can take minutes. Keep the app open.
- Check the copies where they landed, before you delete anything from the vault.
Do albums one at a time if the vault has many. It's easier to check counts album by album.
### Where should you export to?
Choose based on what happens next.
Where to export vault photos, and what each destination keeps
Destination Good for Watch out
Photos library Moving into another vault, or back into your library Visible to anyone with your passcode; syncs with iCloud Photos
Files (On My iPhone) Keeping originals out of Photos for a short time Files has no lock of its own
Computer or drive A long-term backup you control Encrypt the drive, or the copies are open
AirDrop Moving to your own Mac or another iPhone Check the name of the device you send to
### How do popular vault apps export?
From their App Store listings and our reviews:
- Keepsafe : its help center says to open an album, select items, tap the send icon and choose Export to Camera Roll. If you use Space Saver, check exports are full size.
- Private Photo Vault and Vaultaire : their listings say you can export back to the Photos app.
- SPV : its listing tells you to export photos and videos to the photo gallery before deleting the app.
- Secret Photo Vault , Safe Lock and PV : Wi-Fi transfer to a computer; Secret Photo Vault and Safe Lock also export to the photo library, and Safe Lock to Dropbox, Google Drive and others.
- Obscura : share items out, or export the whole vault as one encrypted .obscura file you can restore later.
Menu names change with app updates. If you can't find export, check the app's help pages or contact the developer before deleting anything.
### How do you check nothing was lost?
Compare counts, play videos, and look at size and date.
- Count. The number of exported items should match the album in the vault.
- Play videos to the end. A video that stops early didn't export fully.
- Check size. Open a photo, swipe up and look at its resolution and file size. Much smaller than the camera's usual size means the vault exported a compressed copy. See does a photo vault keep full resolution?
- Check dates. Photos should land on the day they were taken, not today. If they're all dated today, the vault didn't keep the original date.
- Check Live Photos still move when you press on them.
Watch out
Exported copies are ordinary files. Anyone with your passcode can see photos in your library, and they upload to iCloud Photos if it's on. Move them into their new home in the same sitting.
### What should you do after exporting?
Move the copies to where they'll live, then tidy up both ends.
- Moving to another vault: import from Photos, check the new vault's count, then delete the exported copies from Photos and empty Recently Deleted , or they stay there for 30 days.
- Keeping them on a computer: copy them to an encrypted drive or folder, then delete them from the phone's Photos or Files.
- Leaving the old vault: keep it until you've checked everything in the new place, then delete its items and cancel any subscription in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions . Our guide to deleting a vault app covers the safe order.
### How do you export from Noxium?
Select the items, tap Export , and choose Save to Photos , Save to Files or Share… . Noxium, which we make, exports in full quality with the original date taken, including HEIC, ProRAW and Live Photos, and export works on every plan. If Pro ends, you keep full access to view and export everything already in your vault. More in import and export .
Full quality in, full quality out
Noxium keeps your originals and exports them with their dates. Export always works, Pro or not.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
How do I get photos out of a vault app?
Open the vault, select the photos, and tap Export, Share or Save to send them to Photos or Files. Check them before you delete anything.
Will exporting reduce photo quality?
It depends on the app. Some keep originals; others saved a compressed copy when you imported. Compare file sizes after exporting.
Can I export everything at once?
Many apps have Select All in each album. Obscura exports the whole vault as one encrypted file. Doing it album by album makes checking easier.
Can I export if my subscription ended?
Usually, but check first. Noxium and Obscura say export keeps working after a subscription ends.

# Do photo vault apps back up to iCloud?

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/do-photo-vault-apps-back-up-to-icloud
Last updated: 2026-11-24

Guide · Backup
## Do photo vault apps back up to iCloud?
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 24 November 2026
Short answer
Some do, many don't. Of 15 vault apps we've reviewed, 3 back up to your own iCloud, a few use their own paid cloud, and the rest keep photos only on the phone. Your iPhone's iCloud Backup often doesn't cover vault apps either. Check the app's backup screen, and test a restore before you rely on it.
Most people assume that because their iPhone backs up to iCloud, their vault app does too. Often it doesn't. This guide explains the three kinds of vault backup, which apps use which, and how to check yours before you need it. If your photos are already missing, start with photo vault lost photos .
### What are the ways a vault app can back up?
Three, and they're very different:
- Your own iCloud. The app stores its data in your private iCloud space, through Apple's CloudKit. It counts toward your iCloud storage, and the developer doesn't hold it. Done well, it's encrypted on the phone first.
- The developer's cloud. The app uploads to its own servers, usually with an account and often as a paid feature. You depend on the company staying in business and keeping it secure.
- Nothing, or a file you make. Photos live only on the phone. You back up by exporting to a computer or drive yourself.
### Doesn't my iPhone's iCloud Backup include vault apps?
Not reliably. iCloud Backup covers data that apps choose to include. Many vault apps exclude their files on purpose, so a restored iPhone gets the app back but an empty vault. Others include them, but then restoring needs the whole phone restored.
The only way to know is to read the app's own help pages or test it: restore to a spare device, or ask the developer.
### Which vault apps back up to iCloud?
From each app's US App Store listing, checked 11–21 November 2026:
How photo vault apps back up, from their App Store listings. We report claims, not tests.
App Backup
Vaultaire Your own iCloud, encrypted, free; on by default
Encamera Your own iCloud, album by album, with Premium
Noxium (ours) Your own iCloud, encrypted, free
Keepsafe Its Private Cloud: first 200 items free, up to 10,000 with Premium
Private Photo Vault Its Cloud Vault, Premium only
Hide it Pro Its own cloud storage, paid
PV Paid: its own cloud, or Dropbox, Google Drive, Box, OneDrive
Calculator# iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive or OneDrive
MaxVault iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive; encryption not stated
Obscura An encrypted export file you keep; iOS iCloud backup
Safe Lock None automatic; export to clouds yourself
Privault Not in listing; export only
Secret Photo Vault None; stays on the device
SPV None; deleted with the app
HiddenVault Not in listing
"iCloud Drive" sync in some apps is different from a backup in your own iCloud: the files sit in iCloud Drive, where the listing may not say they're encrypted.
### How do you check your vault's backup works?
Find the backup screen, confirm it's up to date, and know how you'd restore.
- Open the app's settings and look for Backup, Cloud or Sync.
- Check the last backup time and that nothing is waiting to upload.
- Check where it goes: your iCloud, the developer's cloud, or nowhere.
- Check what restores it: your PIN, an account login, or a recovery code. Write it down somewhere safe.
- Check your iCloud storage in Settings › [your name] › iCloud . A full iCloud stops backups.
- Keep a second copy of anything irreplaceable, exported to a drive you control.
### What should you ask about a vault's own cloud?
A backup on the developer's servers can work well, but you're trusting the company with your photos. Before you rely on one, find out:
- Is it encrypted on your phone first, so the company can't see your photos?
- What happens if you stop paying? Some cloud plans delete or lock photos when a subscription ends.
- Can you download everything at full size, or only compressed copies?
- What happens if the company shuts down? Keep your own export of anything irreplaceable either way.
### Is a backup in your own iCloud private?
Only if the app encrypts it on the phone first. Your iCloud storage is protected by Apple, but with standard data protection Apple holds the keys to most iCloud data. An app that encrypts before uploading means even Apple sees only scrambled data. How encrypted photo vaults work explains how to tell.
Noxium, which we make, encrypts every photo, video and note on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM, then backs up only that ciphertext to your own iCloud, free on every plan. On a new iPhone, you draw your pattern, or use your recovery phrase, and it restores. Details on encrypted iCloud backup .
An encrypted backup in your own iCloud
Noxium backs up only encrypted data to your private iCloud, on every plan, and restores when you draw your pattern.

### Questions people ask
Do photo vault apps back up to iCloud?
Some do. Of 15 apps we reviewed, Vaultaire, Encamera (with Premium) and Noxium back up to your own iCloud. Several use their own cloud, and many keep photos only on the phone.
Will my vault restore from an iPhone backup?
Not always. Many vault apps leave their files out of the iPhone's iCloud Backup. Check the app's help pages before you erase or replace your phone.
Does a vault backup use my iCloud storage?
If it backs up to your own iCloud, yes, it counts toward your iCloud plan. Backups to the developer's cloud don't.
Can Apple see my vault backup?
Not if the app encrypts it on the phone before uploading. Otherwise, with standard iCloud protection, Apple holds the keys.

# Does a photo vault keep full resolution on iPhone?

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/photo-vault-full-resolution
Last updated: 2026-11-25

Guide · Backup
## Does a photo vault keep full resolution on iPhone?
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 25 November 2026
Short answer
Not always. Some vault apps save a smaller copy to save space, turn HEIC into JPEG, keep only the still part of a Live Photo, or drop the date and place. You can test any vault in two minutes: import one photo, export it back to Photos, and compare its size, resolution and date with the original.
A vault is meant to keep your photos safe, not make them worse. But a few vault apps shrink what you put in, and you often notice only months later, when you zoom in or export. This guide explains how vaults lose quality, what "full resolution" means on an iPhone, and how to check yours before you delete any originals. If you're about to move a whole library, run the two-minute test below first, then follow how to move photos into a vault app .
### Why do some photo vaults lose quality?
To save space. Full-size photos and videos are big, and a smaller copy makes the app look lighter on your phone. The common ways quality goes missing:
- Compression. The vault saves a smaller, lower-quality copy of each photo. Keepsafe's App Store listing says its Space Saver "compresses photos and saves originals to the Cloud", so the full-size file lives in Keepsafe's cloud, not on your phone.
- Format changes. HEIC photos become JPEG, and HDR or wide colour can be lost on the way.
- Live Photos cut down. The vault keeps the still photo and drops the short video that makes it move.
- Missing details. The date taken and the place are removed, so an exported photo lands on today's date.
- Video re-encoding. 4K video is saved at a lower resolution or bitrate.
None of this is always bad. Some people choose a space saver on purpose. It's a problem only when you don't know it's happening and then delete the originals.
### What does full resolution mean on an iPhone?
It means the vault keeps the exact file the camera made, with nothing removed. Your iPhone can make several kinds:
iPhone photo and video formats a vault should keep as they are
Format What it is What can go missing
HEIC (High Efficiency) The iPhone's default photo format Converted to JPEG, HDR lost
JPEG (Most Compatible) Chosen in Settings › Camera › Formats Compressed again
Apple ProRAW Pro models; about 25 MB at 12 MP and 75 MB at 48 MP, Apple says Saved as an ordinary photo
Live Photo A photo with a short video around it The video part
Video (4K, HDR) Set in Settings › Camera › Record Video Lower resolution or bitrate
Details Date taken, place, camera Removed or reset to the import date
Apple's ProRAW support article gives those sizes and says ProRAW files are 10 to 12 times larger than HEIF or JPEG files. That's why a vault that quietly converts them saves so much space.
### How can you tell if a vault keeps full resolution?
Run a round trip with one photo, and compare before and after. It takes two minutes:
- Pick a test photo in Photos: ideally a Live Photo taken outdoors, so it has a place.
- Note its details. Swipe up on the photo, or tap the info button. Write down the resolution (for example 24 MP and the pixel size), the file size, the format, the date and the place.
- Import it into the vault the way you normally would.
- Export it back to Photos from the vault.
- Compare. Open the exported copy, swipe up and check the same details. Press on it to see if the Live Photo still moves.
- Repeat with a video if you'll keep videos in the vault. Check its resolution and length.
Matching numbers and a moving Live Photo mean the vault kept the original. A smaller file, a lower resolution, today's date or a still Live Photo means it didn't. Our guide to exporting photos from a vault app covers the same checks for a whole library.
### Does iCloud Photos affect what the vault gets?
It can slow imports down, but it shouldn't change the result. With Optimize iPhone Storage on, your iPhone keeps smaller copies, and the full-size originals stay in iCloud. When a vault imports one of those photos, iOS has to download the original first.
- Use Wi-Fi for big imports, and keep the vault open until it finishes.
- Check a few imported items afterwards, using the round trip above.
- Before a big move, you can turn on Download and Keep Originals in Settings › Apps › Photos (or Settings › [your name] › iCloud › Photos ), if you have the space.
### How do you move photos without losing quality?
Import from Photos or Files inside the vault app, and avoid routes that compress. Some ways of sending photos shrink them:
- Messages and chat apps often send smaller copies. Messages has a Low Quality Image Mode, and many chat apps compress by default.
- AirDrop sends the original between your own devices.
- The share sheet has an Options button at the top, where you can include all photo data and choose whether to include the location.
- Screenshots of a photo are never full quality. Don't use them as a backup.
### Can you get full quality back after a vault compressed it?
Only if the original still exists somewhere. A vault can't rebuild detail it threw away. Look for the original in:
- Photos and Recently Deleted, which keeps deleted items for 30 days.
- iCloud Photos on iCloud.com or another device signed in to the same Apple Account.
- The vault's own cloud, if you used a space saver. Download the originals from there before you cancel or delete the app.
- A computer backup, or the chat or email you first received the photo in.
If you find the original, import it again into a vault that keeps full resolution, and test it first.
### Does full resolution use more storage?
Yes. A vault that keeps originals takes as much space as the photos did, and more than an optimized Photos library on the same iPhone. ProRAW and 4K video fill a phone fastest. Settings › General › iPhone Storage shows how much each app uses. If the vault backs up to your iCloud, it uses iCloud storage too: see do photo vault apps back up to iCloud?
### Does Noxium keep full resolution?
Yes. Noxium, which we make, imports HEIC, ProRAW and Live Photos as they are, and exports them in full quality with their original dates. Every item is encrypted on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM, with its name, date and place. If space runs short, Settings › iCloud backup › Free up space removes full-size copies that are already in your encrypted iCloud backup; previews stay, and originals download again when you open them. More in import and export .
Your originals, kept as they were
Noxium keeps HEIC, ProRAW and Live Photos as they are, and exports them in full quality with their dates.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Do photo vault apps reduce photo quality?
Some do, to save space, and some only when you turn on a space saver. Test yours: import one photo, export it, and compare size, resolution and date.
How do I check a photo's resolution on iPhone?
Open it in Photos and swipe up, or tap the info button. You'll see the megapixels, the pixel size, the file size and the format.
Do vaults keep Live Photos?
Not all of them. Some keep only the still photo. Press on an exported Live Photo to check it still moves.
Can I get the original back after a vault compressed it?
Only from somewhere else: Photos, Recently Deleted, iCloud Photos, the vault's cloud or a backup. The vault can't restore detail it removed.

# How to move photos into a vault app on iPhone

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/move-photos-into-vault-app
Last updated: 2026-11-26

Guide · Backup
## How to move photos into a vault app on iPhone
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 26 November 2026
Short answer
Import the photos from inside the vault app, check they arrived in full, then delete the originals from Photos and empty Recently Deleted. Importing only copies a photo: until you delete the original, it's still in your library, in iCloud Photos, and on every device signed in to your Apple Account.
Moving photos into a vault looks like one step, but it's really three: copy them in, check them, and remove every other copy. Most people do the first and forget the rest, so the "hidden" photos are still in their camera roll, in Recently Deleted, or on their iPad. This guide covers all three, and the places stray copies hide. Before you start, make sure your vault keeps full resolution , because you're about to delete the originals.
### What should you check before you move photos?
Make sure the vault is one you'll keep. Once the originals are gone, the vault holds your only copy on the phone.
- Encryption. The vault should encrypt photos on the iPhone, not just hide them behind a PIN. See are photo vault apps safe?
- A backup. Many vaults keep photos only on the phone, so deleting the app deletes them. Check how yours backs up first.
- Quality. Test one photo: import it, export it, and compare size, resolution and date.
- A way out. Check that it can export everything again, on every plan.
- Its limit. Free plans often cap the number of photos or videos.
### Does the vault need access to all your photos?
No. Since iOS 14, apps can use Apple's photo picker, which hands over only the photos you select. You can also give an app Limited Access to chosen photos, or Full Access to your whole library.
Check or change it in Settings › Privacy & Security › Photos , then the app. A vault needs Full Access only if it offers to delete originals for you or to scan your library; otherwise the picker is enough.
### How do you import photos into a vault?
From inside the vault app, in batches you can check. The buttons have different names, but the steps are the same:
- Open the vault and the album you want the photos in.
- Tap the add or import button and choose Photos (or Files, for photos saved there).
- Select the photos and videos. Start with one album or one day, not your whole library.
- Wait until it finishes. Large videos and photos stored in iCloud take longer, because iOS downloads the original first. Keep the app open and stay on Wi-Fi.
- Repeat for the next batch.
Some vaults also add photos from the share sheet in Photos, or have their own camera, whose photos never reach your camera roll. Obscura's App Store listing, for example, says it can "import in batches and delete the originals from Photos".
### How do you check the photos arrived?
Compare counts, open a few photos, and play the videos. Before you delete anything:
- Count. The number in the vault should match what you selected.
- Open a few full-size photos, including old ones, not just thumbnails.
- Play videos to the end, and press on Live Photos to see them move.
- Check the backup has finished, if your vault has one.
### How do you delete the originals?
Delete them in Photos, then empty Recently Deleted. Otherwise iOS keeps them for 30 days.
- Select the same photos in Photos. Searching by date or opening the same album makes this easier.
- Tap the Delete button and confirm. With iCloud Photos on, iOS warns that they'll be deleted from all your devices. That's what you want here, but only after checking the vault.
- Open Recently Deleted under Utilities in Photos, and unlock it with Face ID or your passcode.
- Tap Select, then Delete All (or delete just the photos you moved) and confirm.
Watch out
Deleting from Recently Deleted can't be undone. Do it only after the vault holds every photo, and its backup, if it has one, has finished.
### Where else can copies of the photos be?
In more places than your camera roll. Check each one you use:
- The Hidden album. Photos you hid earlier aren't in your main library view, but they're still there.
- Shared albums. Everyone you shared an album with can still see it, and may have saved copies. Delete the photos from the shared album too.
- The iCloud Shared Photo Library. Its photos belong to everyone in it. Check which library the photos are in before you delete, and remember others may have saved copies.
- Messages, WhatsApp and other chats. Photos you sent or received stay in the conversation. WhatsApp can also save incoming photos to your library by itself: turn off Save to Photos in its chat settings.
- Other photo backups, such as Google Photos, OneDrive or Dropbox camera uploads.
- Your Mac or PC, in its Photos library or in an iPhone backup on that computer.
Hidden photos and how they sync are explained in how to hide photos on iPhone .
### How do you move photos from another vault app?
Export from the old vault, import into the new one, check, and only then delete the old app. Vault apps can't read each other's files, so your camera roll or Files is the bridge.
- Export everything from the old vault to Photos or Files, album by album. Our guide to exporting photos from a vault app lists how popular apps do it.
- Check the exports: counts, full size, dates and videos.
- Import them into the new vault, using the steps above.
- Check the new vault, and let its backup finish.
- Delete the exported copies from Photos or Files, and empty Recently Deleted.
- Cancel the old subscription, then delete the old app. Deleting an app removes everything stored only inside it; see does deleting a vault app delete your photos?
Do it in one sitting if you can. While the photos sit in your camera roll between the two vaults, they're unprotected.
### How do you move photos into Noxium?
Tap the add button in your vault and choose From Photos , From Files or Camera . Noxium, which we make, imports HEIC, ProRAW and Live Photos as they are and encrypts each one on the iPhone. Turn on Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos , and after adding it offers to delete the originals; then empty Recently Deleted in Photos. You can also use Send to Noxium from the share sheet; those items go into the vault you open next, so open your main vault, not a decoy. The free plan holds 150 photos and 10 videos. Details in import and export .
Move in, leave nothing behind
Noxium encrypts every photo as it arrives and offers to delete the originals from Photos. Free for 150 photos and 10 videos.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Does moving photos to a vault delete them from iCloud?
No. Importing copies them. They leave iCloud Photos only when you delete them in Photos and empty Recently Deleted.
Will the photos still be in Recently Deleted?
Yes, for 30 days after you delete them in Photos. Empty Recently Deleted to remove them for good.
Can I move photos without giving the app my whole library?
Yes. Apple's photo picker gives the app only the photos you choose, and you can set Limited Access in Settings › Privacy & Security › Photos.
What happens to the photos if I delete the vault app?
Unless the app backed them up, they're deleted with it. Export them, or check the app's backup, before you delete it.

# How to hide photos on iPhone: every method, and what each one protects

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/how-to-hide-photos-on-iphone
Last updated: 2026-11-28

Guide · Hiding photos
## How to hide photos on iPhone: every method, and what each one protects
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
To hide a photo on iPhone, open Photos, touch and hold the photo, tap Hide and confirm. It moves to the Hidden album in Collections › Utilities, which needs Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode to open. That keeps it out of your library, but anyone who knows your iPhone passcode can still open it. For photos that must stay private from them, use a vault app with its own code.
To hide a photo on iPhone, open Photos, touch and hold the photo, tap Hide and confirm. It moves to the Hidden album, which needs Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode to open. This guide is for anyone who wants photos out of sight on their iPhone, and wants to know which method also keeps them from people who know the passcode.
There are four ways to do it, and they protect against different people. Hiding a photo from someone scrolling your camera roll is easy. Keeping it from someone who knows your passcode, or who picks up your iPad, takes more. Each section below gives the exact steps from Apple Support and says what the method doesn't protect.
### Which way of hiding photos should you use?
Use the Hidden album to keep photos out of sight. Use a vault app with its own code when the photos must stay private even from people who know your passcode.
Ways to hide photos on iPhone, from Apple Support pages checked 28 November 2026
Method What opens it Separate from your passcode? Syncs to your other devices? Best for
Hidden album Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode No Yes, with iCloud Photos Keeping photos out of your main library
Locking the Photos app Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode No No, the lock is set per device Stopping casual browsing of the whole library
Locked note Your passcode or a separate Notes password Optional Yes, with iCloud Notes A few photos you rarely need (no videos)
Encrypted vault app The app's own pattern, PIN or password Yes Depends on the app Photos that must stay private from anyone
### How do you hide photos with the Hidden album?
Touch and hold a photo, tap Hide, and confirm. The photo leaves your library and appears only in the Hidden album ( Apple: Hide photos with the Hidden album ). It isn't deleted: Apple's Personal Safety guide says hidden items "remain in your library".
- Open Photos and find the photo or video.
- Touch and hold it , then tap Hide and confirm.
- To hide several at once , tap Select , tap each photo, then tap the More (…) button and choose Hide .
To see hidden photos, tap Collections , scroll down to Utilities , tap Hidden , then View Album , and unlock with Face ID or Touch ID. To unhide one, touch and hold it and tap Unhide . If Hidden isn't there, or you want to know where hidden photos go on iCloud or a new iPhone, see the complete guide to hidden photos on iPhone .
To take the Hidden album itself out of view, go to Settings › Apps › Photos and turn off Show Hidden Album . Apple's Personal Safety guide places this switch under Albums on that screen, so look there if you don't see it straight away. Turning it off hides the album; it doesn't lock anything.
What the Hidden album doesn't protect:
- Your passcode opens it. The lock accepts Face ID, Touch ID or your iPhone passcode, so anyone who knows the passcode can see your hidden photos.
- It syncs. With iCloud Photos on, a photo you hide on your iPhone is hidden, but present, on your iPad and Mac too.
- iCloud holds the keys by default. Photos in iCloud are end-to-end encrypted only if you turn on Advanced Data Protection ( Apple: iCloud data security overview ).
For the full picture, read is the iPhone Hidden album private?
### How do you put Face ID on the Photos app?
The Hidden album already has Face ID on it. To put Face ID on the whole Photos app, the "gallery" in many people's searches, lock the app from its icon. Apple's guide describes this for iOS 18 and later.
- Touch and hold the Photos icon on your Home Screen until the quick actions menu opens.
- Tap Require Face ID (or Touch ID, or Passcode).
- Tap it again to confirm, then authenticate with Face ID.
These steps are from Apple's Personal Safety guide: lock or hide an app . The Hidden album's own lock lives in Photos settings, under Settings › Apps › Photos . Leave it on.
What locking the app doesn't do: it locks your whole library rather than single photos, your passcode still opens it, and the lock applies only to the device where you set it. Apple says a locked app's information stays out of places such as notification previews, search and Siri suggestions. Only apps you download can be hidden, so the Photos icon stays on your Home Screen.
### How do you hide photos on iPad and Mac?
On iPad it works as on iPhone: touch and hold the photo and tap Hide. To find the Hidden album, you may need to tap the sidebar button in the upper-left corner first. On a Mac, Control-click the photo and choose Hide Photo , or press Command-L, then confirm. With iCloud Photos on, a photo you hide on one device is hidden on all of them ( Apple ).
On a Mac the Hidden album is off by default. To see it, choose View › Show Hidden Photo Album in Photos, then unlock it with Touch ID or your login password.
### How do you hide a photo in a locked note?
Add the photo to a note, then lock the note. A locked note can use a password separate from your passcode, which makes it stronger than the Hidden album for a handful of photos.
- Open Notes and start a new note stored on your iPhone or in iCloud.
- Add the photos with the camera button.
- Tap the More (…) button and choose Lock , then pick Use iPhone Passcode or Create Password . A separate password lives in Settings › Apps › Notes › Password .
- Delete the originals from Photos, then from Recently Deleted (see below).
The limits, from Apple: Lock notes on iPhone : you can't lock a note that contains video, audio, PDFs or tags, or a note you share. If you forget a separate Notes password, Apple can't help you open those notes. Notes also have no albums or grid view.
### When should you use a photo vault app?
Use a vault app when photos must stay private from people who know your passcode, or when you have more than a handful. A good vault has its own code, encrypts files on the iPhone, and backs them up in a way you can restore.
Many vault apps only put a PIN screen in front of ordinary files. Before you trust one with photos you can't replace, check four things:
- Does it name its encryption? Look for something specific, such as AES-256, done on the device. How encrypted photo vaults work explains what the terms mean.
- Where does the backup go, and does it restore on a new iPhone?
- What if you forget your code? You want a recovery option you control, not an email reset the developer can use too.
- Does it have a decoy? If someone might make you open the app, a second code that opens a harmless vault helps. See what a decoy vault is .
We compare vault apps on these points in the best photo vault apps for iPhone .
Noxium is the vault app we make. It opens with a pattern you draw across at least 6 bolts on a 5×5 plate, not your iPhone passcode. Files are sealed with AES-256-GCM on the device, with keys from your pattern through Argon2id, and the encrypted backup goes to your own private iCloud. At setup you write down a recovery phrase. Face ID can open the main vault, so under pressure draw a decoy pattern instead.
- Draw your pattern (at least 6 bolts) and write down the recovery phrase.
- Add photos and videos from your library, or use "Send to Noxium" from the share sheet. HEIC, ProRAW and Live Photos import as they are.
- Delete the originals from Photos once they're in the vault, then empty Recently Deleted.
What Noxium doesn't protect: someone who watches you draw your pattern, someone who finds your recovery phrase, and copies you leave outside the app.
Noxium opens with a pattern on a 5×5 plate of bolts, not your iPhone passcode.

### Which mistakes leave hidden photos visible?
Most hidden photos that get seen weren't found in the Hidden album. A copy stayed somewhere else, or the lock was off. Check these:
- Treating Show Hidden Album as a lock. Turning it off only takes the album out of view. Anyone holding your unlocked iPhone can turn it back on in Settings.
- Hiding photos in a Shared Library. In the iCloud Shared Photo Library, a hidden photo moves to the Hidden album for every participant, and any of them can view or unhide it ( Apple: Hide photos on iCloud.com ).
- Leaving it in Recently Deleted. Deleted photos can be recovered there for 30 days ( Apple: If you're missing photos ). Open Collections › Utilities › Recently Deleted , unlock it, and delete them for good.
- Forgetting other copies. A photo you sent or received in Messages, WhatsApp or email has its own copy there. So do old imports on a Mac or PC.
- Erasing the iPhone without a backup. Hidden photos are part of your library. If iCloud Photos is off and there's no recent backup, erasing the iPhone deletes them with everything else.
Photos only you can see

### Questions people ask
How can I hide photos on my iPhone?
Open Photos, touch and hold the photo, tap Hide and confirm. For several, tap Select, choose them, tap More (…) and Hide. They move to the Hidden album in Collections › Utilities.
How do I put Face ID on my gallery on iPhone?
Touch and hold the Photos icon, tap Require Face ID, tap it again and authenticate. The Hidden album inside Photos is already locked by default. Your passcode still opens both.
Does hiding a photo on iPhone delete it?
No. The photo stays in your library and in iCloud Photos, shown only in the Hidden album. You can unhide it at any time.
Can someone see my hidden photos without my Face ID?
Yes, if they know your iPhone passcode, or can unlock another device signed in to your Apple Account with iCloud Photos on.
How do I hide videos on iPhone?
The same way: touch and hold the video in Photos and tap Hide. A locked note can't hold video, so use the Hidden album or a vault app. See how to hide videos on iPhone .
Can I hide the Hidden album?
Yes. In Settings › Apps › Photos, turn off Show Hidden Album. The album disappears from the Photos app until you turn it back on. It's out of view, not locked.

# Is the iPhone Hidden album actually private?

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/is-iphone-hidden-album-private
Last updated: 2026-11-28

Guide · Hidden album
## Is the iPhone Hidden album actually private?
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
Yes from casual eyes, no from anyone who knows your passcode. The Hidden album is locked by default on iOS 16 and later and opens with Face ID, Touch ID or your iPhone passcode. It isn't a separate vault: the passcode opens it, it syncs to your other devices with iCloud Photos, and in iCloud it's end-to-end encrypted only if you turn on Advanced Data Protection.
Yes, the iPhone Hidden album is safe from someone scrolling through your unlocked phone. No, it isn't safe from anyone who knows your iPhone passcode, can unlock your iPad or Mac, or can make you unlock it. This guide is for people who searched "is the iPhone Hidden album safe" and want to know exactly who it keeps out, and who it doesn't.
The Hidden album is the first place most people put private photos, because it's free and already on the iPhone. It's good at one job: keeping photos out of your main library. Here is what it protects, what it doesn't, and how to make it stricter, from Apple's own documentation.
### What does the Hidden album actually do?
It takes photos out of view. A hidden photo shows up only in the Hidden album, under Collections › Utilities ( Apple: If you're missing photos ).
On iOS 16, iPadOS 16.1 and macOS Ventura and later, the Hidden album is locked by default and needs authentication to open in Photos ( Apple: Hide photos with the Hidden album ). You can also take the album out of view with Settings › Apps › Photos › Show Hidden Album . For step-by-step help finding, viewing and adding to it, see how to view hidden photos on iPhone .
What it doesn't do is move, copy or re-encrypt the photo. Apple's Personal Safety guide says hidden photos "remain in your library", and Apple's developer documentation shows that "hidden" is a property of the photo ( Apple: includeHiddenAssets ). Apple doesn't describe any extra encryption for hidden photos.
### Who can see your hidden photos?
Anyone who can unlock your iPhone with its passcode, or unlock another device signed in to your Apple Account, can see them. Here's how it plays out with default settings.
Who can open the Hidden album, with default settings, based on Apple Support pages checked 28 November 2026
Situation Can they see hidden photos?
Someone scrolling your unlocked iPhone No. The album asks for Face ID or Touch ID.
Someone who knows your iPhone passcode Yes. The lock accepts the passcode.
Someone using your iPad or Mac Yes, if they can unlock that device and iCloud Photos is on.
Someone in your iCloud Shared Photo Library Yes, for photos in the shared library. Every participant can view or unhide them.
Someone who makes you unlock your phone Yes. There's no second code or decoy.
Apple, or a legal request to Apple for your iCloud data With standard protection, Apple holds the keys to iCloud Photos. With Advanced Data Protection on, it doesn't.
Apps you give full access to your library are a grey area. Apple's developer documentation lets an app ask for hidden photos along with the rest. It doesn't say whether the Face ID lock stops that, so we don't claim it does.
### Why are your passcode and your other devices the weak points?
Because the Face ID lock on the Hidden album isn't a separate lock. If Face ID fails or is skipped, your iPhone passcode opens the album. Partners, children and housemates often know that passcode, or have watched it typed. A six-digit code, the default length ( Apple: Use a passcode ), is easy to shoulder-surf in public.
The second weak point is syncing. With iCloud Photos on, photos you hide on one device are hidden on your other devices too ( Apple ). They exist on every iPad and Mac signed in to your Apple Account. On a Mac, the Hidden album is off by default and opens with Touch ID or the login password. On a shared family iPad, anyone who can unlock it can open the album. If you think someone already has, see did someone open my Hidden album?
The third is the Shared Library. In the iCloud Shared Photo Library, a hidden photo moves to the Hidden album for every participant, "where they can view or stop hiding it" ( Apple ).
### Is the Hidden album encrypted in iCloud?
End-to-end, only with Advanced Data Protection. With standard data protection, iCloud Photos is encrypted in transit and on Apple's servers, but Apple holds the keys. With Advanced Data Protection on, Photos is end-to-end encrypted and the keys stay on your trusted devices ( Apple: iCloud data security overview ).
To turn it on, go to Settings › [your name] › iCloud › Advanced Data Protection and tap Turn On . You'll need two-factor authentication, iOS 16.2 or later on your iPhone, and a recovery contact or recovery key, because Apple no longer has the keys to help you recover that data ( Apple: Turn on Advanced Data Protection ).
### How do you make the Hidden album more private?
- Keep the lock on. It's on by default; the setting lives in Settings › Apps › Photos . Don't turn it off.
- Hide the album. Turn off Show Hidden Album on the same screen. This takes it out of view; it doesn't lock it.
- Use a stronger passcode. In Settings › Face ID & Passcode › Change Passcode › Passcode Options , choose a custom alphanumeric code ( Apple ).
- Turn on Advanced Data Protection for end-to-end encrypted iCloud Photos.
- Check where else the photos live: Recently Deleted (30 days), shared albums, the Shared Library, Messages, and any Mac or iPad on your account.
### When is the Hidden album not enough?
When the people you're worried about know your passcode, share your devices, or could make you unlock your phone. Then you need a code that's separate from your iPhone's, encryption with a key only you hold, and ideally a way to show something harmless if you're pressured. That last idea is a decoy vault .
That's what a photo vault app is for. Noxium, which we make, opens with a pattern you draw across at least 6 bolts on a 5×5 plate, separate from your passcode. Everything is encrypted on the device with AES-256-GCM, with keys from your pattern through Argon2id, and the pattern is never stored. A second pattern opens a separate, harmless vault; the free plan includes 1. The encrypted backup goes to your own private iCloud, and on a new iPhone you draw your pattern to restore it.
What Noxium doesn't protect: someone who watches you draw your real pattern, someone who finds your recovery phrase, and copies you leave in Photos or Messages. Face ID can open the main vault, so under pressure draw the decoy pattern instead.
In Noxium, a second pattern opens a separate, harmless decoy vault.
Other vault apps differ a lot in how they protect photos. See photo vault apps compared , or read every way to hide photos on iPhone .

### Questions people ask
Is the iPhone Hidden album safe?
Safe from casual browsing, not from anyone who knows your passcode. It opens with Face ID, Touch ID or the passcode, and syncs to your other devices with iCloud Photos.
Can someone see my Hidden album without Face ID?
Yes, if they know your iPhone passcode. The lock accepts Face ID, Touch ID or the passcode.
Does the Hidden album show up on my Mac and iPad?
Yes, if iCloud Photos is on. On a Mac, the Hidden album is off by default and opens with Touch ID or your login password.
Is the Hidden album safe from Apple?
Only with Advanced Data Protection on. With standard protection, Apple holds the keys for iCloud Photos. With Advanced Data Protection, Photos is end-to-end encrypted.
Do hidden photos get deleted if I turn off Show Hidden Album?
No. Turning it off only takes the album out of view. The photos stay in your library until you unhide or delete them.

# Hidden photos on iPhone: how to find, view, add, lock and move them

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/hidden-photos-iphone
Last updated: 2026-11-15

Guide · Hidden album
## Hidden photos on iPhone: how to find, view, add, lock and move them
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 15 November 2026
Short answer
To view hidden photos on iPhone, open Photos, tap Collections, scroll down to Utilities and tap Hidden, then tap View Album and unlock with Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode. If Hidden isn't there, turn on Show Hidden Album in Settings › Apps › Photos. To add a photo, touch and hold it and tap Hide.
The Hidden album is the iPhone's built-in place for photos you don't want in your main library. It's also easy to lose track of: Apple moved it during the iOS 18 Photos redesign, it can be switched off entirely, and it behaves differently on a Mac, on iCloud.com and on a new iPhone. This guide answers each of those questions for iOS 26, with Apple's own steps and links to the Apple Support pages they come from.
### How do you view hidden photos on iPhone?
Open the Hidden album under Utilities in Photos, then unlock it. In iOS 26 it takes four taps ( Apple: Hide photos with the Hidden album ):
- Open Photos and tap Collections . On iPad, tap the sidebar button first.
- Scroll down to Utilities and tap Hidden .
- Tap View Album.
- Unlock it with Face ID, Touch ID or your iPhone passcode.
The album locks again when you leave Photos. On iOS 15 and earlier, look for Hidden under Albums › Utilities or Other Albums instead; it isn't locked on those versions.
### Why can't you find the Hidden album?
Usually because Show Hidden Album is turned off, which removes the album from Photos without touching the photos in it. Turn it back on:
- Open Settings and tap Apps › Photos .
- Turn on Show Hidden Album. It's on by default.
- Go back to Photos , open Collections and scroll to Utilities.
Two other common causes: you're looking at the top of Collections, and Utilities sits near the bottom of the list; or iCloud Photos is still syncing on a new device, so photos hidden elsewhere haven't arrived yet. Hidden photos also disappear from your other albums: Apple says hidden items "don't appear anywhere else in Photos, like the Library, other albums, or even the Photos widget on your Home Screen". If a photo is missing from an album, check Hidden before you assume it's gone. More causes and fixes are in hidden photos disappeared on iPhone .
### Can you view hidden photos without Face ID?
Yes, with your iPhone passcode. Face ID and Touch ID are a shortcut; when they fail or you tap the fallback, the passcode unlocks the Hidden album. There is no separate password for it. That also means anyone who knows your passcode can open it, which is the main limit of the album (more below).
### How do you add photos to the Hidden album?
Touch and hold a photo or video in Photos, tap Hide, then confirm. It moves out of your library and into Hidden.
- One photo: touch and hold it, tap Hide , then confirm.
- Several at once: tap Select , tap each photo, tap the More (…) button, then Hide .
- From an open photo: tap the More (…) button at the top and choose Hide .
Videos, screenshots and Live Photos hide the same way. A photo in another app (Messages, WhatsApp, Files) has to be saved to Photos first, and the copy in that app stays where it is. There's no setting that sends new camera photos straight to Hidden. For every other way to hide photos, including locked notes and vault apps, see how to hide photos on iPhone .
### How do you unhide a photo?
Open the Hidden album, touch and hold the photo, and tap Unhide. It goes back to your library in its original place by date. To unhide several, tap Select in the Hidden album, choose the photos, tap the More (…) button and tap Unhide.
### How do you lock hidden photos on iPhone?
They're already locked on iOS 16 and later. Check that the lock is on in Settings › Apps › Photos : Use Face ID (or Use Touch ID or Use Passcode) should be on. The same switch locks Recently Deleted.
What you can't do is give the Hidden album its own password; changing the Hidden album password means changing your passcode. If you want a lock that's separate from your passcode, you have three options:
- Lock the whole Photos app: touch and hold the Photos icon and tap Require Face ID (iOS 18 and later). It still falls back to your passcode.
- A locked note with a separate Notes password, for a handful of photos.
- A vault app with its own PIN, password or pattern.
Each option, step by step: how to lock photos on iPhone with Face ID or a pattern .
### Do hidden photos go to iCloud?
Yes, if iCloud Photos is on. Hidden photos upload like any other photo, and Apple says photos you hide on one device are hidden on your other devices too. If iCloud Photos is off, they're part of your iPhone's iCloud Backup instead, with the rest of your library ( Apple: What does iCloud back up? ).
In iCloud, hidden photos get the same protection as the rest of your library. Apple holds the encryption keys for iCloud Photos unless you turn on Advanced Data Protection, which makes Photos end-to-end encrypted. Hiding a photo doesn't add encryption of its own; read is the iPhone Hidden album actually private? for what that means in practice.
### Do hidden photos transfer to a new iPhone?
Yes, with the rest of your library, as long as it transfers. How they arrive depends on iCloud Photos:
How hidden photos reach a new iPhone (iOS 26)
Your setup What happens to hidden photos Check before erasing the old iPhone
iCloud Photos on They download from iCloud after you sign in with the same Apple Account, still hidden The upload finished on the old iPhone (Photos shows no items waiting)
iCloud Photos off, iCloud Backup They come back with the backup when you restore from it The last backup is recent and complete
Quick Start, phone to phone With iCloud Photos off, they copy across with the library; with it on, they download from iCloud as above The Hidden album on the new iPhone has the same number of items
Whatever the route, open the Hidden album on the new iPhone and compare the count before you erase the old one. Photos inside vault apps are a different story: many vault apps leave their files out of the iPhone backup on purpose, so read how to move a photo vault to a new iPhone before you switch.
### How do you view hidden photos on a Mac or Windows PC?
On a Mac, the Hidden album is off by default. In Photos, choose View › Show Hidden Photo Album , select Hidden in the sidebar under Utilities, click View Album and unlock with Touch ID or your login password. If your iPhone's hidden photos aren't there, see how to view hidden photos on a Mac .
On a Windows PC, or any computer, use a browser: go to icloud.com/photos, sign in, select Hidden in the sidebar, then Show Hidden Photos ( Apple: Hide photos on iCloud.com ). This needs iCloud Photos on. People report mixed results seeing hidden photos through the iCloud for Windows app, so iCloud.com is the reliable route. More in viewing iPhone hidden photos on Windows .
### Can you have more than one Hidden album?
No. iOS has exactly one Hidden album, and you can't create folders or albums inside it. Everything hidden sits in one grid, behind one lock. If you want separate private albums, for example one for documents and one for personal photos, see how to get multiple hidden albums on iPhone .
### What doesn't the Hidden album protect?
It keeps photos out of sight, not out of reach. Anyone with your passcode can open it, it appears on every iPad and Mac signed in to your Apple Account, and it isn't separately encrypted. A hidden photo is the same file in the same library, with a flag that says "don't show this".
When that's not enough, a vault app with its own code is the next step. Noxium, which we make, opens with a pattern you draw on a 5×5 plate of bolts, separate from your iPhone passcode, and encrypts every photo on the device. You can make albums inside the vault, and a second pattern opens a separate decoy vault.
Get Noxium free on the App Store →
A hidden album with its own key
Noxium opens with a pattern only you know, not your iPhone passcode, and encrypts every photo on your iPhone. Free for 150 photos, 10 videos and 1 decoy vault. No ads, no account.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Where is the Hidden album in iOS 26?
In Photos, tap Collections and scroll down to Utilities. Hidden is listed there with Recently Deleted. If it's missing, turn on Show Hidden Album in Settings › Apps › Photos.
Does hiding a photo delete it?
No. Hiding only moves the photo out of your library view. It stays on your iPhone and in iCloud Photos, and you can unhide it at any time.
Can someone see my hidden photos?
Anyone who knows your iPhone passcode can, and so can anyone who can unlock a Mac or iPad signed in to your Apple Account with iCloud Photos on. Someone scrolling your unlocked iPhone can't, because the album asks for Face ID.
Do hidden photos show up in other apps?
Not while the Hidden album is locked, which it is by default. If you turn off Use Face ID in Settings › Apps › Photos, apps with full access to your library can request hidden photos.
Why did my hidden photos disappear?
Most often, Show Hidden Album was turned off, or iCloud Photos hasn't finished syncing on that device. Check Settings › Apps › Photos, then look in Recently Deleted, where deleted photos stay for 30 days.

# Can you have multiple hidden albums on iPhone?

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/multiple-hidden-albums-iphone
Last updated: 2026-11-15

Guide · Hidden album
## Can you have multiple hidden albums on iPhone?
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 15 November 2026
Short answer
No. iOS has one Hidden album, with no folders or albums inside it, and one lock: your Face ID or passcode. To keep several private groups apart, use separate locked notes (they share one Notes password), or a vault app that lets you make albums and lock each one with its own code.
The Hidden album works well for one pile of photos. It gets awkward when you have several kinds of private photos: scans of your passport and bank cards, photos of a medical issue, a surprise you're planning, personal photos. They all end up in one grid, behind one lock, and anyone you unlock it for sees all of them. This guide explains what iOS 26 can and can't do, and the ways to get properly separate hidden albums.
### Why does iOS only have one Hidden album?
Because hiding in Photos is a flag on each photo, not a place. When you tap Hide, the photo stays in the same library and is marked "hidden"; the Hidden album simply shows every photo with that flag. There's no way to have two flags, so there's no way to have two Hidden albums. You can't create albums inside it either, and it can't be sorted into folders ( Apple: Hide photos with the Hidden album ).
The lock works the same way. The Hidden album opens with Face ID, Touch ID or your iPhone passcode, the same as Recently Deleted. There's no setting to give it, or any part of it, a different code. For how to view, add to and lock the album, see the complete guide to hidden photos on iPhone .
### Can you sort hidden photos into albums?
No. Hiding a photo removes it from every other album as well: Apple says hidden items "don't appear anywhere else in Photos, like the Library, other albums, or even the Photos widget". So you can't use albums to split hidden photos into groups. And leaving private photos unhidden in a named album doesn't help either, because albums you create open without any lock and anyone who opens Photos can browse them.
### What are the ways to get several hidden albums?
There are three that actually keep groups apart. They differ in whether each group gets its own code.
Ways to keep several groups of private photos apart on iPhone (iOS 26)
Method Separate groups? Separate code per group? Good for
Hidden album No, one grid No, your passcode One pile of photos you want out of sight
Locked notes Yes, one note per group No, all locked notes share one password A few photos per group, such as document scans
Vault app with locked albums Yes In some apps, yes Many photos, videos, or groups you open for different people
### How do you use locked notes as separate hidden albums?
Make one note per group, add the photos, and lock each note. Each note then opens on its own, so unlocking your document scans doesn't show anything else.
- Open Notes and create a note. Give it a plain title, such as "Documents" (the title stays visible when the note is locked).
- Tap the camera button , choose Choose Photo or Video , and add the photos for that group.
- Tap the More (…) button and choose Lock .
- Repeat for each group.
- Delete the originals from Photos, then from Recently Deleted.
The catch is the password. All locked notes in an account use the same one: either your iPhone passcode or one Notes password you set in Settings › Apps › Notes › Password ( Apple: Lock or unlock notes on iPhone ). So the notes are separate, but anyone with that password can open every one. Notes also have no photo grid, and long videos are clumsy in them.
### How do vault apps handle multiple hidden albums?
Most photo vault apps let you create as many albums as you like inside the vault, and some let you lock individual albums with a code of their own. That's the closest thing to several separate Hidden albums, each with its own key. What to check before you choose one:
- Is each album locked with its own code, or only the app? Many apps have one PIN for everything, which is the same problem as the Hidden album.
- Is it encrypted? A per-album PIN only matters if the photos behind it are encrypted, not just hidden behind a screen.
- Can you show something harmless if pressured? A decoy vault opens with a different code and shows only what you put in it.
- Does the backup include every album, and does it restore on a new iPhone?
We compared 17 vault apps on these points in the best photo vault apps for iPhone .
### Multiple hidden albums in Noxium
Noxium, which we make, has two ways to keep groups apart. Inside the vault you can make albums and albums inside albums. With Noxium Pro, an album can have its own pattern, so it stays locked even when the vault is open. On the free plan, a second pattern opens a separate decoy vault with its own photos. An album with its own pattern gets its own encryption key, and its photos are re-encrypted with it, so the vault's pattern alone can't open them.
- Make an album: in the vault's albums, tap the New album button, name it, and move photos into it.
- Give it its own pattern (Pro): touch and hold the album, tap Give it its own pattern and draw a new pattern. The album stays locked inside the open vault until that pattern is drawn.
- Add a decoy vault (free): go to Settings › Vaults , draw a second pattern, and keep harmless photos in that vault.
A second pattern opens a separate decoy vault. Pro adds albums with their own pattern.
Get Noxium free on the App Store →
What it doesn't protect: if someone watches you draw a pattern, or makes you draw it, they can open what that pattern opens. And photos you sent in Messages or other apps still have copies there.
Separate albums, separate keys
In Noxium, every photo is encrypted on your iPhone, and a second pattern opens a separate decoy vault. Free for 150 photos, 10 videos and 1 decoy vault. No ads, no account.

### Questions people ask
Can you create a second Hidden album on iPhone?
No. iOS 26 has one Hidden album per photo library, and you can't add albums or folders inside it.
Can you password-protect a single album in Photos?
Not in Apple's Photos app. Only the Hidden album and Recently Deleted are locked, both with Face ID or your passcode. To lock a single album with its own code, you need a vault app that supports it.
Can different locked notes have different passwords?
No. All locked notes in one account use the same password: your iPhone passcode or a single Notes password. If you forget a separate Notes password, Apple can't recover the notes locked with it.
Does the iCloud Shared Photo Library have its own Hidden album?
It shares one. If you hide a photo in the Shared Library, it moves to the Hidden album for every participant, and any of them can view or unhide it.

# How to move a photo vault to a new iPhone in 4 steps without losing photos

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/move-photo-vault-to-new-iphone
Last updated: 2026-11-28

Guide · New iPhone
## How to move a private photo vault to a new iPhone without losing photos
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
Back up the vault inside the vault app first, then restore it inside the app on the new iPhone. Quick Start and iCloud Backup bring the app across, but the photos come back only if the app's own backup has them. Save a copy of anything you can't replace, and erase the old iPhone only after every photo opens on the new one.
To move a photo vault to a new iPhone, back up the vault inside the vault app, then restore it inside the app on the new phone. Quick Start or an iCloud backup brings the app across, but the photos inside it come back only if the app's own backup has them. This guide is for anyone with photos in a vault app, such as Private Photo Vault, Keepsafe, Calculator#, Vaultaire or Noxium, who is about to switch iPhones.
Why photos go missing: an iPhone backup is not a copy of everything. Apple says iCloud backups include what's on the device that doesn't already sync to iCloud , and leave out data stored in other cloud services and Face ID settings. So a vault kept in the developer's own cloud comes back only through that app's login, a vault the app never finished backing up doesn't come back at all, and Face ID has to be set up again before it opens anything. The four steps below work for any vault app.
### Step 1: Where does your vault app keep its backup?
Open the vault's settings and find its backup, sync or cloud section. Answer three questions: where does the backup go, is it on, and what will you need to restore it?
Where vault apps keep their backups, and what restoring needs
Backup type What you need on the new iPhone Risk
iPhone backup or Quick Start A full transfer from the old iPhone Works only if the app's vault files are part of the backup. Check, don't assume.
The developer's own cloud Your login for that app, often a paid plan Lost login, lapsed plan, or a service that shuts down.
Your own iCloud, managed by the app The same Apple Account, plus the vault's code An unfinished upload if iCloud storage is full.
A file you export yourself The file, and its password if it has one Only as current as your last export.
Here is what popular vault apps say about backup in their own US App Store descriptions, checked 28 November 2026. It's what each listing claims, not something we tested.
Backup, as each app's US App Store listing describes it
App What the listing says Check before you switch
Vaultaire Encrypted iCloud backup in your private iCloud, on by default, on Free and Pro. Multi-device sync needs Pro. Same Apple Account on the new iPhone.
Keepsafe Private Cloud stores up to 10,000 items and syncs to your Keepsafe installs on any platform. Your Keepsafe login, and that sync is on.
Calculator# Backup to iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive or OneDrive. Which service you chose, and that the last backup finished.
Private Photo Vault Cloud Vault backup with its own Cloud Vault Password, which isn't stored on their servers. The free version doesn't back up to Cloud Vault. That you're on a plan with Cloud Vault, and that you know that password.
Hide it Pro Backup to its cloud storage, with an optional monthly subscription for more space. That the backup is on and complete.
Secret Photo Vault - Lock Photos "All of your data in this app is stored only in your device." Offers export over iTunes File Sharing and Wi-Fi. Export everything first (Step 2).
Privault The description doesn't mention backup. Ask the developer, and export first.
If you can't find any backup setting, assume the photos exist only on the old phone. For more on which apps keep a cloud copy, read do photo vault apps back up to iCloud?
### Step 2: Finish the backup and save a safety copy
Make sure the vault's backup is complete, then keep a second copy of what you can't replace. Do this on the old iPhone, before you start the new one.
- Connect to Wi-Fi and power, and open the vault app. Look for "backed up", a last-backup time, or a count of items still waiting.
- Back up the iPhone too. Go to Settings › [your name] › iCloud › iCloud Backup and tap Back Up Now . The date and time of the last backup shows under Back Up Now ( Apple Support ). If iPhone says there isn't enough iCloud storage, the backup won't finish until you free up or add space.
- Write down the counts. Note how many photos and videos the vault holds, so you can compare on the new phone.
- Export a safety copy of your most important photos and videos to somewhere you control, such as a Mac or an encrypted external drive. Check that the export keeps full quality and dates (see how to export photos from a vault app ). Exported copies are no longer protected by the vault, so keep them private and delete them once the move is done.
- Write down every way in: the vault code, any recovery phrase or recovery email, and the code for each extra vault, such as a decoy vault . Face ID settings aren't in an iCloud backup ( Apple Support ), so expect to type the code on the new phone first. If you've lost it, read forgot your photo vault password? before you switch.
### Step 3: Set up the new iPhone, then restore inside the vault app
Move the iPhone with Quick Start or from an iCloud backup, signed in to the same Apple Account. Then open the vault app and restore the vault from its own backup.
With Quick Start ( Apple Support ):
- Put the new iPhone next to the old one. The old device needs iOS 11 or later, Wi-Fi on and Bluetooth on. Plug both in.
- Follow the setup screens on the new iPhone and choose how to move your data. Downloading from iCloud lets you use the new phone while apps and data arrive in the background. Transferring directly from the old phone means neither phone can be used until the transfer finishes.
- Keep both phones near each other and plugged in until the move is complete.
From an iCloud backup ( Apple Support ):
- Turn on the new iPhone and follow the setup steps until you reach Transfer Your Apps & Data .
- Tap From iCloud Backup and sign in to your Apple Account.
- Choose the most recent backup , after checking its date and size.
- Stay on Wi-Fi and power until the progress bar finishes. If the phone is already set up, Apple says to erase it before you follow these steps.
Then restore the vault: open the vault app and follow its own restore steps, such as logging in, entering your code or choosing restore. Large libraries can take hours, so keep the new phone on Wi-Fi and power.
### Step 4: Check every photo, then erase the old iPhone
Erase the old iPhone only after the new one passes these checks. Until then, the old phone is your copy.
- Compare the counts with the ones you wrote down in Step 2.
- Open a few full-size photos and play a few videos , including old ones, not just thumbnails.
- Check albums, notes and every extra vault , such as a decoy.
- Delete your safety copies from Step 2 once everything is there.
- Then erase the old iPhone.
If something is missing, stop. Don't delete or reinstall the vault app on either phone, and don't erase the old iPhone. Reinstalling can remove files that might still be recoverable. Our guide to finding lost or deleted vault photos walks through what to try next.
### How do you move Noxium to a new iPhone?
Draw your pattern on the new iPhone and the vault restores. Noxium, which we make, keeps an encrypted backup in your own private iCloud (CloudKit), and only encrypted data leaves the device. Backup and restore are part of the free plan.
- On the new iPhone: sign in to the same Apple Account and install Noxium. Keep the old iPhone as it is for now.
- Draw your pattern. The vault restores. If you've forgotten the pattern, your recovery phrase opens the vault.
- Check it as in Step 4 before you erase the old phone.
Noxium encrypts on the iPhone, then backs up to your own iCloud.
What it doesn't protect: nobody can reset a Noxium pattern, not us and not Apple. If you lose both the pattern and the recovery phrase, the backup can't be opened. Keeping the vault on an iPhone and an iPad at the same time needs iPhone and iPad sync , which is part of Noxium Pro.
The recovery phrase you write down at setup also opens the vault on a new iPhone.
Get Noxium free on the App Store →
New phone? Everything comes back.

Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Does Quick Start move my photo vault app?
It moves the app, but the photos come back only if the vault's own backup, or the iPhone backup, has them. Check where your vault backs up (Step 1) before you switch.
Do I need the same Apple Account on the new iPhone?
Yes, for vaults that back up to your own iCloud: the backup lives in that Apple Account. For vaults that use their own cloud, you need that app's login instead.
Will Face ID open my vault on the new iPhone?
Not straight away. Apple's iCloud backups don't include Face ID settings, so set up Face ID on the new iPhone and expect to enter the vault's code, PIN or pattern first.
Can I keep my vault on both the old and the new iPhone?
Only if the app syncs between devices. Most vaults restore a backup onto one phone and don't keep two devices in step, so look for sync, not just backup, in the app's settings. Backups in your own iCloud only restore on devices signed in to the same Apple Account.
What if vault photos are already missing after the switch?
Stop and keep both phones as they are. Don't reinstall the app or erase the old iPhone. Check whether the old phone still opens the vault, look for a restore option or a web login, and email the developer with your app version and what happened.
How long does restoring a vault take?
It depends on the size of the library and your connection. Thousands of photos and long videos can take hours. Keep the new phone on Wi-Fi and power, and don't erase the old one until it's done.
