# Photo vault recovery: how to get lost or deleted vault photos back

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/photo-vault-lost-photos
Last updated: 2026-11-28

Guide · Missing photos
## Your photo vault app lost your photos: what to do now
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
Photo vault recovery only works from a copy that still exists, so don't delete, reinstall or reset anything yet: deleting an iPhone app deletes its data. Check the app's trash or a second vault, your old phone, the app's own cloud, your iCloud and any computer backup, in that order. Then email the developer with your app version and what happened.
You can often recover photos from a photo vault app, but only from a copy that still exists: a trash folder or second vault inside the app, your old phone, the app's own cloud, your iCloud, or a computer backup. If no copy exists anywhere, no app or service can bring them back. This guide is for iPhone owners whose vault photos went missing or were deleted, with recovery steps for Private Photo Vault, Keepsafe, Gallery Vault and other popular vaults.
Missing photos were one of the most common complaints when we read recent one- and two-star App Store reviews of eight vault apps in October 2026 ( more on our about page ). Often "missing" means "not where you're looking". Locked out rather than missing photos? See what to do if you forgot your photo vault password .
### What should you do before you delete or reinstall the app?
Stop, and don't delete it yet. Apple says deleting an app "removes the app and its related data" ( Apple: check iPhone storage ), and a vault app's photos are that data. Reinstalling gives you an empty vault. More in does deleting a vault app delete your photos?
Before you delete, reinstall, reset or switch phones, do these in order:
- Check the app's backup. Open its settings and look for backup, sync or cloud. Note whether it's on, when it last finished, and which account it uses.
- Export anything that still opens. A plain copy in Photos or Files is better than no copy. See how to export photos from a vault app .
- Write down what a restore will need: the account email, any cloud or backup password, and your PIN, pattern or recovery phrase. Private Photo Vault, for example, says it can't recover a forgotten Cloud Vault password ( Private Photo Vault FAQ ).
- Leave the vault app in your iPhone backup. In Settings › [your name] › iCloud › Storage › Backups (or Manage Account Storage on some versions), tap this iPhone and keep the vault app switched on. Apple says turning an app off there deletes its backup data from iCloud ( Apple: manage iCloud storage ).
- Offload instead of deleting if you only need space. In Settings › General › iPhone Storage , Apple's Offload App "frees up storage used by the app, but keeps its documents and data" ( Apple ).
- Email the developer and wait for an answer. Private Photo Vault's FAQ asks for exactly this before you delete or reinstall.
And don't do these:
- Don't restore an older iPhone backup over your phone yet. Private Photo Vault's FAQ warns that restoring a computer backup can replace the data on the phone now.
- Don't pay for a "vault recovery" tool or service. Software can't decrypt a properly encrypted vault without its key. If the vault isn't encrypted, the developer can help for free.
### Where could the photos still be?
Check these places in order. Most recoveries happen at one of the first three.
- Inside the app, but somewhere else. Look in other albums or folders, in a trash or "Recently Deleted" area (Keepsafe has a Trash, for example), and behind a second PIN. Private Photo Vault's listing includes a decoy password, and a decoy you set up and forgot opens a different set of photos. See what a decoy vault is .
- On your old iPhone or iPad. Some vaults keep photos only on the device you added them on. Secret Photo Vault's App Store listing says all its data is stored only on your device ( App Store ). Open the vault on the old phone before you erase it.
- In the app's cloud or your iCloud. Account-based vaults such as Keepsafe restore when you sign in to the same account. Vaults that back up to your private iCloud, such as Vaultaire, need the same Apple Account. The app-by-app steps are below.
- On a computer. Look for an iPhone backup made with Finder, Apple Devices or iTunes, or for copies you sent over Wi-Fi transfer.
- In Photos. Open Photos, swipe up, and look under Utilities › Recently Deleted. Apple keeps items there for 30 days ( Apple: recover deleted photos ). If you deleted the originals after importing them into the vault, they may still be there.
### How do you recover photos in Private Photo Vault, Keepsafe, Gallery Vault and other apps?
Follow the steps for the app you used, because each one stores and backs up photos differently. All of this comes from each maker's own help pages or App Store listing, checked 28 November 2026.
Where each vault app can keep a copy, from its maker's own pages (checked 28 November 2026)
App Where a copy can be How you get it back
Private Photo Vault Cloud Vault (premium); a computer backup of the iPhone Sign in with your Cloud Vault password, or restore the computer backup
Keepsafe Keepsafe's cloud backup; the in-app Trash Sign in to the same account with Backup & Sync on; Trash needs Premium
Gallery Vault (Android) The phone; Google Drive if you linked it Settings › Find Lost Files, or the Google Drive you linked
PV The phone (deleting the app deletes its data); Wi-Fi transfers; third-party cloud (Pro) Your own transferred copies or cloud backup
Vaultaire Your private iCloud (on by default, Free and Pro) Open the vault on the new iPhone from its iCloud backup
Obscura Automatic local backups; an exported vault file; your iPhone backup when iCloud Backup is on Import Vault, or restore the iPhone backup
Calculator# iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive or OneDrive, if you connected one Restore from the cloud you chose
Noxium (ours) Your private iCloud; Recently Deleted for 30 days Draw your pattern on the new iPhone
#### Private Photo Vault
Private Photo Vault, by Legendary Software Labs, keeps photos on the phone unless you turned on Cloud Vault. Its App Store listing says the free version doesn't back up to Cloud Vault ( App Store ). From its FAQ:
- Cloud Vault was on and finished uploading: sign in on the phone and the files restore. You need your Cloud Vault password, which is separate from the app lock and which the company can't recover.
- You backed up the old iPhone to a computer with Finder, Apple Devices or iTunes: restore that backup to the new iPhone, then check your files before you clear the old one.
- You deleted the app and had neither: the FAQ says they can't restore deleted files without a usable backup.
The same FAQ notes that some customers have had trouble restoring vault data from iCloud device backups, so don't rely on those alone ( Private Photo Vault FAQ ).
#### Keepsafe
Keepsafe is account-based, so recovery runs through your Keepsafe email.
- New phone or reinstall: install Keepsafe, sign in to the same account, turn on Settings › Backup & Sync , and keep the app open with the screen on until syncing finishes ( Keepsafe: transfer to a new phone ).
- Deleted inside the app: go to Settings › Trash , select the items and tap Recover. Keepsafe says recovering from Trash needs Premium, and items removed from Trash can't be recovered ( Keepsafe: recovering items from Trash ).
- Lost access to your email: Keepsafe sends access codes only to a verified address, and says an account can't be recovered without one ( Keepsafe Help Center ).
#### Gallery Vault
Several different apps are called Gallery Vault, so check the maker's name on the app's store page first. The widely used Android GalleryVault has its help center run by ThinkYeah. Its steps:
- Open Gallery Vault's Settings and use Find Lost Files. This works if you haven't cleared the app's data or changed phones ( ThinkYeah: recover lost files ).
- Leave its hidden folder alone. ThinkYeah says not to delete, rename or move the folder that starts with .galleryvault_DoNotDelete, and to stop cleaning apps from removing it.
- Back up before a new phone or factory reset. Its Google Play listing says hidden files are stored only on your device, and ThinkYeah recommends linking Google Drive.
On iPhone, one app named "GalleryVault -Hide Photo Video" (DAOWEI Network Technology) has a developer reply on its App Store page saying files are cleaned up when the app is uninstalled ( App Store ). Other Gallery Vault apps on iPhone come from other makers, so use their own help pages.
### What happened? Match your situation
Pick the row closest to what you did just before the photos went missing.
Common ways vault photos go missing, and where to look first
What happened Look first
Switched to a new iPhone The old iPhone, then the app's own backup or cloud restore
Deleted or reinstalled the app The app's cloud, your iCloud, or a computer backup, signed in with the same account; without one, the photos are usually gone
App was updated, then photos disappeared Force-quit and reopen; check for another update; contact the developer before reinstalling
Subscription ended Whether the app limits access on the free plan; resubscribing may restore access
Entered a different PIN or pattern You may be in a decoy vault; lock it and try your main code
Only thumbnails show, or videos won't play Full-size files may still be syncing; keep the app open on Wi-Fi and power
### How do you ask the developer for help?
Email the developer before you change anything else. Their contact details are on the app's App Store page under App Support, or in the app's settings. Include:
- The app name and version, and your iPhone model and iOS version.
- What you did just before the photos went missing (update, new phone, reinstall, subscription change).
- Roughly how many items are missing, and whether thumbnails show.
- Whether you used the app's cloud backup, and the account email if it has one.
Never send your PIN, password, pattern or recovery phrase. A real developer won't ask for it.
### How do you stop it happening again?
Use a vault with a backup you can restore, check it now and then, and keep your own copy of anything you can't replace.
- Know where your backup lives and what you need to restore it: an account, an Apple Account, a code, a recovery phrase.
- Check that backups finish, and that your iCloud or the app's cloud still has space.
- Export irreplaceable photos to an encrypted drive or a computer you control, as a second copy.
- Before switching phones, follow our new-iPhone checklist .
Noxium, which we make, was built around this problem. Its encrypted backup goes to your own iCloud on the free plan, and only encrypted data leaves the device. On a new iPhone you draw your pattern and the vault comes back. If you forget the pattern, the recovery phrase you wrote down at setup opens it. If Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up everything. What it doesn't protect: a vault deleted before any backup finished, or a lost pattern and a lost phrase together.
Noxium backs up only encrypted data, to your own iCloud, and restores with your pattern.
A backup that actually restores
Noxium backs up an encrypted copy of your vault to your own iCloud, free. New phone? Draw your pattern and everything comes back.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Is there a photo vault recovery app that works?
Not one that can open an encrypted vault. Recovery works by restoring a copy that already exists: the app's cloud, your iCloud, an old phone or a computer backup. Be wary of any tool that promises to unlock a vault, and ask the app's developer instead.
How do you recover deleted photos from a vault app?
Look in the app's trash or Recently Deleted area first, then in its cloud backup. If you deleted the whole app, only a backup can bring them back, because deleting an iPhone app removes its data.
Will reinstalling the vault app bring my photos back?
Only if the app restores them from a cloud backup. Reinstalling by itself gives you an empty vault. Contact the developer first, and offload rather than delete if you only need space.
Does an iCloud backup of my iPhone include my vault photos?
It depends on the app. Obscura says its vault is included when iCloud Backup is on, while Private Photo Vault says some customers have had trouble restoring vault data that way. Check the app's own settings or help pages.
Can the developer recover my vault photos?
Only from a backup they or you still have. Private Photo Vault, for example, says it can't restore deleted files without a usable backup. A developer that encrypts with your own key can't open your vault for you.
I see thumbnails but the photos won't open. Are they lost?
Not necessarily. The full-size files may still be syncing from the cloud. Keepsafe, for example, asks you to keep the app open with the screen on until syncing finishes. Stay on Wi-Fi and power, and check that your cloud storage isn't full.

- Apple Support: How to recover deleted photos . Where Recently Deleted is and the 30-day limit. Checked 28 November 2026.
- Private Photo Vault FAQ . Cloud Vault and computer-backup restores, and what happens after deleting the app. Checked 28 November 2026.
- Keepsafe Help Center: transfer photos to a new phone and recovering items from Trash . Checked 28 November 2026.

# Keepsafe alternatives that don't need an account

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/keepsafe-alternatives
Last updated: 2026-11-28

Guide · Alternatives
## Keepsafe alternatives that don't need an account
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
Vaultaire, Obscura, Encamera and Noxium (which we make) all work without an account or email address, unlike Keepsafe. Vaultaire, Obscura and Noxium each sell lifetime Pro for $39.99; Keepsafe Premium is $9.99 a month or $23.99 a year (US App Store, checked 28 November 2026). Apple's Hidden album is free and needs no extra account, but anyone who knows your iPhone passcode can open it.
The Keepsafe alternatives that need no account are Vaultaire, Obscura, Encamera and Noxium, which we make. None of them asks for an email address, and three of them sell a one-time Pro plan for $39.99 on the US App Store ( Vaultaire , Obscura , Noxium ; checked 28 November 2026). This guide is for iPhone users who want to leave Keepsafe's email sign-in and company cloud, and want to know what each option costs and gives up before they move their photos.
Only deciding between Vaultaire and Keepsafe? See Vaultaire vs Keepsafe , compared point by point.
### Why do people look for Keepsafe alternatives?
Usually because of the account, the cloud, the ads or the price. Keepsafe does a lot well, so start there.
What Keepsafe does well. It is one of the most used vaults on the iPhone, with about 387,000 US ratings averaging 4.7 ( App Store , checked 28 November 2026). Its help center says files are encrypted with 256-bit AES ( Keepsafe Help Center ). Premium adds a fake PIN that opens a decoy vault, intruder alerts and trash recovery ( Keepsafe Help Center ). And because you have an account, you can sign in on a new phone with a code sent to your email.
What people want to leave behind:
- An email account. Keepsafe sends an access code to your account email when you sign in on a new device. Its help center says that if you lose access to that email, the account and its contents can't be recovered ( Keepsafe Help Center ).
- Keepsafe's own cloud. The free plan backs up your first 200 items to Keepsafe's cloud. Premium raises that to 10,000 items, and the Lifetime plan to 100,000. Premium's Space Saver compresses photos on the phone and keeps the originals in that cloud.
- Ads. The listing says Keepsafe Basic, the free version, is ad supported. Premium removes the ads.
- Price. Premium is $9.99 a month or $23.99 a year on the US App Store.
- Tracking. Keepsafe's privacy label lists Usage Data under "Data Used to Track You".
None of that makes Keepsafe unsafe. It's a different model: the company holds your account and a copy of your vault.
### Which Keepsafe alternatives need no account?
Vaultaire, Obscura, Encamera and Noxium. Each says in its own App Store listing that it needs no account or email. Apple's Hidden album is built into iOS and needs no extra account.
Keepsafe and its no-account alternatives. Source: each app's US App Store page and Keepsafe's help center, checked 28 November 2026; Apple Support for the Hidden album.

### Is Vaultaire a good Keepsafe alternative?
Yes, if the account is what you want to leave behind. Vaultaire needs no account and backs up, encrypted, to your own iCloud, including on its free plan. Its privacy label lists no data used to track you, though it does link your email address and support messages to you if you contact the developer ( App Store ).
The trade-off: Vaultaire is new. It had 72 US ratings when we checked, against Keepsafe's 387,000 or so. Our Vaultaire review and Keepsafe review look at each app on its own.
Vaultaire vs Keepsafe
Price, encryption, backup and decoy vaults side by side: Vaultaire vs Keepsafe compared .
### Which Keepsafe alternative should you choose?
Pick by what mattered to you about leaving Keepsafe.
- No account, encrypted iCloud backup and a decoy on the free plan: Noxium or Vaultaire. Both open with a drawn pattern. Noxium's free plan holds 150 photos and 10 videos with 1 decoy vault. Vaultaire's holds 100 photos and 10 videos across up to 3 vaults. A decoy only helps if it looks lived in; see what a decoy vault is and its limits.
- Encryption code you can read: Obscura or Encamera. Obscura keeps the vault on the device, with no cloud of its own, and gives each vault a 24-word recovery key. Encamera can store albums on the device or in your own iCloud.
- Nothing to install: Apple's Hidden album. It's free and locked with Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode ( Apple Support ). Anyone who knows your passcode can open it. See is the Hidden album private?
What none of them protects. No vault, Noxium included, protects photos while they sit in your Photos library before you import them, or copies you have already sent to someone. A drawn pattern can be watched over your shoulder, like a PIN. And with no account, there is no email reset: if you forget your code, only the app's own recovery can get you back in. Noxium has you write down a recovery phrase at setup, and nobody, not us and not Apple, can reset a pattern. Our guide on forgotten vault passwords covers what to check before you trust any vault with years of photos.
### How do you switch from Keepsafe without losing photos?
Export from Keepsafe back to Photos, check everything arrived at full quality, move it into the new vault, and only then delete Keepsafe's copies.
- If you used Space Saver, the full-size originals live in Keepsafe's cloud, not on the phone. Make sure you export the originals, not the compressed copies: open a few photos and check they're full quality before you go on.
- Export from Keepsafe to your Photos library, album by album. Note how many items each album has.
- Check the export in Photos: counts match, videos play, Live Photos move.
- Import into the new vault, and let it delete the originals from Photos if it offers to. Then empty Recently Deleted in Photos.
- Check the new vault's backup has finished.
- Only then delete items from Keepsafe and cancel the subscription in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions .
Watch out
Exported photos sit unencrypted in your Photos library until the new vault imports them. Do the move in one sitting, on a phone only you are using.
Noxium has no sign-up and no account. The backup goes to your own iCloud.
No account. No email. No ads.
Noxium opens with a pattern only you know and backs up, encrypted, to your own iCloud. Free for 150 photos and 10 videos.

### Questions people ask
What is the best Keepsafe alternative?
It depends on why you're leaving. For no account plus encrypted iCloud backup and a decoy on the free plan, look at Noxium (ours) or Vaultaire. For encryption code you can read, look at Obscura or Encamera. For nothing to install, Apple's Hidden album.
Is there a Keepsafe alternative without an account?
Yes. Vaultaire, Obscura, Encamera and Noxium all say in their App Store listings that they need no account or email address. Keepsafe signs you in with an email address.
What is Keepsafe Cloud and how much does it hold?
It's Keepsafe's own encrypted backup, stored with Keepsafe and tied to your account. Its help center says the free plan backs up your first 200 items, Premium up to 10,000 and the Lifetime plan up to 100,000.
What are the alternatives to Vaultaire?
Noxium, which we make, works the most like it: no account, a drawn pattern, AES-256-GCM and an encrypted backup to your own iCloud. Obscura and Encamera also need no account. Our Vaultaire review compares it with Noxium point by point.
Can I move my photos from Keepsafe to another vault?
Yes. Export them from Keepsafe to Photos, check they arrived at full quality, import them into the new vault, and only then delete them from Keepsafe.
If a vault has no account, how do I recover it if I forget my code?
Only through the recovery the app gives you, such as a recovery phrase or key you keep yourself. With no account there is no email reset, so set up recovery before you need it.

# Vaultaire vs Keepsafe: which photo vault fits you?

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/vaultaire-vs-keepsafe
Last updated: 2026-11-28

Guide · Comparison
## Vaultaire vs Keepsafe: which photo vault fits you?
By Inertia Projects · Published 26 October 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
The main difference is who holds your photos. Vaultaire needs no account and backs up, encrypted, to your own iCloud, including on its free plan. Keepsafe signs you in with an email address and keeps its cloud copy on Keepsafe's own servers. On the US App Store (checked 28 November 2026), Vaultaire Pro is $19.99 a year or $39.99 once; Keepsafe Premium is $9.99 a month or $23.99 a year. Keepsafe is far better known, with about 387,000 ratings against Vaultaire's 72.
Choose Vaultaire if you want no account and an encrypted backup in your own iCloud. Choose Keepsafe if you want an email account to sign in with and don't mind a copy of your vault living on Keepsafe's servers. This comparison is for iPhone users picking between the two, or thinking of leaving Keepsafe, and it uses each app's US App Store page and its maker's own pages, checked 28 November 2026.
Keepsafe is one of the best-known vaults on the iPhone, with about 387,000 US ratings averaging 4.7 ( App Store ). Vaultaire, from Wraxle LLC, is new, with 72 ratings averaging 4.7 ( App Store ). Both hide photos and videos behind a lock, but they're built on different ideas about accounts and the cloud.
### How do Vaultaire and Keepsafe differ?
Vaultaire works without an account and keeps backups in your iCloud; Keepsafe works through an email account and its own cloud. Most other differences follow from that.
Vaultaire and Keepsafe side by side. Source: each app's US App Store page, vaultaire.app and the Keepsafe Help Center, checked 28 November 2026.
Vaultaire Keepsafe
Developer Wraxle LLC KeepSafe Software, Inc

For 17 vault apps in one table, see the full photo vault comparison .
### Do you need an account for Vaultaire or Keepsafe?
Vaultaire doesn't ask for one. Keepsafe does: you sign in with an email address.
Vaultaire's listing says "No account is required", and its website says no email, no phone number and no signup ( vaultaire.app ). Keepsafe sends an access code to your account email when you sign in on a new device. Its help center says that if you lose access to that email, the account and its contents can't be recovered, and suggests adding a second email address ( Keepsafe Help Center ).
So an account is not a full safety net either. With no account, nobody can reset your code for you, so check what a no-account vault offers if you forget your code. Our guide on forgotten vault passwords covers what to look for.
### Where do Vaultaire and Keepsafe back up your photos?
Vaultaire backs up to your own iCloud, encrypted, on both its free and Pro plans. Keepsafe backs up to its own cloud.
- Vaultaire: the listing says iCloud backup is on by default, and the vault is encrypted on the device before it goes to your private iCloud. Its website says you can turn the backup off. Syncing across several devices needs Pro.
- Keepsafe: the free plan backs up your first 200 items. Premium raises that to 10,000 and the Lifetime plan to 100,000 ( Keepsafe Help Center ). Premium's Space Saver compresses photos on the phone and keeps the originals in Keepsafe's cloud.
Watch out
If you use Keepsafe's Space Saver, the full-size originals are in Keepsafe's cloud, not on your phone. If you ever leave Keepsafe, export the originals, not the small copies.
### Which is cheaper, Vaultaire or Keepsafe?
Vaultaire, on every plan we could compare: $19.99 a year against Keepsafe's $23.99, and $5.99 a month against $9.99. Vaultaire also sells Pro Lifetime for $39.99.
Vaultaire's full US price list: Pro Weekly $1.99, Pro Monthly $5.99, Pro Annual $19.99, Pro Lifetime $39.99, and Family plans at $49.99 a year or $99.99 once ( App Store ). Keepsafe's listing shows Monthly Premium at $9.99 and Yearly Premium at $23.99, plus other Premium items from $4.99 to $35.99 that it doesn't label ( App Store ). Keepsafe's help center offers Monthly, Yearly and Lifetime plans but gives no prices.
Prices differ by country and change; check the App Store in your region before you buy. More apps with one-time prices are in vaults without subscriptions or ads .
### Which one is more secure?
Both say they encrypt your files. Vaultaire names AES-256-GCM in its listing; Keepsafe's help center says 256-bit AES, with all files encrypted at rest ( Keepsafe Help Center ).
Vaultaire's website goes further. It says AES-256-GCM covers file content, metadata and thumbnails, and that the key comes from your pattern through PBKDF2 ( vaultaire.app ). It also says plainly what that can't hide: a forensic examiner could still estimate how many vaults exist.
The bigger difference is where copies live. With Vaultaire, the copies are on your devices and in your iCloud. With Keepsafe, a copy also lives on Keepsafe's servers, tied to your account. For what the encryption terms mean, see how encrypted photo vaults work .
### Does Vaultaire or Keepsafe have a decoy vault?
Both do. In Vaultaire, a different pattern opens a different vault, and Pro adds a duress vault. In Keepsafe, Premium lets you create a fake PIN that opens a decoy vault ( Keepsafe Help Center ).
Vaultaire's duress pattern opens one chosen vault and removes the other vaults from the device. Keepsafe's decoy needs a paid plan; Vaultaire's separate vaults work on the free plan, which allows up to 3. A decoy only helps if it looks real. Our guide on what a decoy vault is explains how they work and their limits.
### Should you choose Vaultaire or Keepsafe?
Choose Vaultaire if you don't want an account or a company cloud. Choose Keepsafe if you want an email account to sign in with and a long track record, and don't mind its cloud or its ads on the free plan.
- Vaultaire fits if you want no account, an encrypted backup in your own iCloud, a decoy on the free plan, and a one-time price.
- Keepsafe fits if you want an email account and a backup that doesn't depend on your iCloud, and you're comfortable with Keepsafe storing your cloud copy and with its prices.
Moving from Keepsafe? Follow the steps in how to switch from Keepsafe without losing photos : export the originals, check them, import, and only then delete. Other no-account options are in our Keepsafe alternatives guide, and our Keepsafe review looks at Keepsafe on its own.
Is there another option like Vaultaire? Yes. Noxium photo vault, which we make, works the same way on the points above: no account, a drawn pattern, AES-256-GCM, and an encrypted backup to your own iCloud on the free plan. The differences: its keys come from your pattern through Argon2id, you write down a recovery phrase at setup, and its privacy label is Data Not Collected. Noxium's free plan holds 150 photos and 10 videos with 1 decoy vault. Pro is $2.99 a week, $17.99 a year or $39.99 once. It has the same limit as any vault: if you lose both your pattern and your recovery phrase, nobody can open it, not us and not Apple. For the full side-by-side, read our Vaultaire review, compared with Noxium .
No account. Your own iCloud.

### Questions people ask
Is Vaultaire better than Keepsafe?
It depends on what you want. Vaultaire needs no account, backs up to your own iCloud and costs less on the US App Store. Keepsafe gives you an email account to sign in with and a much longer track record, with its cloud copy on Keepsafe's servers.
Are Vaultaire's reviews good?
So far, yes, but there are few of them. On 28 November 2026 its US App Store page showed 72 ratings averaging 4.7, against about 387,000 for Keepsafe. Our Vaultaire review looks at what the app does from its listing and website.
Is vaultaire.app the official Vaultaire website?
It appears to be. The site names Wraxle LLC as the maker, the same developer as Vaultaire's App Store listing, and describes the same app: no account, a 5×5 pattern and encrypted iCloud backup.
Does Vaultaire need an account?
No. Vaultaire works without an account, email address or phone number. Its backups go to your own iCloud, encrypted.
Is Keepsafe free?
Keepsafe has a free, ad-supported plan that backs up your first 200 items to its cloud. Premium costs $9.99 a month or $23.99 a year on the US App Store, checked 28 November 2026.
Can I move my photos from Keepsafe to Vaultaire?
Yes. Export them from Keepsafe to your Photos library at full quality, import them into Vaultaire, check the backup has finished, and only then delete them from Keepsafe.

# How to lock photos on iPhone with Face ID, step by step

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/lock-photos-iphone-face-id
Last updated: 2026-11-28

Guide · Locking photos
## How to lock photos on iPhone with Face ID, a passcode or a pattern
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
Hide the photos: touch and hold a photo in Photos and tap Hide. Since iOS 16, the Hidden album is locked with Face ID by default; check that Settings › Apps › Photos › Use Face ID is on. You can also make the whole Photos app require Face ID, or put photos in a locked note. The Hidden album and the app lock also open with your iPhone passcode. For a lock that's separate from your passcode, use a locked note with its own password or a vault app.
To lock photos on iPhone with Face ID, hide them: in Photos, touch and hold a photo and tap Hide. Hidden photos go to the Hidden album, which has been locked with Face ID by default since iOS 16. This guide is for anyone who wants to put Face ID on their photo gallery, keep a few photos away from people who borrow their phone, or find a lock that's separate from their iPhone passcode.
There's no "lock this album" button in Photos. Instead, iPhone has locks at three levels: the Hidden album, the whole Photos app, and a single note. Each one is below, with what it actually stops and what it doesn't.
### How do you put Face ID on photos in the Photos app?
Hide the photos, then check that the Face ID switch for Photos is on. Apple's menu paths, checked 28 November 2026:
- Hide one photo: in Photos, touch and hold the photo, tap Hide , then confirm ( Apple Support ).
- Hide several: tap Select , tap the photos, tap the More (…) button, then Hide ( Apple Personal Safety User Guide ).
- Check the lock: open Settings › Apps › Photos and make sure Use Face ID is on. It's on by default in iOS 16 and later, and it locks both the Hidden and the Recently Deleted albums. If you turn it off, Apple says the Hidden album is unlocked too ( Apple Support ).
- Test it: in Photos, tap Collections , scroll to Utilities › Hidden , and tap View Album . It should ask for Face ID before showing anything.
- Optional: in Settings › Apps › Photos , turn off Show Hidden Album so the album doesn't appear under Utilities at all.
What it doesn't protect: Apple's Personal Safety guide says the Hidden album needs "Face ID, Touch ID, or a passcode" to unlock, so someone who knows your iPhone passcode can open it. With iCloud Photos on, photos you hide on one device are hidden on your other devices too ( Apple Support ), so check the lock on each one. Where the Hidden album is and what happens to it on iCloud: hidden photos on iPhone, the complete guide . Whether the lock is enough for you: is the Hidden album private?
### How do you lock the whole Photos app with Face ID?
Touch and hold the Photos icon and tap Require Face ID. Then Photos asks for Face ID every time it opens. Apple's steps ( Apple Personal Safety User Guide ):
- Touch and hold the Photos icon on the Home Screen until the quick actions menu opens.
- Tap Require Face ID (or Touch ID or Passcode).
- Tap Require Face ID again and authenticate.
This stops someone you've handed your unlocked phone from browsing your whole library. Apple says information from a locked app may also stay out of notification previews, search and Siri suggestions. What it doesn't protect: the passcode still opens the app, the lock applies only to that one device and doesn't sync through iCloud, and it's all or nothing, so you'll unlock your whole library many times a day.
#### Showing someone one photo: Guided Access
To hand over your phone with one photo on screen, use Guided Access. It keeps the phone in the app you're in ( Apple Support ).
- Turn it on once in Settings › Accessibility › Guided Access and set a Guided Access passcode.
- Open the photo, triple-click the side button, and tap Start . To stop swipes to other photos, circle the screen to disable it, or turn off Touch in the session settings.
- To end it, triple-click the side button, authenticate, and tap End .
### How do you lock photos with a separate password?
Put the photos in a note and lock it with a Notes password. It's the only built-in lock that can be separate from your iPhone passcode. Apple's steps ( Apple Support ):
- Set a Notes password: open Settings › Apps › Notes › Password , create a password only for Notes, and turn on Face ID if you want it as a shortcut. Since iOS 16, the other choice is to lock notes with your iPhone passcode.
- Add the photos to a note in Notes.
- Lock the note: open it, tap the More (…) button, then Lock .
- Delete the originals from Photos, then from Recently Deleted.
What it doesn't protect: Apple says notes with video, audio, PDFs or tags can't be locked, so this suits a handful of photos, not videos or a library. There are no albums. And if you forget a separate Notes password, resetting it doesn't give you access to the notes you already locked. If you want notes that open only with a vault code, see encrypted notes in Noxium , which we make.
### Can you lock one album, or use a pattern instead of Face ID?
Not in Photos. Only the Hidden and Recently Deleted albums have a lock, and iPhone's own locks use Face ID, Touch ID or a passcode. To lock an album of your choice, or to use a pattern, you need a vault app.
A lock is only as good as what's behind it. In some vault apps the code just opens a screen in front of ordinary files; in others it's used to make the encryption key. Ask how the app uses it before you trust it. We explain the difference in how encrypted photo vaults work .
In Noxium, which we make, you draw a pattern across at least 6 bolts on a 5×5 plate of 25 bolts. The pattern is never stored: keys come from it through Argon2id, and files are sealed on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM. Face ID can open the main vault. In Noxium Pro, an album can have its own pattern , and a second pattern can open a separate, harmless decoy vault (the free plan includes 1). What it doesn't protect: if you turn on Face ID for the main vault, your face opens it, and if you forget both your pattern and your recovery phrase, nobody can open the vault, not us and not Apple.
Noxium's lock: a pattern across a 5×5 plate of bolts, separate from your iPhone passcode.
Get Noxium free on the App Store →
### Which photo lock should you use?
Use the Hidden album lock to keep photos out of your library, Require Face ID when you hand your phone over, and a separate code when someone may know your passcode.

### Questions people ask
How do I put Face ID on my gallery on iPhone?
Hide the photos and check that Settings › Apps › Photos › Use Face ID is on: the Hidden album then asks for Face ID. To put Face ID on the whole gallery, touch and hold the Photos icon and tap Require Face ID .
Can someone open my Hidden album without Face ID?
Yes, if they know your iPhone passcode, because the lock accepts a passcode. If Use Face ID is off in Photos settings, the album doesn't ask at all.
Can I lock a specific album on iPhone?
No. Photos only locks the Hidden and Recently Deleted albums. To lock other photos, hide them, put them in a locked note, or use a vault app with album locks.
Can I lock photos with a different password than my iPhone passcode?
Yes, in two ways: a locked note with a separate Notes password, or a vault app with its own PIN, password or pattern.
Does locking the Photos app hide it?
No. Require Face ID only asks for Face ID when Photos opens. The app stays on your Home Screen.
Does hiding a photo encrypt it?
Not with a separate key. Hiding moves the photo to the Hidden album and puts Face ID or your passcode in front of it; Apple's Hidden album page describes no extra encryption. Vault apps that derive a key from your code work differently.
### Sources

- Apple Personal Safety User Guide, Hide photos and videos and Lock or hide apps on your iPhone : hiding several photos, the passcode fallback, Require Face ID and its limits. Checked 28 November 2026.
- Apple Support, How to lock or unlock notes on your iPhone or iPad : Notes password, which notes can't be locked, forgotten passwords. Checked 28 November 2026.

# What is a decoy vault, and how is it different from a duress code?

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/what-is-a-decoy-vault
Last updated: 2026-11-28

Guide · Decoy vaults
## What is a decoy vault, and does it actually protect you?
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
A decoy vault is a second, harmless vault inside a photo vault app that opens with a different PIN, password or pattern. If someone pressures you to open the app, you open the decoy, and they see ordinary photos instead of your private ones. A duress or emergency erase code goes further and erases your other vaults or locks you out of them, which can't be undone on that phone. Neither is a guarantee: a decoy works best when it's believable and nothing in the app reveals that a second vault exists.
A decoy vault is a second, harmless vault inside a photo vault app that opens with a different PIN, password or pattern. If someone makes you open the app, you open the decoy, and they see ordinary photos instead of your private ones. This guide is for anyone who might be pressured to unlock their vault, by a partner, a parent or anyone else, and wants to know how decoys, duress codes and emergency erase differ before choosing one.
Refusing to open a vault can make a tense moment worse. A decoy gives you a third option. A duress or erase code goes further and destroys data. Each one helps in a different situation, and each has limits.
### How does a decoy vault work?
The app accepts more than one code. Your real code opens your real vault. A second code opens a separate vault that you've filled with ordinary photos. To anyone watching, both look like you simply opened the app.
You'll also see it called a fake PIN, decoy password, fake vault, secondary passcode or decoy account. The idea is the same, but apps build it in two very different ways:
- A fake screen or fake gallery. The decoy code opens a different view in the same app, often with a settings menu that still shows the decoy option. Anyone who looks through settings, or knows the app, may see that a decoy exists.
- A separate encrypted vault. Each code unlocks its own vault with its own key. The app can't list the other vaults, because it can't read them without their codes.
The second kind is much harder to see through, because nothing inside the decoy points to anything else. Listings rarely say which kind they are, so you have to test it (see the steps below). For how vault encryption and keys work in general, see how photo vault apps work .
### What are a duress code and an emergency erase?
A duress code is a code you give when you're being forced to unlock something. It looks like a normal unlock but does something else. In photo vault apps, that something else usually means removing or erasing your other vaults, which is why apps also call it emergency erase, panic erase or an erase-all code.
- Emergency erase or duress vault. A separate code opens a harmless vault and, at the same moment, deletes your other vaults or removes access to them. Your photos can't be seen, but on that phone they're gone.
- Escape code or panic switch. These don't open a decoy or erase anything. An escape code makes the app look empty, and a panic switch jumps to another app or locks the vault, for example when you turn the phone face down. They help when someone glances at your screen, not when someone asks you to unlock. Some disguised vaults, such as Calculator#, add one; see calculator vault apps .
A decoy hides your vault; an erase code destroys it. Only set up an erase code if losing those photos is better than them being seen, and keep a copy you control somewhere else if you can't afford to lose them.
### How do decoy vaults, duress codes and panic switches differ?
The main difference is what happens to your real photos when you use the code.
What each feature does when you use it
Feature What the other person sees Your real photos Undo?
Decoy vault A vault of harmless photos Untouched, still on the phone Nothing to undo
Duress code or emergency erase A harmless vault Erased or locked away on that phone Only from a backup the app didn't erase
Escape code or panic switch An empty app, or another app Untouched Nothing to undo
A decoy is the safer first choice for most people: it costs nothing if you use it by mistake. An erase code is for the rarer case where being seen is worse than losing the photos. A panic switch suits a quick glance over your shoulder.
### What can't a decoy vault or duress code protect against?
A decoy buys you a calm moment; it doesn't make your real photos disappear. An erase code makes them disappear from the phone, but not from everywhere.
- A decoy has to be believable. An empty decoy, or one with three photos, invites more questions. Put real, boring photos in it and add a few now and then.
- It doesn't beat a determined expert. Storage use, backups or forensic tools may show there's more data than the decoy explains.
- Face ID can give it away in apps where Face ID opens your real vault while someone watches. Use the decoy code under pressure, not Face ID.
- Copies elsewhere aren't touched. Neither feature reaches photos still in the Photos app, Recently Deleted, iCloud Photos, chats or another phone. An erase code may also leave a cloud backup, depending on the app.
- Someone who watched you enter your real code, or found your recovery phrase, can still open your real vault later.
- It's not legal protection. Rules on unlocking devices, and on deleting data when asked, differ by country and situation. A decoy is a privacy tool, not advice on what you must or mustn't do.
If you're worried about someone who controls your phone or accounts, a vault is only one part of staying safe. Our guide to whether the iPhone Hidden album is private explains how hidden photos sync to your other devices.
### Which photo vault apps have a decoy vault or duress code?
This is what each app's US App Store description says, checked on 28 November 2026. App names link to the listing. We have full reviews of several of these in our comparison . A decoy matters less than the basics, so check those too: are photo vault apps safe?

"None named" means the listing doesn't mention one, not that the app can't do it. A listing also won't tell you whether its decoy is a fake screen or a separate vault, so test it before you rely on it.
### How do you set up and test a decoy vault?
Set it up as if you'll need it tomorrow, then open it as if you were the other person. It takes a few minutes and saves a bad moment later.
- Pick a code you won't mix up with your real one, but can recall under stress.
- Fill it with real, dull photos: food, a trip, screenshots, a pet. Dozens, not three.
- Open the decoy with its own code, starting from a locked app.
- Go through every screen , settings included. Anything that names another vault, counts more items than you can see, or offers to "switch vault" is a giveaway.
- Check the storage and backup screens. A total far larger than the decoy's contents invites questions.
- Check Face ID. If it opens the real vault, practise using the decoy code instead.
- Use it now and then and add a few photos, so the newest items aren't months old.
If you also want an erase code, read exactly what the app says it erases, including any cloud backup, before you set one up. Never test an erase code on a vault you care about.
In Noxium, which we make, a second pattern opens a separate, harmless vault, and the free plan includes 1. Keys come from your pattern through Argon2id, and the pattern is never stored. Face ID can open the main vault, so under pressure draw the decoy pattern instead. With Noxium Pro, emergency erase adds a third pattern that opens a harmless vault and erases the others. Like any decoy, Noxium's only works if it's believable, and it doesn't touch copies outside the app. Details are on the decoy vault feature page and the pattern lock page .
In Noxium, a second pattern opens a separate decoy vault.
A second pattern, a harmless vault
Noxium's decoy vault is a separate encrypted vault with its own pattern, included free. Face ID never opens it, and nothing in it points to your real one. See how Noxium's decoy vault works , and Pro's emergency erase pattern .

### Questions people ask
What is a decoy vault?
A second vault in a photo vault app that opens with a different code and holds harmless photos. If someone makes you open the app, you open the decoy instead of your real vault.
Is a decoy vault the same as a duress code?
No. A decoy only opens a harmless vault and leaves your real one alone. A duress or emergency erase code also deletes your other vaults or removes access to them, which you can't undo on that phone.
Can someone tell I'm using a decoy vault?
Possibly. Apps that show the decoy option in settings, or decoys with very few photos, are easy to spot. A decoy that's a separate encrypted vault, filled with ordinary photos, is much harder to see through.
Can you have more than one decoy vault?
In some apps. Most listings we checked describe a single decoy code or account. Noxium's free plan includes 1 decoy vault.
Does the iPhone Hidden album have a decoy?
No. Apple describes one Hidden album, locked by default and opened with Face ID or Touch ID on iPhone, with no second, harmless version.

# How to hide videos on iPhone, and keep them playable

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/how-to-hide-videos-on-iphone
Last updated: 2026-11-28

Guide · Hiding videos
## How to hide videos on iPhone, and keep them playable
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
To hide a video on iPhone, open Photos, touch and hold the video, tap Hide and confirm. It moves to the Hidden album, which needs Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode to open, and keeps playing as normal. A locked note can't hold videos. For videos that must stay private from someone who knows your passcode, use a vault app with its own code, and check that it keeps videos at full quality.
To hide a video on iPhone, open Photos, touch and hold the video, tap Hide and confirm. It moves to the Hidden album, keeps its quality, and plays as normal. This guide is for anyone hiding videos rather than photos, because videos bring their own problems: they're big, they fill iCloud, and one popular hiding trick, the locked note, doesn't work for them at all.
### How do you hide a video in the Photos app?
The same way as a photo: touch and hold, then Hide. Apple's steps cover photos and videos alike ( Apple: Hide photos with the Hidden album ).
- Open Photos and find the video.
- Touch and hold it , tap Hide , and confirm. For several, tap Select , choose them, tap More (…) and Hide .
- Leave the lock on. The Hidden album is locked by default on iOS 16 and later; its setting lives in Settings › Apps › Photos .
To find hidden videos later:
- Open Photos , tap Collections and scroll down to Utilities .
- Tap Hidden , then View Album , and unlock with Face ID or Touch ID.
- Can't see it? Turn on Settings › Apps › Photos › Show Hidden Album .
- To unhide a video, touch and hold it and tap Unhide .
What this doesn't protect: your iPhone passcode opens the Hidden album, and with iCloud Photos on, hidden videos are hidden, but present, on your other devices too. More on that in is the Hidden album private? For everything else about the album, including what happens on a new iPhone, see hidden photos on iPhone .
### Can you hide a video in a locked note?
No. Apple says you can't lock notes that contain video, audio, PDFs or tags ( Apple: Lock notes on iPhone ). A note with a video in it stays unlocked, so it hides nothing. Locked notes work only for photos, and only a handful; the guide to hiding photos covers that method.
### How do you hide videos in a vault app?
Import them from Photos into the vault, check they play, then delete the originals from Photos and Recently Deleted. Our guide to moving photos into a vault app walks through doing that without leaving copies. Before you trust a vault with videos, check four things:
- Does it keep full quality? Some vaults compress videos, or keep originals only in their own cloud. Look for "original quality" or similar in the listing
- Does it handle big files? 4K, HDR, slow-motion and long videos can be very large. Import one long video as a test before you move the rest.
- Do videos play without waiting? Some encrypted vaults decrypt the whole file before playing it, which takes time and space.
- Are videos in the free plan? Many free plans limit videos more than photos. Noxium's free plan, for example, holds 10 videos.
In Noxium, which we make, videos are encrypted on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM, behind a pattern that's separate from your passcode. Live Photos import as they are, videos export in full quality with their original dates, and the built-in camera records straight into the vault, so a clip never touches your camera roll. Vault content is hidden in the app switcher and during screen recording.
What Noxium doesn't protect: someone who watches you draw your pattern, someone who finds your recovery phrase, and copies of a video left in Photos, Recently Deleted or a chat app.
Photos and videos in a Noxium vault, encrypted on the iPhone.
Get Noxium free on the App Store →
### Why do videos cause trouble in vault apps?
Size, mostly. Anything a vault does to a video (import, encrypt, back up, restore) takes longer than with a photo, and has more chances to stop half-way.
- Imports stop when the app is closed mid-way or the phone runs low on space.
- Backups lag behind, especially when iCloud is nearly full, so the newest videos are the ones missing after a restore.
- Playback stalls when the app decrypts the whole file first.
- Formats get lost: Live Photos can lose their video part, and HDR can be flattened, if the app re-encodes.
After importing, play a few videos from the start, middle and end, and check one Live Photo still moves.
### What happens to hidden videos in backups and iCloud storage?
They're backed up like any other video, and they take the same space. Hiding doesn't take a video out of iCloud or shrink it.
- With iCloud Photos on, your photos and videos sync to iCloud, and hidden ones stay hidden on your other devices. Because they sync, they aren't part of your daily iCloud Backup ( Apple: What does iCloud back up? ).
- With iCloud Photos off, iCloud Backup may include the photos and videos in your library instead.
- With Optimize iPhone Storage on, the full-resolution video lives in iCloud and a smaller copy on the iPhone ( Apple: Manage your photo and video storage ). A vault needs the full video on the phone to import it, so let it download first.
- In a vault app, it depends on the app: some keep videos only on the phone, some upload to their own cloud, and some back up to your iCloud. Noxium sends only encrypted data to your own private iCloud; see encrypted iCloud backup .
Moving videos into a vault creates a second copy until you delete the originals, so check free space first in Settings › General › iPhone Storage . If the vault backs up to iCloud, those videos count against your iCloud space too; check it in Settings › [your name] › iCloud . Every Apple Account starts with 5 GB of free iCloud storage ( Apple ), which a few long videos can fill.
### What should you clean up after hiding videos?
- Recently Deleted: deleted originals can be recovered for 30 days ( Apple ). Open Collections › Utilities › Recently Deleted , unlock it, and delete them for good.
- Messages and chat apps: a video you sent or received has its own copy in that conversation.
- Shared albums and the Shared Library: in the iCloud Shared Photo Library, every participant can view or unhide a hidden item.
- Your computer: check old imports on a Mac or PC.
Big videos, played straight away
Noxium hides videos behind a pattern only you know, encrypted on your iPhone, and exports them in full quality with their original dates. Free for 10 videos and 150 photos.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Can you hide videos on iPhone without an app?
Yes. Touch and hold the video in Photos and tap Hide. It moves to the Hidden album, which opens with Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode.
Can someone see my hidden videos if they know my passcode?
Yes. The Hidden album's lock accepts your iPhone passcode. To keep videos private from someone who knows it, use a vault app with its own code.
Can I lock a note with a video in it?
No. Apple doesn't let you lock notes that contain video, audio, PDFs or tags. Use the Hidden album or a vault app for videos.
Do hidden videos lose quality?
Not in the Photos app; hiding doesn't change the file. Some vault apps compress videos or keep the original only in their cloud, so check before you move large videos into one.
Do hidden videos still use iCloud storage?
Yes. Hidden videos stay in iCloud Photos and use the same space, and videos in a vault that backs up to iCloud count against your iCloud storage too.

- Apple Support: Hide photos with the Hidden album . Steps to hide, find and unhide photos and videos. Checked 28 November 2026.
- Apple Support: Lock notes on iPhone or iPad . Notes with video can't be locked. Checked 28 November 2026.
- Apple Support: What does iCloud back up? . Photos and videos in iCloud Backup with iCloud Photos on or off. Checked 28 November 2026.
- Apple Support: Manage your photo and video storage . Optimize iPhone Storage, 5 GB free, storage settings. Checked 28 November 2026.
- Apple Support: If you're missing photos or videos . Recently Deleted keeps items for 30 days. Checked 28 November 2026.

Yes. Vaultaire, Obscura, Encamera and Noxium say they have no ads. Keepsafe's help center now names a Lifetime plan, but its free version shows ads. Apple's Hidden album is free.
Yes, several iPhone photo vaults let you pay once instead of subscribing. If you'll keep the app for more than about two years, usually yes. Divide the one-time price by the yearly price to see when it pays for itself.

### What do free photo vault plans include?
Free plans cap different things, and some leave out backup. From each app's listing or help pages:
- Noxium: 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, 1 decoy vault, and encrypted iCloud backup and restore.
- Vaultaire: up to 3 vaults, 100 photos and 10 videos in total, with encrypted iCloud backup on by default.
- Obscura: up to 50 photos and documents, with a free encrypted export of the whole vault.
- Keepsafe: the free version limits its private cloud to 200 items ( Keepsafe Help Center ), and shows ads.
- Private Photo Vault: its listing says the free version doesn't back up to its Cloud Vault.
- Apple's Hidden album: free and built into Photos, locked with Face ID, Touch ID or a passcode ( Apple Support ). It isn't a separate vault: anyone who knows your iPhone passcode can open it.
Check whether backup is in the free plan. Without it, a free user's photos may exist on one phone only, and losing that phone loses them. Our guide on moving a photo vault to a new iPhone covers what a backup has to do to survive a phone change.
### What happens to your photos if you stop paying?
Check this before anything else, because a vault holds your own photos. If a music subscription lapses, you lose songs you can stream elsewhere. If a vault limits access when you stop paying, your photos are on the other side of the paywall.
The good answer is: you keep full access to everything already in the vault, including export and backup, and only new imports or premium features stop. The bad answer is anything that limits viewing, exporting or restoring photos you already have. An App Store listing may not say, so check the app's help pages or ask the developer before you move a library in.
Noxium's rule, which we make: if Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up everything already in your vault. Only adding past the free limits and Pro features (unlimited items, emergency erase, iPhone and iPad sync, custom icons, album patterns, shared vaults) pause. What Noxium doesn't protect: photos still in your Photos library before you import them, and copies you've already sent. And nobody can reset a forgotten pattern, so keep the recovery phrase you write down at setup.
Noxium: no ads, no account, and your photos stay yours if Pro ends.

- Find the "stop paying" rule in the app or its support pages.
- Compare a year of subscription with the one-time price. If you'll use it for years, one-time usually wins.
- Check what one-time covers: cloud storage, updates and family members can be sold separately.
- Check the privacy label on the App Store page for "Data Used to Track You".
- Check the decoy if someone might make you open the app. See what a decoy vault is and what it can't do.

# Forgot your photo vault password? How to reset it, app by app

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/forgot-photo-vault-password
Last updated: 2026-11-28

Guide · Locked out
## Forgot your photo vault password or PIN? What you can still do
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
Don't delete or reinstall the app: that erases the vault. Then use the recovery your app was built with. Keepsafe, Private Photo Vault, PV, Calculator# and Gallery Vault reset through an email you set up; Vaultaire, Obscura and Noxium use a recovery phrase or key you saved; without either, nobody can open the vault without the code. Check the lock screen for a Forgot option, then your email and password manager, then contact the developer.
If you forgot your photo vault password, use the recovery your app was built with: an email reset, a recovery phrase or key you saved at setup, or in some apps nothing at all. Don't delete or reinstall the app while you try, because that erases the vault. This guide is for iPhone users locked out of a vault app, with steps for Private Photo Vault, Keepsafe, Gallery Vault and others, and short notes for Android vaults.
Getting locked out was one of the most common complaints when we read recent one- and two-star App Store reviews of eight vault apps in October 2026 ( more on our about page ). What you can do depends almost entirely on how your app was built, so start with what's safe to try.
### What should you not do when you forget a vault password?
- Don't delete or reinstall the app. Apple says deleting an app "removes the app and its related data" ( Apple Support ), and the vault is that data. See does deleting a vault app delete your photos?
- Don't guess wildly. Try a few likely codes, note what you tried, then stop and look for the app's own recovery.
- Don't pay an unlock service. No outside tool can open a properly encrypted vault without its key. If the vault isn't encrypted, the developer may be able to help you directly.
- Don't restore an old iPhone backup over your phone hoping for an older code. You could lose newer photos and data.
### What should you try first?
Work through these in order, and stop as soon as one works.
- Look for a "Forgot" option on the app's lock screen: forgot PIN, forgot password, use recovery phrase, or similar. Some apps show it only after wrong tries.
- Search your email for messages from the app: a recovery email, a setup confirmation, or a code. Search for the app's name and its developer's name.
- Check where you keep passwords: your password manager, your notes, or a paper note from setup.
- Check other devices. If the vault is also on your iPad, it might still be unlocked there.
- Try Face ID or Touch ID if you turned it on in the app.
- Contact the developer (App Store page › App Support). Give your app version and iPhone model. Never send them other passwords.
### How do you reset the password in each vault app?
Use your app's own method. This is from each maker's help pages or App Store listing, checked 28 November 2026; menus can change between versions. Full reviews are linked where we've written one.
#### Private Photo Vault
Recovery works only if you set a recovery email when you first used the app. Its FAQ gives these steps ( Private Photo Vault FAQ ):
- App password: enter a wrong password eight times in a row, then choose Yes when the recovery prompt appears.
- Album password: enter a wrong album password five times in a row, then choose Yes.
- Cloud Vault password: this one is separate, and the company says it can't recover it. Losing it means losing access to your Cloud Vault data.
The FAQ also warns not to uninstall the app to reset a password. More in our Private Photo Vault review .
#### Keepsafe
Keepsafe resets your PIN with a code sent to a verified email on your account ( Keepsafe Help Center ):
- Open Keepsafe and tap Forgot PIN in the top right corner.
- Find the access code in your email. Keepsafe says the email is delayed by 5 minutes.
- Enter the code in Keepsafe, tap Submit, and create a new PIN.
If you've lost access to that email for good, Keepsafe says the account can't be recovered ( Keepsafe Help Center ). More in our Keepsafe review .
#### Other iPhone vault apps
- PV (Secret Photo Album): set a recovery email in App Setting › Set Recovery Email ; it's used if you forget the passcode. Set it before you need it ( App Store ).
- Calculator#: the listing says you can retrieve a lost password through your registered email. Anyone with access to that email may be able to use it too ( App Store ).
- Privault: its version 4.0 notes (April 2022) list "passcode reset with email" ( App Store ).
- Hide it Pro: its US App Store page lists a "Password Reset" in-app purchase for $4.99 (checked 15 November 2026), without saying how it works. Ask the developer first. See our Hide it Pro review .
- Secret Photo Vault - Lock Photos: an optional question and answer for password resetting, if you added one ( App Store ).
- Vaultaire: a nine-word secret phrase made when you create the vault. Choose the recovery option on the unlock screen and enter the words in order, then set a new pattern. Vaultaire says support can't replace a lost pattern or phrase ( Vaultaire: secret phrase ).
- Obscura: every vault has a 24-word recovery key that lets you set a new password, and the developer keeps no copy of either ( App Store ).
- Noxium (which we make): you write down a recovery phrase at setup, and it opens your vault. Nobody can reset a pattern: not us, not Apple. If you lose both the pattern and the phrase, nobody can open the vault. How the recovery phrase works .
Noxium asks you to write down a recovery phrase at setup. It's the only spare key.
Get Noxium free on the App Store →
### Which kind of vault recovery is safest?
The one only you can use. Each kind trades convenience against who else could get in.
Ways vault apps let you back in after a forgotten code (from the makers' pages above, checked 28 November 2026)
Method Who else could use it Examples
Email reset Anyone with access to that email account Keepsafe, Private Photo Vault, PV, Calculator#, Privault, Gallery Vault
Security question Anyone who knows or can guess the answer Secret Photo Vault - Lock Photos
Paid reset Depends on how the developer checks it's you Hide it Pro
Recovery phrase or key you keep Only someone who finds your written phrase Vaultaire, Obscura, Noxium
No recovery Nobody, including you Private Photo Vault's Cloud Vault password
If an email can reset your code, your photos are only as private as that email account. A recovery phrase avoids that, but only if you write it down and keep it somewhere safe. For how a phrase opens an encrypted vault, see how encrypted photo vaults work . A security question is the weakest of these, because answers like a pet's name are often easy to find.
### What if your vault is on Android, like Gallery Vault?
The Android vaults people search for most reset through an email or an account. This site is about iPhone, so here are only the makers' own steps.
- Gallery Vault: its Google Play listing says to search your mailbox for "thinkyeah" and follow the latest mail from them. If there's none, fail to unlock twice, tap the Forgot button, then Resend Auth Email ( Google Play ). ThinkYeah's help center describes the same flow: tap Forgot? on the password page, verify the code, and reset ( ThinkYeah support ).
- Keepsafe on Android: tap the three-dot menu, then Reset PIN and Send code, and enter the code from your email ( Keepsafe Help Center ).
- Samsung Secure Folder: choose Forgot PIN, sign in with the Samsung account linked to Secure Folder, and set a new lock ( Samsung Support ).
- A Tecno Spark or another Android phone: if you installed Gallery Vault from Google Play, its steps above are the same on any brand. If the lock is built into the phone's own gallery, the reset comes from the phone maker, so check its support pages.
On iPhone, several unrelated apps are called Gallery Vault. Check the maker's name under the app's name on its App Store page, and use that maker's help pages.
### What if you forgot your iPhone passcode (Hidden album)?
Since iOS 16, Apple's Hidden album is locked by default and opens with Face ID or Touch ID ( Apple: Hidden album ). If Face ID still works, it still opens. If you changed your iPhone passcode in the last 72 hours, iOS 17 and later let you tap Forgot Passcode? on the lock screen, then Enter Previous Passcode. The phone needs to be online, signed in to your Apple Account, with Find My on ( Apple: use your old passcode ).
Otherwise, the way back is to erase the iPhone with a computer, which Apple says erases the data on it ( Apple: reset your iPhone and passcode ). Anything that was only on the phone, and not in iCloud or a backup, is lost.
### How do you avoid getting locked out next time?
- Save the code in a password manager, with a note of which app it's for.
- Set up recovery now, whatever your app offers, and test it once.
- Write a recovery phrase on paper and keep it somewhere safe, away from the phone.
- Keep a backup you understand, so a lockout isn't also a loss. See photo vault recovery for lost photos .
- Write down every code you use. A decoy vault means a second code to remember, and it's the one people forget.
Never locked out, never reset by anyone else
Noxium has you write down a recovery phrase at setup. It opens your vault if you forget your pattern, and nobody else, including us, can reset it.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
How do I reset a forgotten vault password?
Use the app's Forgot option on its lock screen. Most vaults then send a code to the recovery email you set up; others ask for a recovery phrase or key you saved. If you set up neither, contact the developer before you try anything else.
How do I unlock Private Photo Vault if I forgot the password?
Enter a wrong password eight times in a row and choose Yes at the recovery prompt. This works only if you set a recovery email when you first used the app. A forgotten Cloud Vault password can't be recovered.
How can I find out my vault password?
Usually only from where you saved it: a password manager, your notes, or your email. If you can't find it, use the app's reset or recovery option instead.
What if I forgot my Gallery Vault password?
On Android, search your email for "thinkyeah" and follow the latest reset mail. If there isn't one, fail to unlock twice, tap Forgot and then Resend Auth Email. On iPhone, check which company makes your Gallery Vault and follow its help pages.
How do I recover a forgotten vault password on Android, for example on a Tecno Spark?
Use the vault app's own reset, which is the same on any phone brand. For a lock built into the phone's gallery, follow the phone maker's support pages. Don't clear the app's data or uninstall it, because that can delete the hidden files.
Is there software that can unlock a photo vault?
Not for a properly encrypted vault. Treat any paid unlock tool or service with suspicion, and contact the app's developer instead.

# How encrypted photo vaults work, in plain English

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/how-encrypted-photo-vaults-work
Last updated: 2026-11-28

Guide · Encryption explained
## How encrypted photo vaults work, in plain English
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
An encrypted photo vault app scrambles each photo with a secret key, so the stored file is unreadable without it. Your PIN, password or pattern is turned into that key, or into a key that unlocks it, on your phone and slowly on purpose, so guessing is expensive. A vault that only shows a PIN screen in front of ordinary files is hiding photos, not encrypting them.
A photo vault app works by encrypting each photo with a secret key, so the file stored on your phone or in the cloud is unreadable without that key. Your code (a PIN, password or pattern) is what unlocks the key, so the code is what an attacker has to guess. This guide is for anyone who searched "how does a vault app work" or "best iPhone encryption app" and wants to read a vault's security claims and know what they mean, without the math.
Vault apps love the word "encrypted". On its own it tells you very little. The sections below explain what real encryption involves, what a few popular apps say about theirs, and what no encryption can protect.
### What's the difference between hiding and encrypting a photo?
Hiding puts a door in front of a normal photo. Encrypting turns the photo itself into unreadable data.
A vault that only hides stores your photos as ordinary image files inside the app, and shows a PIN screen before it displays them. Anyone who gets at those files another way (a computer backup, a forensic tool, a bug) sees the photos. An encrypting vault stores only scrambled data. Without the key, even a perfect copy of the files is useless. The iPhone's own Hidden album is the first kind: is the iPhone Hidden album private? explains why.
### How does a PIN or pattern become an encryption key?
Through a key derivation function: a recipe that turns your code into a key. Good ones are deliberately slow, and the best are also memory-hungry, so each guess costs real time and hardware.
A key is a long random number. AES, the cipher NIST standardised in FIPS 197, uses keys of 128, 192 or 256 bits ( NIST: AES ). A 256-bit key has 2 256 possible values, about 10 77 , so nobody guesses the key itself. Attackers go after the code that unlocks it instead.
That's why stretching matters. A 4-digit PIN has 10,000 possibilities. If each guess took a microsecond, a computer would try them all in a hundredth of a second. If each guess takes half a second, the same search takes about 83 minutes, and every extra character or bolt multiplies it.
- Argon2id is a "memory-hard" function: each guess needs a set amount of memory as well as time, which raises the cost of dedicated cracking hardware. Its standard, RFC 9106, makes Argon2id the variant every implementation must support, and gives 64 MiB of memory with 3 passes as its second recommended setting for devices with less memory ( RFC 9106 ).
- PBKDF2-style functions repeat a hash many times. They're slow, but need little memory. NIST's guidance on password-based key derivation is SP 800-132, which NIST said in 2023 it plans to revise ( NIST SP 800-132 ).
- A plain hash, or nothing, means guesses are nearly free.
A random "salt" is mixed in too, so the same code never produces the same key in two vaults. RFC 9106 says a 128-bit salt is enough for all applications. Noxium, which we make, derives its keys from your pattern through Argon2id, and the pattern is never stored. Our pattern lock page shows how many patterns the 5×5 plate allows.
### What do AES-256-GCM and "keys inside keys" mean?
AES-256-GCM is the cipher that scrambles the photos, in a mode that also detects tampering.
- AES is the standard cipher ( NIST FIPS 197 ).
- 256 is the key size in bits.
- GCM is a mode NIST calls "authenticated encryption" ( NIST SP 800-38D ). If the encrypted file is changed or damaged, decryption fails instead of producing a corrupted photo.
Marketing words like "military" or "bank" grade usually just mean AES. The questions that matter are what the key comes from, where it's kept, and whether the backup is encrypted too.
Good vaults also use keys inside keys, the same idea Apple uses for the iPhone's storage. In iOS Data Protection, every file has its own key, which is wrapped by a class key, which is protected by the device's hardware key and, for some classes, your passcode ( Apple Platform Security: Data Protection ). A vault does the same with your code:
- Your code is stretched into a wrapping key .
- The wrapping key unlocks a random vault key , stored only in encrypted form.
- The vault key unlocks the file keys that encrypt each photo, video and note.
Changing your code then only re-wraps the vault key, instead of re-encrypting every photo. A recovery phrase can be a second wrapping of the same vault key, so either the code or the phrase opens the vault. Noxium's layers are explained on our on-device encryption page.
### How does an encrypted backup stay private?
By encrypting on the phone before anything is uploaded, so the cloud only ever stores scrambled data. This is end-to-end encryption.
The test is simple: could the company reset your code by email and give you your photos back? If yes, it can reach the key, and so could anyone who gets into its systems or your email. If no, only you can decrypt the backup, which is also why losing both your code and your recovery phrase means losing access. If that's happened, see forgot your photo vault password .
Noxium encrypts everything on the device, including names, dates and places, and only encrypted data goes to your own private iCloud (CloudKit). Nobody can reset your pattern: not us, not Apple.
### Doesn't the iPhone already encrypt my photos?
Yes, with keys tied to your device and passcode. Once the iPhone is unlocked, anyone holding it can open Photos, so a vault adds a second lock with its own key.
- On the iPhone. iOS encrypts each file with its own key under Data Protection, with key management rooted in the Secure Enclave ( Apple Platform Security: Encryption overview ). That protects a lost, locked phone. It doesn't separate one app's photos from someone who knows your passcode.
- The Hidden album. It needs Face ID or your passcode to open, but it's the same passcode, and it syncs to your other devices. See how to lock photos on iPhone .
- iCloud Photos. With standard data protection, Apple holds the keys. With Advanced Data Protection on, iCloud Photos is end-to-end encrypted ( Apple: iCloud data security overview ).
A vault that encrypts with a key from its own code means your iPhone passcode alone doesn't open it.
### How can you tell if a vault app really encrypts?
Read what it names. There's no single best iPhone encryption app for everyone, but a trustworthy one tells you these things:
- The cipher and the key derivation (for example AES-256-GCM and Argon2id), not just "secure".
- That encryption happens on the device, before backup.
- Whether it can reset your code by email. If it can, it can reach your key.
- That its backup is encrypted with your key, not just "secure cloud".
- Ideally, published encryption code or an independent review.
Here's what a sample of popular vault apps say. We report their claims, not test results.
What each app's US App Store listing (and, for Keepsafe, its help center) says about encryption, checked 28 November 2026
App What it says about encryption
Vaultaire AES-256-GCM on the iPhone; a random file key unlocked by your pattern; backup encrypted before it goes to your iCloud
Obscura AES-256-GCM; 600,000 rounds of key derivation; a 24-word recovery key; encryption code is open source
Encamera Encrypts all media; code open for review; cipher not named in the listing
Keepsafe 256-bit AES, files encrypted at rest, encrypted backups (help center)
KYMS AES; key size and mode not named

SPV - Secret Photo Vault Not mentioned; PIN protection, stored on the device only
Hide it Pro Not mentioned
