"Not mentioned" doesn't prove an app doesn't encrypt; it means you can't tell from what the developer publishes. Published code helps, but it isn't an audit, it may cover only the encryption part, and you can't easily confirm the App Store build matches it. Noxium isn't open source; we publish what it uses on our on-device encryption page instead. For full app-by-app reviews, see the best photo vault apps for iPhone .
### What can encryption not protect against?
- Someone watching you enter your code, or making you enter it. A decoy vault helps with the second, not the first.
- An open vault. While it's unlocked on screen, the photos are visible. Good apps hide content in the app switcher; Noxium also hides it during screen recording.
- A short code. Slow key derivation helps, but a 4-digit PIN can still be tried exhaustively.
- Copies outside the vault, such as originals left in Photos, Messages or Recently Deleted.
In Noxium, your pattern is never stored. Keys come from it through Argon2id.
Encryption you can read about
Noxium names every piece: Argon2id for your pattern, AES-256-GCM for each file, and only encrypted data in your own iCloud. Free for 150 photos and 10 videos.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
How does a vault app work?
It stores your photos inside the app behind its own code. A good one also encrypts each photo with a key that only your code unlocks, so the stored files are unreadable without it.
What is the best encryption app for iPhone?
There's no single best one. Pick a vault that names its cipher (such as AES-256-GCM), encrypts on the device before backup, and can't reset your code by email. We compare apps in our vault app comparison .
Are photo vault apps encrypted?
Some are, some don't say. Of the 9 rival listings and help pages in our table, 2 name AES-256-GCM, 2 more name AES, and 2 don't mention encryption.
What is Argon2id?
A key derivation function that turns a password or pattern into a key, using a set amount of memory and time for each guess, so guessing codes is expensive. It's standardised in RFC 9106.
Can an encrypted vault be hacked?
The cipher itself isn't the weak point. Short codes, codes seen by someone else, and unencrypted copies left elsewhere are. Use a long code and remove originals after importing.

- RFC 9106: Argon2 . Argon2id as the main variant, its recommended settings and salt length. Checked 28 November 2026.
- Apple Platform Security: Data Protection . Per-file keys wrapped by class keys on iPhone. Checked 28 November 2026.

# Are photo vault apps safe? A 7-point checklist before you trust one

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/are-photo-vault-apps-safe
Last updated: 2026-11-28

Guide · Safety
## Are photo vault apps safe? What to check before you trust one
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
Some are. A safe photo vault encrypts photos on your iPhone with a key made from your own code, keeps an encrypted backup you can restore on a new phone, and doesn't track you. Many vaults only put a PIN screen in front of ordinary files, and of 19 vault and private photo apps we checked in November 2026, 10 report data used to track you. Check the 7 points below before you trust one.
A photo vault app is safe when it encrypts your photos on your iPhone with a key made from your own code, and lets you restore them on a new phone. Many vaults only put a PIN screen in front of ordinary files, and some track you, so "safe" depends on the app, not the category. This guide is for anyone deciding whether to trust a vault (Keepsafe or any other) with private photos, or wondering how the one they already use works.
"Is it safe?" really asks two things: can other people see my photos, and could I lose them? A good vault gets both right. Below is a 7-point checklist you can run on any vault, with Keepsafe as a worked example.
### How does a photo vault app work?
A vault app keeps photos inside its own storage, away from the Photos app, and asks for a code before it shows them. What matters is what happens to the files behind that code.
- A lock screen only. The app stores normal image files and shows a PIN screen first. The PIN guards the app's screens, not the files themselves.
- Real encryption with your key. The app turns each photo into scrambled data that can only be read with a key made from your code. Without the code, the files are useless, even to the developer.
Your iPhone already encrypts app files with Data Protection , and third-party apps get it automatically. For the strongest class, Apple says the key "is protected with a key derived from the user passcode or password and the device UID" ( Apple Platform Security ). That protects a lost or locked phone. It doesn't protect against someone who knows your iPhone passcode, or who picks up your phone while it's unlocked. A vault's own encryption adds a second key that isn't your iPhone passcode. For the longer version, see how photo vault apps work .
### What are the real risks of photo vault apps?
- No real encryption. If a vault only hides files behind a PIN screen, anyone who reaches those files another way can see them.
- Losing your photos. If a vault keeps photos only on the phone, a broken phone, a reinstall or a new iPhone can leave them stranded.
- Getting locked out. A forgotten code with no recovery option can mean losing everything.
- Someone else getting in. If the developer can reset your code by email, anyone who controls that email may be able to as well.
- Your data going elsewhere. Ad and analytics tools send activity data off your phone. Backups on the developer's servers can mean your photos leave your control.
- Paywalls around your own photos. Some apps limit access or export when you stop paying.
### What should you check before trusting a photo vault?
Run these 7 checks on the App Store page, the app's help pages and the app itself. Most take a minute each.
- Named encryption, done on the phone. Look for a specific scheme such as AES-256-GCM, and a statement that photos are encrypted on the device. GCM is a NIST-standard mode that encrypts and also lets the app detect if a file was changed ( NIST SP 800-38D calls it "authenticated encryption"). "Secure" and "military-grade" on their own tell you nothing.
- Where the key comes from. The safest answer is: from your code, through a slow key-derivation function, and never stored. NIST describes this approach for protecting stored data in SP 800-132 . If the key sits next to the files, or the developer holds it, someone other than you can open them.
- Account or not. Does the app need an email account? An account isn't bad in itself, but find out what it can do. If the account can reset your code, the security of your vault now depends on your email.
- A backup you can restore. Where does it go, is it encrypted with your key, is it on the free plan, and how do you restore on a new iPhone? Our new-iPhone checklist covers the restore.
- The privacy label. On the App Store page, scroll to App Privacy. "Data Used to Track You" means data from the app is combined with other companies' data for ads or shared with data brokers. For a vault, the best answer is "Data Not Collected". The labels are self-reported by developers ( Apple Support ), so treat them as a claim.
- Recovery that doesn't weaken privacy. A recovery phrase or key that only you keep is safer than an email reset the developer controls. No recovery at all is private but unforgiving.
- What it doesn't protect. A good vault says so. No vault protects photos that are still in Photos or Recently Deleted, copies in iCloud Photos or chats, someone who watches you enter your code, or a moment when someone makes you open the app. For that last one, read how decoy vaults and duress codes work .
Good signs and warning signs for each check
Check Good sign Warning sign
Encryption Named scheme, on the device Only "secure" or "military-grade"
Key Made from your code, never stored Developer holds it, or not explained
Account None needed, or it can't open the vault Email can reset your code
Backup Encrypted with your key, on the free plan Paid only, or one copy on one phone
Privacy label Data Not Collected Data Used to Track You
Recovery A phrase or key only you keep Developer reset, or nothing
Limits Says what it doesn't protect Claims to protect everything
### What do vault apps' privacy labels show?
Of 19 iPhone vault and private photo apps we recorded between 11 and 22 November 2026, 10 report "Data Used to Track You" on their US App Store page and 4 report "Data Not Collected". Each app links to its listing, so you can check the label yourself; developers can change it with any update.

A good label doesn't prove an app encrypts, and a tracking label doesn't mean someone can see your photos. It tells you whether usage data leaves your phone for ads. Encryption and keys are checks 1 and 2 above. For app-by-app details, see our comparison .
### Is Keepsafe photo vault safe?
Keepsafe says it encrypts your files, and it's one of the most used vaults, but it relies on an email account and the free version tracks you for ads. On its US App Store page , checked 14 November 2026, it has a 4.7 rating from 386,264 ratings. Here's how it does on the checklist, from its own pages, checked 28 November 2026:
- Encryption: its help center says files are protected with "256-bit AES encryption", that "all files are encrypted at rest", and that unlocking with your Keepsafe PIN is the only way to decrypt them ( Keepsafe Support ). It doesn't name the mode or say where the key comes from.
- Account and recovery: signing in uses an access code sent to your account email, and a forgotten PIN is reset the same way. That's convenient, but your email account becomes a way into the vault.
- Backup: the listing includes photo backup, and Premium adds Private Cloud for up to 10,000 items.
- Privacy label: "Data Used to Track You" (usage data), and the listing says Keepsafe Basic is ad supported.
So Keepsafe is a reasonable choice if you want a well-known app with cloud backup and email recovery, and you're comfortable with ads and an account. If you'd rather have no account, see Keepsafe alternatives .
### How do you use a photo vault more safely?
- Use a long code, and don't reuse your iPhone passcode.
- Save your recovery phrase or key on paper, somewhere safe and away from the phone.
- Remove originals from Photos and Recently Deleted after importing, and check whether iCloud Photos still has a copy.
- Test the backup before you need it, especially before changing phones.
- Keep a second copy of anything irreplaceable, somewhere you control.
Noxium, which we make, was built to pass this checklist. Photos are encrypted on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM (Apple CryptoKit), using keys that come from your pattern through Argon2id; the pattern is never stored. Names, dates and places are encrypted too. There's no account. The encrypted backup goes to your own private iCloud, on the free plan. A recovery phrase you write down at setup is the only way back in if you forget your pattern, and nobody can reset a pattern for you. If Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up. It doesn't protect photos you leave in Photos, and it can't help if someone sees you draw your pattern or finds your recovery phrase. It's also new: its US App Store page had no ratings yet when we checked on 20 November 2026, so judge it by the same checklist.
Noxium: no account, no ads, encrypted on your iPhone.

### Questions people ask
Is a photo vault safe?
It can be. A safe vault encrypts photos on your phone with a key made from your code, keeps a backup you can restore, and doesn't track you. A vault that only shows a PIN screen in front of normal files is much weaker. Run the 7 checks above before you trust one.
Is a photo vault secure against hackers?
A properly encrypted one is, as long as your code stays private. Weak vaults can leak photos through unencrypted files or a cloud account. With strong encryption, the weak points become your code, your recovery phrase and any email account that can reset the vault.
Is a vault app safe to keep on my phone?
Yes, if it passes the checklist. Having one installed tells people you have something private, so if someone might make you open it, set up a decoy vault and see how decoy vaults work .
Is Keepsafe photo vault safe?
Keepsafe says it encrypts files with 256-bit AES at rest, and it's widely used. The trade-offs are an email account that can reset your PIN, ads in the free version, and a privacy label that lists data used to track you.
How does a vault app work?
It keeps photos in its own storage, away from the Photos app, and asks for a code before showing them. Good vaults also encrypt each file with a key made from that code, so the files can't be read without it.
Can photo vault apps see my photos?
Not if the app encrypts on your phone with a key only you hold. If it keeps photos unencrypted, or stores them on its own servers with a key it controls, it could.

# Pattern lock: how Noxium opens with a shape, not a PIN

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/pattern-lock
Last updated: 2026-11-13

Feature
## Pattern lock: how Noxium opens with a shape, not a PIN
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 13 November 2026
Short answer
Noxium opens when you draw a pattern across at least 6 bolts on a 5×5 plate of 25 bolts. The pattern isn't a screen in front of your photos: it is turned into the key that decrypts them, and it is never stored. Face ID can open the main vault once you've set it up.
Most photo vault apps ask for a 4-digit PIN. That's 10,000 codes, and people pick birthdays and years. Noxium, the photo vault we make, uses a pattern on a larger grid instead. It is quick to draw with one thumb, hard to guess, and it is the only thing that can unlock your vault. This page explains how the pattern lock works, how to pick a strong one, and what it can't do.
### How does the pattern lock work?
Your pattern is turned into an encryption key on the iPhone, and that key unlocks the vault. Nothing compares your pattern to a saved copy, because there is no saved copy.
- You draw. The plate has 25 bolts in 5 rows of 5. A pattern must touch at least 6 of them. If your line passes straight over a bolt you haven't used yet, that bolt is added for you, as on Android pattern locks.
- The pattern becomes a key. Noxium runs the pattern through Argon2id (from libsodium) with 64 MiB of memory and 3 passes. This is slow on purpose, so every guess costs time and memory.
- The key opens the vault key. Each vault has its own random key, sealed with the pattern key using AES-256-GCM. If the seal opens, you're in. If it doesn't, nothing opens and nothing is shown.
Because the check is "does this key open a vault?", one lock screen can serve several vaults. A decoy vault simply has its own pattern. Noxium tries every vault each time, so a wrong pattern looks the same however many vaults exist. For the cryptography in plain English, see how encrypted photo vaults work and our page on on-device encryption .
### How many patterns are there?
On Noxium's 5×5 plate there are 19,174,112 different patterns that touch exactly 6 bolts. We counted them with the same drawing rules the app uses. Longer patterns add far more:
Possible codes by lock type
Lock Possible codes
4-digit PIN 10,000
6-digit PIN 1,000,000
Android 3×3 pattern (4 to 9 dots) 389,112
Noxium 5×5, exactly 6 bolts 19,174,112
Noxium 5×5, exactly 7 bolts 261,248,096
Noxium 5×5, exactly 8 bolts 3,428,210,784
These are counts of what's possible, not what people choose. Studies of Android pattern locks found that most people draw short shapes that start in a corner and move left to right and top to bottom. A shape like that is guessed long before the big numbers matter. The count only protects you if your pattern isn't an obvious one.
### How do you pick a strong pattern?
Use more than 6 bolts, change direction, and avoid letters and simple shapes. A few rules of thumb:
- Go to 8 or more bolts. Each extra bolt multiplies the number of possible patterns by roughly 13.
- Don't start in a corner. The top-left corner is the most common start on any pattern lock.
- Cross your own line. Diagonals and knight-like jumps (two across, one down) are rarer than straight runs.
- Skip letters, initials and outlines. An L, a Z, a square or your initial are the first things someone tries.
- Make it different from your iPhone passcode and any decoy pattern. Noxium refuses a pattern that already opens another vault.
### How do you set it up?
You draw your pattern the first time you open Noxium, and you can change it any time from inside the vault.
- Draw your pattern. On Set your pattern , draw across at least 6 bolts. If you use fewer, Noxium tells you how many you drew.
- Draw it again. Step 2 of 2 asks for the same pattern. If the two don't match, you start over.
- Save your recovery phrase. Setup ends with a recovery phrase , the spare key if you forget your pattern.
- Change it later. Open the vault, tap Settings › Change pattern , and draw the new one. Only the vault key's seal changes; your photos aren't re-encrypted.
The lock screen: draw across at least 6 of the 25 bolts.
### How does Face ID fit in?
Face ID is a shortcut to the main vault, not a replacement for the pattern. When you turn it on in Settings › Lock , Noxium keeps the main vault's key in the iPhone's Keychain, locked to Face ID on this device only. It never syncs to iCloud. If someone adds a new face to your iPhone, the saved key stops working and you draw your pattern again. Decoy vaults never use Face ID: they open only with their own patterns. To lock other apps and the Photos app with Face ID, see how to lock photos on iPhone .
### What doesn't the pattern lock protect?
A pattern is only as private as the moment you draw it. Be honest with yourself about these limits:
- Someone watching. Patterns are easier to see over a shoulder than a PIN. Draw it with the screen angled away, or use Face ID in public.
- Smudges. A greasy screen can show the path of a pattern you draw often. Wipe the screen now and then.
- A short or obvious pattern. The 19 million figure means nothing if your pattern is a Z.
- Being forced to open it. No lock stops someone who makes you draw it. That's what a decoy vault is for.
- An unlocked phone left open. While the vault is open, anyone holding the phone can see it. Set Settings › Lock after leaving to Immediately.
Wrong guesses are slowed down too. After 5 wrong patterns Noxium waits 30 seconds before the next try, after 10 it waits 5 minutes, and after 15 it waits 30 minutes.
### Is it free or Pro?
The pattern lock is part of every Noxium vault, free and Pro. The free plan includes 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, 1 decoy vault, and full iCloud backup and restore. Noxium Pro adds unlimited items and album patterns , which put a separate pattern on a single album.
A lock that is also the key
Your pattern is never stored. It is stretched with Argon2id into the key that opens your vault.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Is a pattern lock safer than a PIN?
It can be. A 6-bolt pattern on Noxium's 5×5 plate has about 19 million possibilities, against 10,000 for a 4-digit PIN. But people pick predictable patterns, so a long, irregular pattern is what makes it safer.
Is my pattern stored on the phone?
No. Noxium keeps only the vault key sealed with a key made from your pattern. When you draw, it rebuilds that key and tries to open the seal.
What happens if I draw the wrong pattern?
Nothing opens. After 5 wrong tries Noxium makes you wait 30 seconds, then 5 minutes after 10, and 30 minutes after 15.
What if I forget my pattern?
Tap Forgot your pattern? on the lock screen and enter your recovery phrase. Nobody can reset a pattern: not us, not Apple. More in forgot your photo vault password .
Can I use the same pattern on a new iPhone?
Yes. On a new iPhone signed in to the same Apple Account, choose Restore your vault and draw the same pattern. Face ID has to be turned on again there.

# On-device encryption: what Noxium encrypts, and how

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/on-device-encryption
Last updated: 2026-11-13

Feature
## On-device encryption: what Noxium encrypts, and how
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 13 November 2026
Short answer
Noxium encrypts every photo, video and note on your iPhone before it is stored or backed up. Keys come from your pattern through Argon2id, and files are sealed with AES-256-GCM. Names, dates and places are encrypted too, and your pattern is never stored.
Many photo vault apps show a PIN screen in front of ordinary image files. If someone gets at those files another way, through a computer backup, a forensic tool or a bug, the photos are just there. An encrypted photo vault app stores only scrambled data, so a copy of the files is useless without your key. This page explains exactly what Noxium, the vault we make, encrypts on your iPhone, with which tools, and where the protection stops.
### How does Noxium's encryption work?
Noxium uses keys inside keys. Your pattern makes one key, that key opens a vault key, and the vault key opens a separate key for every file. Here is the chain, from your finger to a photo:
- Pattern key. When you draw your pattern , Argon2id (from libsodium) stretches it into a 256-bit key, using 64 MiB of memory and 3 passes and a random salt. The slowness is the point: each guess costs real time and memory.
- Vault key. Each vault has its own random 256-bit key. It is stored only sealed by the pattern key, with AES-256-GCM from Apple's CryptoKit.
- File keys. Every photo, video and note gets its own random key, sealed by the vault key. Thumbnails use a separate key derived from the file key.
- The file itself. Each file is encrypted with AES-256-GCM in 1 MiB chunks, each with its own authentication tag. A long video can play without decrypting the whole file first, and a changed or damaged chunk fails to open instead of showing corrupted data.
Changing your pattern only re-seals the vault key, so it takes a moment even with thousands of photos. Your recovery phrase is a second seal on the same vault key. For the ideas behind this, without math, read how encrypted photo vaults work .
### What exactly is encrypted?
Everything you put in a vault, plus the details about it. That matters, because a list of file names and dates can say a lot on its own.
What Noxium encrypts on the iPhone
Data Encrypted?
Photos, videos, Live Photos Yes, AES-256-GCM, one key per file
Thumbnails and previews Yes, with their own derived key
Names, dates and places Yes
Album names and notes Yes
Your pattern Never stored at all
The iCloud backup Yes, only already-encrypted data is uploaded
On disk, vault files carry random names and use iOS's strongest file protection class, so they are also locked by iOS while the iPhone is locked. They are left out of the iPhone's own backup on purpose; Noxium makes its own encrypted iCloud backup instead.
### What about photos added from the share sheet?
They are encrypted before Noxium's main app even opens. When you use Send to Noxium from another app, the share extension encrypts each file with a new key and seals that key to a public key. The extension never holds your vault key. The next time you unlock, Noxium opens the envelope and moves the file into your vault.
### How do you turn it on?
You don't need to. Encryption is always on, for every vault and every item, free or Pro.
- Set your pattern. The first time you open Noxium, draw a pattern across at least 6 bolts. This creates your first vault and its key.
- Add photos. Import from Photos, take them with the built-in camera, or use Send to Noxium . Each item is encrypted as it is added.
- Remove the originals. Copies left in the Photos app aren't protected. Turn on Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos (see import and export ) so Noxium offers to delete them after an import, then empty Collections › Utilities › Recently Deleted in Photos.
Encryption happens on the iPhone first. Only the encrypted result is backed up.
### What doesn't encryption protect?
Encryption protects files at rest. It can't protect a photo while you're looking at it, or a copy outside the vault.
- An open vault. While it is unlocked, anyone holding the phone sees what you see. Use Settings › Lock after leaving and Lock when face down .
- A weak pattern. Argon2id slows guessing, but a Z-shaped pattern is still guessed quickly.
- Copies elsewhere. Originals still in Photos or iCloud Photos, screenshots, and files you export are not encrypted by Noxium.
- A compromised iPhone. Spyware, or a jailbroken phone running hostile code, can see the screen while the vault is open.
- Being forced. If someone makes you draw your pattern, encryption doesn't help. A decoy vault does.
Vault content is hidden in the app switcher and during screen recording, which covers casual glances. It isn't a defense against spyware.
### Is it free or Pro?
Encryption is the same on every plan. The free plan holds 150 photos, 10 videos and unlimited notes, with full iCloud backup and restore. Noxium Pro adds unlimited items, emergency erase, iPhone and iPad sync, custom icons, album patterns and shared vaults. If Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up everything already in your vault.
Encryption you can read about
Argon2id for your pattern, AES-256-GCM for every file, and only ciphertext in your own iCloud.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Are photo vault apps on iPhone encrypted?
Some are, many aren't. Look for a named cipher such as AES-256, encryption on the device before backup, and no password reset by email. Our guide are photo vault apps safe? has a checklist.
Can the developer see my photos?
No. Noxium has no accounts and no servers that hold your photos. The keys come from your pattern on your iPhone, and the backup in your iCloud is already encrypted.
Isn't the iPhone already encrypted?
Yes, iOS encrypts the whole phone, but it unlocks with your iPhone passcode. Anyone who knows the passcode, or a backup made from the phone, can see your Photos library. Noxium adds a second lock with a key only your pattern makes.
What is AES-256-GCM?
AES with a 256-bit key is the standard cipher used across the industry. GCM adds a tag that detects any change to the encrypted data, so damaged or altered files don't open.
Does encryption make Noxium slow?
Unlocking takes a moment on purpose, because Argon2id is slow by design. Browsing is quick: thumbnails come first, and videos decrypt in 1 MiB chunks as they play.
Something wrong or out of date? Email business@inertiaprojects.info and we'll fix it.

- How encrypted vaults work

# Encrypted iCloud backup: your vault, in your iCloud, unreadable to anyone else

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/encrypted-icloud-backup
Last updated: 2026-11-13

Feature
## Encrypted iCloud backup: your vault, in your iCloud, unreadable to anyone else
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 13 November 2026
Short answer
Noxium backs up an encrypted copy of your vault to your own private iCloud (CloudKit). Only encrypted data leaves the iPhone, so Apple stores it but can't read it. On a new iPhone, draw your pattern and the vault restores. Backup and restore are included in the free plan.
A photo vault without a backup is one dropped phone away from losing everything. A backup that isn't encrypted defeats the point of a vault. Noxium, the vault we make, does both: it keeps its own backup in your iCloud, and everything in it is encrypted on your iPhone first. There is no Noxium account and no Noxium server in between. This page shows what is uploaded, how restoring works, and what the backup can't do.
### How does the encrypted backup work?
Noxium encrypts each item on the iPhone, then uploads only that encrypted data to the private CloudKit database in your iCloud. Apple's servers hold it, but the keys stay with your pattern.
- Encrypt first. Every photo, video, note and thumbnail is already encrypted with AES-256-GCM by the time it is stored (see on-device encryption ). The backup reuses that ciphertext.
- Upload to your iCloud. Each vault gets its own space in your private iCloud database. It holds the vault's sealed key, its encrypted details, and its encrypted items.
- Keep going while locked. Because the backup only handles encrypted data, uploads continue after you lock the vault.
- Restore with your pattern. On a new iPhone, your pattern rebuilds the key that opens the vault key in iCloud. Nothing else can.
The backup is separate from the iPhone's own iCloud Backup. Noxium deliberately leaves its vault files out of the device backup and Quick Start transfers, so private photos don't sit in an ordinary backup. Its own encrypted backup is what brings them back.
### What goes to iCloud, and what doesn't?
What Noxium uploads to your private iCloud
Data In iCloud?
Photos, videos, notes, thumbnails Yes, encrypted
Names, dates, places, album names Yes, encrypted
Each vault's key Only sealed by your pattern (and recovery phrase)
The salt and Argon2id settings Yes, so a new iPhone can rebuild your key
Your pattern or recovery phrase No, never
Face ID key No, it stays in this iPhone's Keychain
This holds with or without Apple's Advanced Data Protection. With standard iCloud protection, Apple can decrypt your iCloud Backup and iCloud Photos (Apple lists the categories in its iCloud data security overview ). Noxium's backup is different: Apple only ever receives data that is already encrypted with a key it doesn't have.
### How do you set it up and check it?
Turn it on during setup, then check it before you change phones.
- Turn it on. During setup, choose Back up to iCloud . Your iPhone must be signed in to iCloud. You can turn it on later in Settings › iCloud backup › Back up this vault .
- Check the status. Settings › iCloud backup shows when the vault was last backed up and how many items are waiting. Tap Back up now to start right away.
- Choose how videos upload. Wi-Fi only for videos is on by default, so large videos wait for Wi-Fi.
- Back up each vault. A decoy vault has its own backup switch. The status only counts the vault you're in, so it never reveals that other vaults exist.
- Watch your storage. The backup counts toward your iCloud storage. Used in iCloud shows how much. If iCloud is full, Noxium pauses and tells you about how much more space it needs.
Only encrypted data leaves the iPhone. It is stored in your private iCloud.
### How do you restore on a new iPhone?
Sign in to the same Apple Account, open Noxium, and draw your pattern. The full checklist is in how to move a photo vault to a new iPhone .
- Find the backup. On first launch, Noxium looks for a backup in your iCloud and shows Restore your vault .
- Draw your pattern. Draw the pattern you used on your old iPhone, or choose Restore with recovery phrase .
- Browse right away. Details and thumbnails arrive first. Choose whether full-size photos download Now or When I open them .
- Open the other vaults. Other vaults, such as a decoy, stay in iCloud until you draw their patterns. Later, use Settings › iCloud backup › Restore from iCloud .
Short on space? Free up space removes full-size copies that are already backed up. Previews stay, and the originals download again when you open them.
### What doesn't the backup protect?
- Forgetting both keys. If you lose your pattern and your recovery phrase , nobody can open the backup: not us, not Apple.
- Someone in your iCloud with time to guess. Your iCloud holds the sealed keys and the salt. A person who gets into your Apple Account could try patterns offline. Argon2id makes every guess slow, but a short or obvious pattern can still fall. Protect your Apple Account with a strong password and two-factor authentication.
- What Apple can see. Apple can see that Noxium stores data in your iCloud, and roughly how much. It can't see the photos or their details.
- Deleting the backup. The backup lives in your iCloud. If the Apple Account is lost or the data is deleted, the backup is gone too. Turning off Back up this vault stops new uploads; what's already in iCloud stays.
- Live sync. The backup restores a vault; keeping an iPhone and an iPad in step is a separate Pro feature.
### Is it free or Pro?
Full iCloud backup and restore is part of the free plan, which holds 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes and 1 decoy vault. Noxium Pro adds unlimited items and iPhone and iPad sync , among other things. If Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up everything already in your vault.
New phone? Everything comes back.
An encrypted backup goes to your own private iCloud. On a new iPhone, draw your pattern and your vault restores.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Do photo vault apps back up to iCloud?
Some do, some use their own cloud, and some keep photos only on the phone. Check the app's settings for a backup section before you rely on it. Noxium backs up to your own iCloud, encrypted.
Will my vault photos show up in iCloud Photos?
No. Noxium's backup sits in its own private CloudKit space, not in iCloud Photos, and it is encrypted. Nothing appears in the Photos app or on iCloud.com. Apple's Hidden album is a different case: see is the iPhone Hidden album private?
Does the backup use my iCloud storage?
Yes. It counts toward your iCloud plan. Settings › iCloud backup shows how much it uses, and Noxium tells you if iCloud is full.
Can I restore with a different Apple Account?
No. The backup lives in the iCloud of the Apple Account that made it, so the new iPhone must be signed in to that account.
Do I need Advanced Data Protection?
Not for Noxium's backup, which is encrypted before upload either way. Advanced Data Protection is still worth turning on for the rest of your iCloud, such as Photos and device backups.
Something wrong or out of date? Email business@inertiaprojects.info and we'll fix it.

# Recovery phrase: the spare key only you hold

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/recovery-phrase
Last updated: 2026-11-13

Feature
## Recovery phrase: the spare key only you hold
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 13 November 2026
Short answer
At setup, Noxium gives you a recovery phrase to write down. If you forget your pattern, the phrase opens your main vault, on this iPhone or a new one. Nobody can reset a pattern: not the developer, not Apple. So the phrase is the only spare key.
A vault that can be reset by email is a vault someone else can open. A vault with no way back punishes one bad day of memory. Noxium, the photo vault we make, sits in between: there is no reset, but there is a spare key that only you hold. This page explains how the recovery phrase works, how to make and store it, and what happens if you lose it.
### How does the recovery phrase work?
The phrase is a second way to make the key that opens your vault. Your pattern and your phrase each seal the same vault key, so either one opens it.
- A generated phrase is 8 words. Noxium picks them at random from the 2,048-word BIP-39 English list, the same list many crypto wallets use. That's 88 bits of randomness, far more than any pattern.
- It becomes a key the same way your pattern does. Argon2id (libsodium) stretches it, with 64 MiB of memory and 3 passes, into a key that seals your vault key with AES-256-GCM.
- It is never stored. Like your pattern , the phrase isn't kept anywhere by Noxium. Only the sealed vault key is, on your iPhone and in your encrypted iCloud backup .
- Case and spacing don't matter. "Author Tuition" and "author tuition" are read the same, so a phrase copied from paper still works.
Because the phrase opens the vault key itself, it works without the old phone, and without us. For how keys inside keys work, see how encrypted photo vaults work .
### How do you set it up?
The phrase is the last step of setup, and you can replace it any time.
- Get your phrase. On Recovery phrase , keep Generated to use 8 random words. Tap New phrase if you'd like different ones.
- Or choose your own. Tap Your own and type 6 to 9 words, at least 20 characters in all. A phrase you make up is easier to remember and easier to guess, so avoid song lyrics and quotes.
- Write it down on paper. Copy and Save to Files exist, but a copied phrase leaves the clipboard after 2 minutes and a saved file isn't encrypted.
- Pass the quick check. Tap I've saved it . For a generated phrase, Noxium asks for a word or two, such as "Which is word 3 of your phrase?", so you know your copy is right.
- Replace it later. Inside the vault, open Settings › Recovery phrase and tap Make a new recovery phrase or Choose my own phrase . The new phrase replaces the old one, which stops working.
Step 5 of setup: eight random words. Write them down on paper.
### How do you use it if you forget your pattern?
Tap Forgot your pattern? on the lock screen and type the phrase. It opens your main vault.
- On the same iPhone: on the lock screen, tap Forgot your pattern? , enter the phrase in Use your recovery phrase , and the main vault opens.
- Set a new pattern: once you're in, go to Settings › Change pattern .
- On a new iPhone: sign in to the same Apple Account, open Noxium, and on Restore your vault choose Restore with recovery phrase .
Locked out of a different app? Our guide on what to do if you forgot your photo vault password covers how other vaults handle it.
### Where should you keep it?
On paper, somewhere safe, away from the phone. Some practical choices:
- A place you'd keep a passport. A drawer or a document folder at home, not your wallet or phone case.
- A password manager, if you already use one well. It's encrypted and backed up. Don't put it in a plain note, an email to yourself, or a photo.
- Not inside the vault. The phrase is for when you can't get in.
- Never share it. Anyone with the phrase can open your main vault without your pattern.
### What doesn't the recovery phrase protect?
- Losing both. If you forget your pattern and lose the phrase, nobody can open the vault: not us, not Apple. That's the cost of a vault no one else can open.
- A phrase someone finds. A phrase on paper is only as safe as where you keep it. If you think someone saw it, make a new one.
- Other vaults. The phrase from setup opens your main vault only. A decoy vault opens with its own pattern, or with a phrase you make for it in that vault's Settings.
- A deleted app with no backup. The phrase opens a vault that still exists, on the phone or in iCloud. If the app is deleted and there's no backup, there's nothing left to open.
### Is it free or Pro?
The recovery phrase is part of every Noxium vault, free and Pro. The free plan includes 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, 1 decoy vault, and full iCloud backup and restore.
Never locked out, never reset by anyone else
You write down a recovery phrase at setup, and it opens your vault. Nobody can reset a pattern: not the developer, not Apple.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
What is a recovery phrase in a photo vault?
A set of words you save at setup that can open the vault if you forget your code. Unlike an email reset, only the person holding the words can use it.
Can I see my recovery phrase again later?
No. Noxium doesn't store it, so it can't show it again. If you've lost your copy, make a new one in Settings › Recovery phrase while you can still open the vault.
Does changing my pattern change the phrase?
No. The pattern and the phrase are two separate keys to the same vault. Changing one leaves the other working.
Is it the same as a crypto wallet seed phrase?
It uses the same BIP-39 word list, but it isn't a wallet seed and can't be used for one. Treat it with the same care.
Can Noxium's developer recover my vault?
No. We never have your pattern, your phrase or your keys. That's why the phrase matters.
Something wrong or out of date? Email business@inertiaprojects.info and we'll fix it.

- Pattern lock
- Encrypted iCloud backup
- On-device encryption
- All features

# Privault review: how it compares with Noxium in 2026

URL: https://getnoxium.app/compare/privault
Last updated: 2026-11-14

Compare
## Privault review: how it compares with Noxium in 2026
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 14 November 2026
Short answer
Privault is a popular, long-running vault with a keypad lock, a second passcode for a decoy folder and an erase-all passcode. Its App Store listing doesn't name a cipher or describe any backup, and the app hasn't been updated since 28 February 2025. Pick Privault for its media player and Wi-Fi transfer; pick Noxium if you want named encryption, an encrypted backup in your own iCloud and no data used to track you.
Privault, from Binspir Technologies, has been on the App Store since January 2017 and has 76,566 US ratings at 4.7 stars. It's one of the vaults people find first when they search for a private photo vault. This review looks at what Privault offers, using its App Store listing checked on 14 November 2026, and compares it point by point with Noxium. We make Noxium, so weigh what we say about it accordingly; everything about Privault below comes from Privault's own listing.
### Noxium vs Privault at a glance
Source: each app's US App Store listing, checked 14 November 2026. Noxium: our published facts.
Noxium Privault
Account needed No Not in listing
Opens with Pattern on a 5×5 plate; Face ID optional Digit passcode on a keypad
Encryption named AES-256-GCM, key from your pattern (Argon2id) Says storage is encrypted; cipher not named
Backup Your own iCloud, encrypted, free Not in listing; export to Camera Roll or over Wi-Fi
Decoy Yes, 1 free Secondary passcode opens a secondary folder
Panic erase Emergency erase pattern (Pro) Erase-all passcode
Forgot your code Recovery phrase you write down at setup Not in listing
Ads None Sells a "Remove ADs" purchase ($2.99)
Price (US) Free; Pro $2.99/week, $17.99/year or $39.99 once Free; Pro $3.49/month, $24.99/year or $45.99 permanent
Privacy label Data Not Collected Data Used to Track You; Data Linked to You; Data Not Linked to You
Last update 13 November 2026 (version 1.1) 28 February 2025 (version 10.2)
Requires iOS 17 or later iOS 11 or later
For 17 vault apps side by side, see our photo vault comparison .
### What does Privault do well, and where does it fall short?
Privault does a lot with media and offers three passcodes for different situations. Its weak points are what the listing leaves out: the cipher, a backup, and recovery.
#### What Privault does well
- Three passcodes. The primary passcode opens your files. A secondary passcode opens a separate folder, which the listing suggests giving out if someone threatens you. An erase-all passcode deletes all hidden files when you decide you have to.
- Media support. The listing says its player handles about 150 video formats, including MKV, AVI and WMV, and its photo browser reads HEIC, TIFF and more.
- A built-in voice recorder for private audio notes, set up from the keypad.
- Wi-Fi transfer. An embedded Wi-Fi server lets you move files to and from a computer, as well as through the Camera Roll.
- A one-time price. Permanent Pro is $45.99, so you don't have to subscribe.
- Old devices. It runs on iOS 11 and later and supports iPad.
#### Where Privault falls short
- No named encryption. The listing says the "encrypted storage" opens with your passcode, but it doesn't say how files are encrypted or how the passcode becomes a key. A short digit passcode is also far easier to guess than a long one, unless the app slows guessing down.
- No backup described. The listing doesn't mention iCloud or any cloud backup. If the phone is lost or the app is deleted, assume the only copies were on that phone, unless you exported them.
- No recovery described. The listing doesn't say what happens if you forget the passcode.
- Tracking. Its privacy label lists data used to track you and data linked to you.
- Not recently updated. The last update was 28 February 2025, more than 20 months before we checked. That isn't proof of a problem, but long gaps between updates can matter for an app that holds private files.
### How are Privault and Noxium different?
The real differences are in what's documented: how files are encrypted, where the backup lives, and what happens when you forget your code.
#### Encryption
Noxium names every piece. Your pattern is turned into a key with Argon2id, and every photo, video and note is encrypted on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM, including names, dates and places. The pattern itself is never stored. Our page on on-device encryption lists every layer. Privault's listing says its storage is encrypted, and stops there. If encryption matters to you, ask any vault to name its cipher; how encrypted photo vaults work explains what to look for.
#### Backup and moving to a new phone
Noxium keeps an encrypted backup in your own private iCloud, on the free plan too. On a new iPhone you draw your pattern and the vault restores. Privault's listing describes no backup; it offers export to the Camera Roll and a Wi-Fi server for copying files to a computer. That works as a manual backup, but the copies leave the vault unencrypted.
#### Decoys and panic erase
Both apps have a second code for a harmless space. Privault's secondary passcode opens a secondary folder; Noxium's second pattern opens a separate decoy vault, and the free plan includes 1. Both also have a way to erase: Privault's erase-all passcode, and Noxium's emergency erase pattern (Pro), which opens a harmless vault and erases the others. Read what a decoy vault is before you rely on one.
#### Forgetting your code
Noxium has no reset, by design. At setup you write down a recovery phrase, and it opens your vault if you forget your pattern. Privault's listing doesn't describe recovery, so contact its developer (support@binspir.com) before you need it.
#### Price and privacy
Both are free to start, with a one-time option. Privault's Permanent Pro is $45.99; Noxium Pro is $39.99 once. Noxium has no ads, no accounts and no analytics, and its privacy label is Data Not Collected. Privault sells a $2.99 purchase to remove ads, and its label lists data used to track you.
### Which should you choose?
- Pick Privault if you need to play many video formats, move files over Wi-Fi to a computer, record private voice notes, or use an iPhone older than iOS 17.
- Pick Noxium if you want encryption that's named and documented, an encrypted backup in your own iCloud that restores with your pattern, a recovery phrase, and no ads or tracking.
### How do you switch from Privault without losing photos?
Export from Privault, check the copies, import them into the new vault, and only then delete anything. Privault's listing says you can export through the Camera Roll or its Wi-Fi server.
- Count what you have. Note how many photos and videos are in each Privault folder, including the secondary folder.
- Export to the Camera Roll from inside Privault, folder by folder. For large videos, the Wi-Fi server to a computer may be quicker.
- Check the copies in Photos: counts match, videos play, quality is full size.
- Import into Noxium. Turn on Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos so it offers to remove the copies from Photos after import. Then empty Recently Deleted in Photos.
- Check the backup in Settings › iCloud backup : nothing waiting.
- Only then delete files from Privault, and cancel any subscription in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions .
Watch out
Exported photos sit unencrypted in your Photos library until the new vault imports them. Do the move in one sitting, on a phone only you are using. More tips: moving a vault without losing photos .
Encryption you can read about
Noxium encrypts everything on your iPhone with AES-256-GCM and backs up only encrypted data to your own iCloud. Free for 150 photos and 10 videos.

Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.

Is Privault safe?
It hides files behind a passcode and says its storage is encrypted, but its listing doesn't name the cipher, describe a backup or explain recovery, and it was last updated on 28 February 2025. Our checklist in are photo vault apps safe? covers what to check.
Is Privault free?
Yes, to download. On the US App Store, Pro costs $3.49 a month, $24.99 a year or $45.99 once, and removing ads is a $2.99 purchase.
Does Privault back up to iCloud?
Its App Store listing doesn't mention iCloud or any cloud backup. It describes export to the Camera Roll and a Wi-Fi server for copying files to a computer.
What is Privault's secondary passcode?
A second passcode that opens a separate folder instead of your main files. The listing suggests giving it out if someone forces you to open the app.
What if I forget my Privault passcode?
The listing doesn't describe recovery. Don't delete the app, and contact the developer at support@binspir.com. Our guide to a forgotten vault password explains what's safe to try.

# Keepsafe review: how it compares with Noxium in 2026

URL: https://getnoxium.app/compare/keepsafe
Last updated: 2026-11-28

Compare
## Keepsafe review: how it compares with Noxium in 2026
By Inertia Projects · Published 14 November 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
Keepsafe is a mature, actively updated vault that encrypts files with 256-bit AES and syncs through an email account and its own Keepsafe cloud. The free plan shows ads and backs up your first 200 items; Premium adds a decoy vault (fake PIN) and backs up up to 10,000. Pick Keepsafe if you want email sign-in and Android; pick Noxium, which we make, if you want no account, a backup encrypted in your own iCloud and a one-time price.
Keepsafe is a safe, well-maintained photo vault if you're comfortable with two things: an email account you sign in with, and a copy of your vault in Keepsafe's own cloud. If you want neither, a vault with no account fits you better. This review is for iPhone users deciding whether to start with Keepsafe, stay on it, or leave it. It uses Keepsafe's US App Store page and its help center, checked 28 November 2026, and compares it with Noxium. We make Noxium, so weigh what we say about our own app accordingly.
Keepsafe has been around a long time and it shows: about 387,000 US ratings averaging 4.7, and version 13.36.0 out on 12 November 2026 ( App Store ). Already decided to leave? Our list of Keepsafe alternatives with no account compares four of them, and Vaultaire vs Keepsafe covers that pair point by point.
### Noxium vs Keepsafe at a glance

### What does Keepsafe do well, and where does it fall short?
Keepsafe is mature, well designed and works across platforms. Its trade-offs come from the account, the company cloud and the ads.
#### What Keepsafe does well
- It's actively maintained. Version 13.36.0 came out on 12 November 2026, and the app has a large, long-running user base ( App Store ).
- It works on Android too. The listing says your items sync to all your Keepsafe installations on any platform, and the help center gives export steps for both iOS and Android ( Keepsafe Help Center ). That's rare among vaults.
- Its encryption is named. The help center says all files are encrypted at rest with 256-bit AES and that backups are encrypted ( Keepsafe Help Center ).
- A decoy vault, now documented. With Premium, a fake PIN opens a second, separate gallery you can show someone instead of your real one ( Keepsafe Help Center ). Premium also adds intruder alerts and trash recovery ( Keepsafe Subscriptions ).
- A Lifetime plan. The help center lists Monthly, Yearly and Lifetime plans, and Lifetime backs up up to 100,000 items.
- Useful extras. Album Lock gives single albums their own PIN (Premium), and Space Saver keeps compressed copies on the phone and the originals in the cloud, which frees space on a full iPhone.
#### Where Keepsafe falls short
- The account is the only key to your cloud copy. Keepsafe signs you in by sending an access code to your verified email. Its help center says that if you permanently lose access to that email, the account and its contents can't be recovered, and it suggests adding a second email address ( Keepsafe Help Center ).
- Your backup lives with Keepsafe. It goes to "your own private Keepsafe cloud", not to your iCloud ( Keepsafe Help Center ). The help pages we read don't say who holds the encryption keys for that cloud copy.
- The free backup is small. Basic backs up your first 200 items. Items you move to the Trash still count toward that limit until you empty it.
- Ads and tracking on the free plan. The listing says Keepsafe Basic is ad supported, and its privacy label lists Usage Data under "Data Used to Track You".
- Unclear Lifetime price. The listing labels only Monthly Premium ($9.99) and Yearly Premium ($23.99). Its other Premium items run from $4.99 to $35.99 without saying which one is Lifetime, so check the purchase screen before you pay.
- Space Saver's catch. With it on, the full-size originals exist only in Keepsafe's cloud. Leaving later means getting the originals back first.
### How are Keepsafe and Noxium different?
The main difference is who holds your account and your backup. With Keepsafe, the company does. With Noxium, there is no account, and the backup sits in your own iCloud, encrypted with a key only your pattern makes.
#### What is Keepsafe Cloud, and how is it different from iCloud backup?
Keepsafe Cloud, also called Private Cloud, is Keepsafe's own backup. It mirrors the gallery on your phone, is tied to your Keepsafe account, and is turned on or off in Settings › Backup & Sync inside the app ( Keepsafe Help Center ). Keepsafe says that if your phone is lost or replaced, only the synced items come back. The limits are 200 items free, 10,000 with Premium and 100,000 with Lifetime.
Noxium backs up everything, free, to your own private iCloud, and only encrypted data leaves the phone. On a new iPhone you draw your pattern and the vault restores. See encrypted iCloud backup for what's uploaded and how restore works. What it doesn't protect: the backup opens only with your pattern or recovery phrase, so if you lose both, nobody can restore it, not us and not Apple.
Noxium encrypts on the iPhone, then backs up to your own iCloud.
#### Account and recovery
Keepsafe's email account gives you a way back in on a new phone, as long as you still have that email. Noxium has no account and no reset by anyone, including us or Apple. Instead, you write down a recovery phrase at setup, and it opens your vault if you forget your pattern. Lose both and nobody can open the vault, which is also why nobody else can. Our guide to forgotten vault passwords compares how each kind of vault handles this.
#### Encryption
Both say they use AES-256. Noxium names the whole chain: Argon2id turns your pattern into a key, every file is sealed with AES-256-GCM on the iPhone, and names, dates and places are encrypted too. Keepsafe's help center names 256-bit AES for files at rest and for backups. With Keepsafe, a copy of your files also lives on the company's servers, tied to your account.
#### Decoys and lock
Both now have a decoy. In Keepsafe, turn it on in Settings › Decoy Vault : switch the toggle on, confirm your real PIN, then create a decoy PIN ( Keepsafe Help Center ). It's a Premium feature. Noxium opens with a pattern across a 5×5 plate, and a second pattern opens a separate decoy vault, 1 on the free plan. A decoy only helps if it looks lived in; see what a decoy vault is and what it can't hide.
#### Price and privacy
Over a year, Keepsafe Premium is $23.99 on the US App Store. Noxium Pro is $17.99 a year, or $39.99 once ( our pricing ). Keepsafe has a Lifetime plan too, but its listing doesn't say which price it is. Noxium has no ads and no analytics, and its privacy label is Data Not Collected.
### Which should you choose?
Choose by whether you want an account and a company cloud.
- Pick Keepsafe if you use Android too, you want an email account to sign in with on a new phone, or you want Space Saver to free up phone storage. Keep a second email on the account.
- Pick Noxium if you don't want an account or a company cloud, you want your backup in your own iCloud, encrypted, and a decoy on the free plan.
- Not sure yet? Our guide are photo vault apps safe? has a checklist for any vault you're thinking about.
What no vault protects, Noxium and Keepsafe included: photos still sitting in your Photos library before you import them, copies you've already sent someone, and a code someone watched you enter.
### How do you switch from Keepsafe without losing photos?
Export from Keepsafe to your Photos library, check everything arrived at full quality, import it into the new vault, and only then delete Keepsafe's copies.
- Mind Space Saver. If you use it, the originals are in Keepsafe's cloud. Export a few photos first and check they're full size before you go on.
- Export album by album. Keepsafe's help center describes it: open an album, tap Select , choose the items, tap the send icon at the bottom left, and choose Export to Camera Roll ( Keepsafe Help Center ).
- Check the export in Photos: counts match, videos play, and a few photos open at full size. Exported photos return to the date they were taken, so look further back in your library.
- Import into Noxium with Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos turned on. Then empty Recently Deleted in Photos.
- Check Noxium's backup in Settings › iCloud backup .
- Only then delete items from Keepsafe and cancel Premium in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions .
Watch out
Exported photos sit unencrypted in your Photos library until the new vault imports them. Do the move in one sitting, on a phone only you are using.

### Questions people ask
Is Keepsafe Photo Vault safe?
Yes, for most people. It's a long-running, actively updated app, and its help center says files are encrypted at rest with 256-bit AES. The trade-offs are that your account and your cloud copy sit with Keepsafe, losing your email can lock you out for good, and the free plan shows ads. Our checklist: are photo vault apps safe?
What is Keepsafe Cloud?
It's Keepsafe's own encrypted backup, tied to your Keepsafe account and stored with Keepsafe, not in your iCloud. It holds 200 items on the free plan, 10,000 with Premium and 100,000 with Lifetime. Turn it on or off in Settings › Backup & Sync .
Does Keepsafe have a fake PIN or decoy vault?
Yes, with Premium. Keepsafe calls it Decoy Vault: a second PIN opens a separate gallery. Turn it on in Settings › Decoy Vault .
Is Keepsafe free, and is there a lifetime plan?
It has a free, ad-supported plan that backs up your first 200 items. Premium costs $9.99 a month or $23.99 a year on the US App Store, checked 28 November 2026. The help center also lists a Lifetime plan, but the listing doesn't say which price it is.
What is a good Keepsafe alternative?
If the account is what bothers you, pick a vault that needs none and backs up to your own iCloud, such as Vaultaire or Noxium, which we make. Our Keepsafe alternatives guide compares the options and their prices.
How do I get my photos out of Keepsafe?
Open an album, tap Select, pick the items, tap the send icon and choose Export to Camera Roll. If you use Space Saver, check that the exported photos are full size.

# Private Photo Vault review: how it compares with Noxium

URL: https://getnoxium.app/compare/private-photo-vault
Last updated: 2026-11-28

Compare
## Private Photo Vault review: how it compares with Noxium
By Inertia Projects · Published 14 November 2026 · Last updated 28 November 2026
Short answer
Private Photo Vault (Pic Safe) is the most-reviewed vault on the US App Store, with about a million ratings, a break-in report, a decoy password and a private browser. If you forget its password, a recovery email you set up earlier is the way back in. Its encrypted Cloud Vault backup needs Premium and an account; the free version doesn't back up. Pick it for its features and track record; pick Noxium, which we make, for a free encrypted backup in your own iCloud and no data used to track you.
Private Photo Vault is a capable, long-running vault with more features than most, but its free version has no backup, and its privacy label lists data used to track you. If you want a free encrypted backup and no tracking, look elsewhere; if you want a break-in report, a private browser and a long track record, it's a strong pick. This review is for iPhone users who use Private Photo Vault, are locked out of it, or are deciding whether to start with it.
The app, also listed as Pic Safe, comes from Legendary Software Labs LLC and has about a million US ratings averaging 4.8 ( App Store ). This review uses its App Store page and its own website, privatephotovault.com, checked 28 November 2026, and compares it with Noxium. We make Noxium, so weigh what we say about our own app accordingly.
### Noxium vs Private Photo Vault at a glance
The biggest gaps are the backup, the account and the privacy label.
Source: Private Photo Vault's US App Store page and privatephotovault.com, checked 28 November 2026. Noxium: our published facts.
Noxium Private Photo Vault
Account needed No Not for the vault on the phone; Cloud Vault needs an account
Opens with Pattern on a 5×5 plate; Face ID optional PIN, pattern (dot) lock or password
Encryption named AES-256-GCM on the device, key from your pattern (Argon2id) AES-256 (website FAQ); Cloud Vault adds a key from your Cloud Vault Password

For more vault apps in one table, see the full photo vault comparison .
### What does Private Photo Vault do well, and where does it fall short?
It has more features than almost any vault and a long track record. Its gaps are in what's free, in the account its backup needs, and in what it tracks.
#### What Private Photo Vault does well
- Track record. Still updated (version 30.1 came out in late November 2026), and rated 4.8 by about a million people.
- Choice of lock. A PIN, a pattern (dot) lock or a password, plus separate passwords for individual albums.
- Break-in report. The listing describes a photo plus the GPS location of break-in attempts. Noxium doesn't have this.
- Decoy password and face-down lock , for when someone grabs the phone or makes you open it.
- A Cloud Vault the company can't read. Its website says Cloud Vault encrypts files on your device, with a key made from your Cloud Vault Password, before uploading them, and that the password is never uploaded to its servers ( privatephotovault.com ).
- A way back in. If you set up a recovery email when you first used the app, it can recover your app or album password ( Private Photo Vault FAQ ).
- Extras : a private web browser that saves straight to the vault, wireless photo transfer, and apps for iPad, Mac and Apple Vision.
#### Where Private Photo Vault falls short
- No backup on the free version. The listing says the free version doesn't back up your files to Cloud Vault. Lose the phone and the vault goes with it.
- The backup needs Premium and an account. Its website says Cloud Vault "requires Premium, an account and internet". And if Premium expires and you choose Switch to Basic, the FAQ says your Cloud Backup will be deleted.
- Its own cloud, not yours. Cloud Vault backups live with the developer, protected by your Cloud Vault Password. Forget that password and the listing says you can't view your Cloud Vault data; nobody can recover it for you.
- No recovery email, no recovery. The FAQ says that without a recovery email, a forgotten app or album password can't be recovered through its process.
- Tracking and ads. Its privacy label lists Usage Data under "Data Used to Track You", including for third-party advertising, and the listing says the app contains ads.
- Unclear pricing. The listing shows Premium items at $6.99, $12.99, $35.99 and $39.99 without saying which is monthly, yearly or lifetime.
### How are Private Photo Vault and Noxium different?
The biggest difference is the backup: Noxium's is free and goes to your own iCloud, while Private Photo Vault's needs Premium and an account and goes to its own cloud. After that, it's how you get back in when you forget your code, and what each app tracks.
#### How do you unlock Private Photo Vault if you forgot the password?
With the recovery email, if you set one up. Its FAQ gives the steps ( Private Photo Vault FAQ ):
- App password: enter it wrong 8 times in a row, then choose Yes when the recovery prompt appears.
- Album password: enter it wrong 5 times in a row, then choose Yes at the prompt.
- Don't delete the app to reset the password. The FAQ warns that files stored only in the app can be lost.
Without a recovery email, the FAQ says those passwords can't be recovered this way. The Cloud Vault Password is separate, and nothing recovers it: not support, not your app passcode, not your recovery email. If you're stuck, contact the developer through its support page before you try anything else. Our guide to forgotten vault passwords covers what to check for other apps.
Noxium works differently. There's no email and no reset by anyone, including us or Apple. You write down a recovery phrase at setup, and it opens your vault. Lose both your pattern and the phrase and nobody can open the vault, which is also why nobody else can.
#### Backup and restore
Noxium backs up everything to your own private iCloud on the free plan, and only encrypted data leaves the phone. On a new iPhone you draw your pattern and the vault restores; see encrypted iCloud backup . If Noxium Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up everything already in your vault. Private Photo Vault's Cloud Vault also encrypts with a secret only you know, which is good, but it needs Premium and an account, lives on the developer's servers, and is deleted if you switch to Basic.
Noxium backs up only encrypted data, to your own iCloud, and restores with your pattern.
#### Encryption on the phone
Both name AES-256. Noxium encrypts every photo, video and note on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM, with a key made from your pattern through Argon2id. Names, dates and places are encrypted too, and the pattern is never stored. Private Photo Vault's FAQ says it uses AES-256 to protect your data, but the pages we read don't say how the key is made from your PIN. Our page on on-device encryption explains why that part matters.
#### Locks, decoys and alerts
Both offer a decoy. Private Photo Vault adds a break-in report, a face-down lock and per-album passwords. Noxium adds album patterns (Pro) and an emergency erase pattern (Pro), which opens a harmless vault and erases the others. A decoy only helps if it looks real; see what a decoy vault is .
#### Price and privacy
Noxium Pro is $2.99 a week, $17.99 a year or $39.99 once ( our pricing ), and the free plan includes 150 photos, 10 videos and full backup. Noxium has no ads, no accounts and no analytics; its privacy label is Data Not Collected.
### Which should you choose?
Choose by what matters more: features or a free backup with no tracking.
- Pick Private Photo Vault if you want a break-in report, a private browser, a Mac app, a long track record, or an iPhone on iOS 15 or 16. Set up a recovery email on day one.
- Pick Noxium if you want a free encrypted backup in your own iCloud, encryption that's named and documented end to end, a recovery phrase instead of an email, and no data used to track you.
What neither protects: photos still in your Photos library before you import them, copies you've already sent, and a code someone watched you enter.
### How do you switch from Private Photo Vault without losing photos?
Export to the Photos app, check the copies, import them into the new vault, and only then delete anything. Private Photo Vault's listing says it can import from and export to the Photos app.
- Count what you have in each album, including any album with its own password and the decoy.
- Get the originals onto the phone. If you use Cloud Vault with Space Saver, the originals are in Cloud Vault. Make sure the full-size files are on the phone before you export, and do it before Premium ends.
- Export each album to Photos from inside Private Photo Vault.
- Check the copies in Photos: counts match, videos play, photos are full size.
- Import into Noxium. With Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos on, it offers to remove the copies from Photos. Then empty Recently Deleted .
- Check the backup in Noxium's Settings › iCloud backup , and only then delete from Private Photo Vault and cancel Premium in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions .
Watch out
Photos you export are unencrypted in your library until the new vault imports them. Move them in one sitting, on a phone only you are using. More on this in moving a vault without losing photos .
Backup included. In your own iCloud.
Noxium backs up an encrypted copy of your vault to your own iCloud, on the free plan. On a new iPhone, draw your pattern and it restores.

Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
How do I unlock Private Photo Vault if I forgot my password?
Use the recovery email, if you set one up. Enter the app password wrong 8 times in a row (5 for an album) and choose Yes at the recovery prompt. Without a recovery email, its FAQ says the password can't be recovered this way. Don't delete the app to reset it.
What happens if I forget my Cloud Vault Password?
You can't view your Cloud Vault data. The password is never uploaded to its servers, and its website says neither support, your app passcode nor your recovery email can recover it. Write it down somewhere safe.
Does Private Photo Vault back up my photos?
Only with Premium. The free version doesn't back up to Cloud Vault, and Cloud Vault needs an account. If Premium ends and you switch to Basic, its FAQ says the cloud backup is deleted.

It's a long-running, actively updated app that says it uses AES-256, with a Cloud Vault the company says it can't read. The free version has no backup, and its privacy label lists data used to track you. See are photo vault apps safe?
Is Private Photo Vault the same as Keepsafe?
No. They're different apps from different companies. Keepsafe signs you in with an email account; our Keepsafe review compares it with Noxium.
