Opens with Pattern across at least 6 of 25 bolts (5×5); Face ID optional Pattern across at least 6 of 25 dots (5×5), with at least one turn
File encryption AES-256-GCM AES-256-GCM
Pattern to key Argon2id (libsodium); pattern never stored PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 600,000 iterations; pattern kept in an encrypted recovery database in the Keychain
Backup Your own iCloud, encrypted, free Your own iCloud, encrypted, Free and Pro; on by default, can be turned off
Free plan 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, 1 decoy vault Up to 3 vaults, 100 photos and 10 videos in total
Panic option (Pro) Emergency erase: a third pattern opens a harmless vault and erases the others Duress vault: opens one vault and removes the others from the device
Recovery Recovery phrase you write down at setup 9-word sentence, viewable later in the vault's settings
Price (US) Pro $2.99 a week, $17.99 a year or $39.99 once Pro $1.99 a week, $5.99 a month, $19.99 a year or $39.99 lifetime; Family $49.99 a year or $99.99 lifetime
Privacy label Data Not Collected Data Linked to You: email address, support messages. Data Not Linked to You: usage and diagnostics. None used to track you
### What does Vaultaire do well, and where does it fall short?
Vaultaire gets the important things right: real encryption on the device, no account, a free encrypted backup and decoys. Its trade-offs are a smaller free plan, a key derivation that needs little memory, a recovery sentence you can view again, and some data collection.
#### What Vaultaire does well
- Encryption it explains. The listing names AES-256-GCM, and its website describes how the pattern becomes a key, that a random master key encrypts file headers, content, thumbnails and metadata, and how backups are sealed before CloudKit receives them ( vaultaire.app ). Few vaults publish this much.
- It says what it can't hide. Its website warns that an examiner with a copy of the app's files can still estimate how many vaults you have ( vaultaire.app ). That kind of honesty is rare.
- No account, no ads, no tracking. The listing says "No account is required" and "No ads or cross-app tracking", and its privacy label lists no data used to track you.
- Free backup. Encrypted iCloud backup is included on the free plan and turned on by default.
- 3 vaults on the free plan , so a decoy plus two more without paying.
- Family plans. Pro for your Apple family, at $49.99 a year or $99.99 for life. Noxium doesn't sell one.
- 31 languages , and import from Files and by drag and drop as well as from Photos.
#### Where Vaultaire falls short
- Few reviews so far. 72 ratings is a small sample. The average is good, but there isn't much history yet.
- A smaller free plan : 100 photos and 10 videos in total, across all vaults.
- PBKDF2 rather than a memory-hard function. 600,000 iterations of PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 is a standard, reasonable choice, but PBKDF2 needs almost no memory. Argon2, which Noxium uses, is a memory-hard function ( RFC 9106 ): every guess has to use a lot of memory, which makes guessing in bulk more expensive.
- The recovery sentence can be viewed later. Vaultaire's own page says anyone who can open the vault and reach its settings may be able to see it ( vaultaire.app ).
- Some data collected. Its privacy label links your email address and support messages to you if you contact the developer, and collects usage and crash data not linked to you.
- Optimized imports by default. Vaultaire's own guide says imports default to Optimized, which can convert or downscale some photos and videos. Choose Original in Settings to keep files as they are ( vaultaire.app ).
### How are Vaultaire and Noxium different?
On the big things they match: no account, AES-256-GCM on the device, a 5×5 pattern, decoys, and a free encrypted backup in your own iCloud. The differences are in how the pattern becomes a key, how recovery works, the free plan, price and data collection.
#### How the pattern becomes a key
Noxium stretches your pattern with Argon2id (libsodium), and the pattern itself is never stored. Vaultaire uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 with 600,000 iterations and a device-wide salt, and, its site says, keeps recovery information, including the pattern, inside an AES-GCM encrypted recovery database in the iOS Keychain. Both are sound designs; the difference is how costly each guess is for someone with a copy of your files. For the background, see how encrypted photo vaults work and our pattern lock page. Neither protects you if someone watches you draw your pattern.
#### Recovery
Both give you a phrase in case you forget your pattern. Noxium has you write down a recovery phrase at setup, and nobody can reset a pattern, not us and not Apple. Vaultaire's is a 9-word generated sentence, or a custom one of at least 6 words, that you can view again later in the vault's settings. Vaultaire says that on a new device the phrase restores only from an encrypted iCloud backup. Viewable later is easier if you lose your paper copy; not viewable is safer if someone gets into your open vault. More on ours: recovery phrase .
Noxium asks you to write down a recovery phrase at setup. It's the only spare key.
#### Decoys and panic options
Both open a decoy vault with a second pattern. With Pro, both have a pattern for when you're forced to open the app: Noxium's emergency erase opens a harmless vault and erases the others; Vaultaire's duress mode opens one chosen vault and removes the other vaults from the device, while its encrypted cloud backups stay available for recovery with the phrase. Read what a decoy vault is for the limits of both.
#### Free plan and price
Noxium's free plan holds 150 photos, 10 videos and unlimited notes, with 1 decoy vault. Vaultaire's holds 100 photos and 10 videos across up to 3 vaults. For yearly Pro, Vaultaire charges $19.99 on its US App Store page. Noxium Pro is $17.99 a year ( our pricing ). Both sell lifetime Pro for $39.99. Vaultaire's weekly plan is cheaper at $1.99 a week. If Noxium Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up everything already in your vault.
#### Privacy label
Noxium has no ads, no accounts and no analytics, and its label is Data Not Collected. Vaultaire lists no tracking but does list data linked to you and data not linked to you.
### Which should you choose?
Both are reasonable picks. Choose on the details.
- Pick Vaultaire if you want 3 vaults without paying, a family plan, a recovery sentence you can look up again, or the app in one of its 31 languages.
- Pick Noxium if you want a bigger free plan, Argon2id key stretching, a pattern that is never stored, a cheaper yearly Pro, and a Data Not Collected label.
Looking for other Vaultaire alternatives? Obscura and Encamera also need no account; our no-account vault comparison lists their prices and backups side by side.
### How do you switch from Vaultaire without losing photos?
Export to Photos, check the copies, import into the new vault, and only then delete anything.
- Check your import setting. If photos went into Vaultaire under its Optimized setting, the export brings back the compressed copies, not the originals. Compare a few with the originals if you still have them.
- Export each vault to Photos , one at a time, including any decoy you want to keep: unlock the vault, tap Select , pick the items and choose Export or Save to Photos. Note how many items each holds.
- Check the copies : counts match, videos play, dates look right. Exports usually return to their capture date, so look further back in your library.
- Import into Noxium with Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos on, then empty Recently Deleted in Photos.
- Wait for Noxium's backup to finish in Settings › iCloud backup .
- Only then delete from Vaultaire, including its iCloud backup if you no longer want it, and cancel Pro in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions .
Watch out
Exported photos are unencrypted in your library until the new vault imports them. Do the move in one sitting, on a phone only you are using.
Same idea, more room on the free plan
Noxium is free for 150 photos, 10 videos and unlimited notes, with full encrypted iCloud backup and restore.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Are Vaultaire's reviews good?
Yes, but there are few of them. On 28 November 2026 its US App Store page showed 72 ratings averaging 4.7. That's a good start for a new app, not a long track record.
Is vaultaire.app the official Vaultaire website?
It appears to be. The site's footer names Wraxle LLC, the same developer as Vaultaire's App Store listing, and it describes the same app: no account, a 5×5 pattern and encrypted iCloud backup.
What are the alternatives to Vaultaire?
Noxium, which we make, works the most like it: no account, a drawn pattern, AES-256-GCM and an encrypted backup to your own iCloud. Obscura and Encamera also need no account. Keepsafe is the better-known option, with an email account and its own cloud.
Is Vaultaire safe?
It encrypts files on the device with AES-256-GCM, needs no account, and seals its iCloud backup before upload. Like any vault, it's only as strong as your pattern, so use a long one with several turns.
Is Vaultaire free?
Yes, for up to 3 vaults, 100 photos and 10 videos in total, with encrypted iCloud backup. Pro starts at $1.99 a week on the US App Store; lifetime is $39.99.
What if I forget my Vaultaire pattern?
Use the recovery sentence from setup. Vaultaire says it has no account reset or provider-held key, so if you lose both the pattern and the sentence, it can't recover the vault for you.

# Hidden album vs a photo vault app: which do you need?

URL: https://getnoxium.app/compare/apple-hidden-album
Last updated: 2026-11-15

Compare
## Hidden album vs a photo vault app: which do you need?
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 15 November 2026
Short answer
Apple's Hidden album is free, built in and locked with Face ID, which is enough to keep photos out of casual view. It opens with your iPhone passcode, has no decoy, and syncs to every device on your Apple Account. A photo vault app like Noxium adds a separate code, encryption with a key only you hold, and a decoy for when you're made to unlock.
Most people try the Hidden album first, and for many it's all they need. This page compares it point by point with a dedicated vault app, using Noxium, which we make, as the example. We say plainly where the Hidden album is the better choice. Apple's details come from its own support pages, checked on 15 November 2026; for a closer look at the album alone, read is the iPhone Hidden album private?
### Hidden album vs Noxium at a glance
Source: Apple Support, checked 15 November 2026. Noxium: our published facts.
Noxium Hidden album
Price Free for 150 photos and 10 videos; Pro $2.99/week, $17.99/year or $39.99 once Free, built into Photos
Opens with A pattern on a 5×5 plate, separate from your passcode; Face ID optional Face ID, Touch ID or your iPhone passcode
Encryption AES-256-GCM on the device, key from your pattern The iPhone's own encryption, unlocked by your passcode
Backup Your own iCloud, encrypted before upload iCloud Photos; end-to-end only with Advanced Data Protection
Other devices Separate; iPhone and iPad sync is Pro Hidden photos sync to every device with iCloud Photos on
Decoy Yes, 1 free No
Notes Encrypted notes Photos and videos only
Editing and sharing View, export, share Full Photos editing, search and sharing
If you forget your code Recovery phrase you write down at setup Your iPhone passcode recovery
### What does the Hidden album do well, and where does it fall short?
The Hidden album is the easiest private space on an iPhone. Its limits all come from one fact: it's part of your normal library, behind your normal passcode.
#### What the Hidden album does well
- It's free and already there. Touch and hold a photo, then tap Hide . Nothing to install, nothing to pay.
- Locked by default. Since iOS 16, the Hidden album and Recently Deleted need Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode to open.
- You can hide the album itself. Turn off Settings › Apps › Photos › Show Hidden Album and it disappears from Collections.
- Full quality, full Photos. Hidden photos keep their originals, edits, Live Photos and metadata, and you can edit or share them as usual.
- Backed up with everything else through iCloud Photos, and end-to-end encrypted if you turn on Advanced Data Protection.
#### Where it falls short
- Your passcode opens it. Anyone who knows or has watched your iPhone passcode can open the Hidden album. Face ID is a convenience, not a second lock.
- No decoy. If someone makes you unlock the phone, there's nothing harmless to show instead.
- It spreads to other devices. With iCloud Photos on, hidden photos are on every iPad and Mac signed in to your Apple Account, including a shared family iPad.
- Apple holds the iCloud keys unless you turn on Advanced Data Protection.
- Photos only. There's nowhere for private notes or documents.
### How is a vault app different from the Hidden album?
A vault adds a separate lock and its own encryption key. That changes who can get in, not just who can see a thumbnail.
#### A separate code
Noxium opens with a pattern across a 5×5 plate , which has nothing to do with your iPhone passcode. Someone who knows your passcode can unlock the phone but still can't open the vault.
#### A key only you hold
Every photo, video and note in Noxium is encrypted on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM, using a key made from your pattern. Names, dates and places are encrypted too. The Hidden album relies on the iPhone's own encryption, which unlocks with the passcode. See on-device encryption .
#### What happens in iCloud
Hidden photos sit in iCloud Photos with the rest of your library. With standard iCloud protection, Apple can decrypt them; with Advanced Data Protection on, it can't. Noxium's backup is encrypted on the iPhone before upload either way, and goes to its own space in your iCloud, not to iCloud Photos.
#### Decoys
In Noxium, a second pattern opens a separate decoy vault that looks like an ordinary Noxium. The Hidden album has nothing like it. Our guide on decoy vaults explains when that helps.
#### Convenience
The Hidden album wins here. It's free, it's part of Photos, and it keeps your edits, search and sharing. A vault is one more app and one more code to remember.
### Which should you use?
- Use the Hidden album if you only want photos out of your main library and nobody around you knows your passcode. Turn on Advanced Data Protection for end-to-end encrypted iCloud Photos.
- Use a vault app if people around you know your passcode, you share an iPad or Mac, you might be pressured to unlock your phone, or you want notes kept private too.
Many people use both: the Hidden album for things that are merely personal, a vault for things that must stay private. For the full range of options, see every way to hide photos on iPhone .
### How do you move photos from the Hidden album into a vault?
Bring them back into the library, import them into the vault, and then delete them from Photos and from Recently Deleted.
- Open the Hidden album. In Photos, tap Collections , scroll to Utilities › Hidden , tap View Album and unlock it with Face ID or Touch ID.
- Unhide the photos. Touch and hold a photo, then tap Unhide . It goes back to your library at full quality.
- Import them into Noxium with Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos on, so it offers to delete them from Photos after import.
- Empty Recently Deleted in Collections › Utilities › Recently Deleted . Until you do, the copies are still on the phone and in iCloud Photos.
- Check Noxium's backup in Settings › iCloud backup .
Watch out
Unhidden photos appear in your main library until you import and delete them. Do it in one sitting, on a phone only you are using.
A vault with its own key
Noxium opens with a pattern only you know, not your iPhone passcode. Free for 150 photos, 10 videos and 1 decoy vault.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Is the Hidden album as safe as a photo vault app?
Not against someone who knows your iPhone passcode, because the passcode opens it. Against someone just scrolling your phone, it's fine. A vault adds a separate code and its own encryption.
Can someone see my Hidden album with my passcode?
Yes. The Hidden album unlocks with Face ID, Touch ID or the iPhone passcode, so anyone with the passcode can open it.
Do hidden photos sync to iCloud?
Yes, with iCloud Photos on. They stay hidden on your other devices too. They're end-to-end encrypted in iCloud only if you turn on Advanced Data Protection.
Do I need a vault app if I use Advanced Data Protection?
It depends on who you're worried about. Advanced Data Protection keeps Apple out of your iCloud Photos, but anyone with your passcode can still open the Hidden album on the phone.
Will photos I move into a vault still be in iCloud Photos?
Only until you delete them from Photos and empty Recently Deleted. After that, the only copies are in the vault and its own encrypted backup.
### Sources
- Apple Support, Hide photos on your iPhone, iPad, Mac, or Apple Vision Pro with the Hidden album (hiding, unhiding, locking, Show Hidden Album, iCloud Photos), checked 15 November 2026.
- Apple Support, iCloud data security overview (iCloud Photos with standard protection and Advanced Data Protection).
- Apple Support, How to turn on Advanced Data Protection for iCloud .
- Private Photo Vault - Noxium, US App Store listing , checked 15 November 2026.
Apple, iPhone and iCloud are trademarks of Apple Inc., used only to identify its products.

## Calculator# Hide Photos review: how it compares with Noxium
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 15 November 2026
Short answer
Calculator# disguises itself as a calculator and packs in a lot: photos, documents, a password manager, notes, contacts, cloud backup to iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive or OneDrive, and email password recovery. Its listing doesn't name any encryption, and the free version has ads. Pick Calculator# for its disguise and extras; pick Noxium if you want named encryption and no ads or tracking.
Calculator# Hide Photos Videos has been on the App Store since November 2016 and has 28,955 US ratings at 4.4 stars. It's one of the best-known "calculator" vaults: the app looks like a working calculator, and the right code opens the hidden space. This review covers what it does well and where it falls short, from its App Store listing checked on 15 November 2026, and compares it with Noxium. We make Noxium, so weigh what we say about our own app accordingly.

### What does Calculator# do well, and where does it fall short?
Calculator# does more than almost any vault, at a low price. What its listing doesn't say is how any of it is protected.
#### What Calculator# does well
- A convincing disguise. It works as a calculator, so a quick look at the phone shows nothing unusual.
- Many lock options: a calculator code, PIN, password, pattern, or Touch ID / Face ID.
- Far more than photos. Documents, audio, notes, to-dos, secret contacts and a password manager and wallet, all in one place.
- Backup to the cloud you choose : iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive or OneDrive.
- Email recovery if you forget your password.
- Hack Monitor logs wrong password attempts, a panic switch jumps to another app, and a disguise mode shows a fake crash message.
- Cheap. $4.99 a year removes ads and limits. It's actively updated (30 October 2026) and works on iPad.
#### Where Calculator# falls short
- No encryption named. The listing talks about hiding, locking and password-protecting, but never says how files are encrypted, or whether the cloud backups are.
- A disguise isn't encryption. A calculator front keeps out a casual glance. It does nothing if someone gets at the files another way, or knows what the app is.
- No decoy space. The panic switch jumps to another app, which helps against someone looking over your shoulder but not someone who makes you open the vault.
- Ads and tracking. The free version shows ads, and its privacy label lists data used to track you.
- Email recovery cuts both ways. It's a safety net, but anyone with access to that email account may be able to use it too.
### How are Calculator# and Noxium different?
Calculator# hides things behind a disguise and many features. Noxium does fewer things and encrypts all of them with a key only your pattern makes.
#### Encryption
Noxium encrypts every photo, video and note on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM, with a key made from your pattern through Argon2id. Names, dates and places are encrypted too. Calculator#'s listing names no cipher. If that matters to you, ask the developer; our guide on how encrypted photo vaults work explains what to ask.
#### Backup
Calculator# lets you back up to iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive or OneDrive. Its listing doesn't say whether those backups are encrypted first. Noxium backs up only encrypted data, to your own iCloud, and restores on a new iPhone with your pattern; see encrypted iCloud backup .
#### Disguise
Calculator# is a working calculator. Noxium Pro can change its Home Screen icon to a Calculator, Notes or Weather lookalike , and hides vault content in the app switcher and in screen recordings, but it opens to its own lock screen, not a working calculator. For other apps with this disguise, see calculator vault apps .
#### When someone makes you open it
Noxium's second pattern opens a separate decoy vault, 1 on the free plan, and Pro adds an emergency erase pattern. Calculator#'s listing offers a panic switch and a fake crash message instead. See what a decoy vault is .
#### Price and privacy
Calculator#'s yearly plan is $4.99. Noxium's free plan has no ads and holds 150 photos, 10 videos and unlimited notes, with full backup; Noxium Pro is $17.99 a year or $39.99 once. Noxium has no ads, no accounts and no analytics, and its privacy label is Data Not Collected.
### Which should you choose?
- Pick Calculator# if a working calculator disguise matters most, or you want one app for photos, documents, passwords and contacts, with backup to Dropbox or Google Drive.
- Pick Noxium if you want encryption that's named and documented, an encrypted backup in your own iCloud, a decoy vault, and no ads or tracking.
### How do you switch from Calculator# without losing photos?
Move the photos back to your Photos library, check them, import them into the new vault, and only then delete them from Calculator#.
- Count what you have in each Calculator# album, and note any documents or passwords you'll need to move elsewhere.
- Get the photos and videos out of Calculator#, back to your Photos library from inside the app, or to a computer with the Wi-Fi transfer its listing describes.
- Check them in Photos: counts match, videos play, photos open at full size.
- Import into Noxium with Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos on, then empty Recently Deleted in Photos.
- Check the backup in Noxium's Settings › iCloud backup .
- Only then delete from Calculator#, remove any cloud backups you made with it, and cancel the subscription in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions .
Watch out
Exported photos sit unencrypted in your Photos library until the new vault imports them. Do the move in one sitting, on a phone only you are using.
Encryption, not just a disguise
Noxium encrypts everything on your iPhone with AES-256-GCM. Pro can also change its icon to a Calculator, Notes or Weather lookalike.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Is Calculator# Hide Photos safe?
It hides files behind a working calculator and a code, and it's actively updated. Its listing doesn't name any encryption, and its privacy label lists data used to track you. See are photo vault apps safe?
How much does Calculator# cost?
It's free with ads and limits. A year without ads costs $4.99 on the US App Store, and a Premium Features Pack is another $4.99.
What if I forget my Calculator# password?
Its listing says you can recover it through the email address you registered. Make sure that email account is secure, because it's a way into the vault.
Do calculator vault apps really hide photos?
They hide the app's purpose from a quick look. Whether the photos are protected depends on encryption, which a disguise doesn't provide by itself. Many vaults, including Noxium Pro, offer a lookalike icon on top of encryption.
Does Calculator# back up my photos?
Yes, if you set it up. Its listing says it can back up to iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive or OneDrive.

Hide it Pro is a long-running, simple photo hider with albums, a fake-crash disguise, an "escape" code that makes the app look empty, one-tap USB export, and no data used to track you. Its listing doesn't name any encryption, and cloud storage and password reset are paid extras. ### What does Hide it Pro do well, and where does it fall short?
Hide it Pro keeps things simple and makes it easy to get your files back out. What its listing leaves unsaid is how the files are protected.
#### What Hide it Pro does well
- Simple and long-running. More than 13 years on the App Store, rated 4.7 by nearly 25,000 people.
- Albums you can rename and give their own thumbnail, with GIF support, a built-in viewer and player, and moving between albums.
- Easy to get files out. Unhide back to the gallery, or export everything over USB in one tap. That makes leaving, or keeping your own copy, painless.
- Tricks for prying eyes. A fake crash screen, automatic locking when you leave the app, and an escape code that opens the app looking empty.
- No tracking. Its privacy label lists no data used to track you.
- No subscription unless you want cloud storage. The app itself is free.
#### Where Hide it Pro falls short
- No encryption named. The listing describes hiding photos behind a lock screen but doesn't say whether, or how, files are encrypted.
- Backup costs extra for real space. Cloud storage is in its own cloud, and unlimited space is a monthly subscription. The listing doesn't say whether that backup is encrypted.
- Paid password reset. Recovery is sold separately for $4.99, and the listing doesn't explain how the reset works.
- Not updated since 11 January 2026 , and the app is in English only.
### How are Hide it Pro and Noxium different?
Hide it Pro is about hiding and easy export. Noxium is about encryption you can rely on and a backup only you can open.
#### Encryption
Noxium encrypts every photo, video and note on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM, using a key made from your pattern through Argon2id; names, dates and places are encrypted too. Hide it Pro's listing names no cipher. Read on-device encryption for why this matters if someone gets at the files another way.
#### Backup
Noxium's backup is free, encrypted on the iPhone first, and stored in your own iCloud; on a new iPhone you draw your pattern and it restores. Hide it Pro offers backup to its cloud storage, with unlimited space on a monthly plan. For a checklist before you switch phones, see moving a vault to a new iPhone .
#### Decoys
Hide it Pro's escape code makes the app look empty. Noxium's second pattern opens a decoy vault with photos you choose, which can look more natural than an empty app. Pro adds an emergency erase pattern .
#### Forgetting your code
Noxium has no reset by anyone. You write down a recovery phrase at setup, and it opens your vault on this iPhone or a new one. Hide it Pro sells a password reset for $4.99.
#### Price and privacy
Hide it Pro's Cloud Storage is $9.99. Noxium's free plan includes 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes and full backup; Pro is $17.99 a year or $39.99 once. Both report no tracking; Noxium's label is Data Not Collected.
### Which should you choose?
- Pick Hide it Pro if you want a simple hider, easy one-tap USB export, and an escape code that shows an empty app.
- Pick Noxium if you want named encryption, a free encrypted backup in your own iCloud, a decoy with real-looking photos, and a recovery phrase instead of a paid reset.
### How do you switch from Hide it Pro without losing photos?
Unhide the photos back to your gallery, check them, import them into the new vault, and only then delete them from Hide it Pro.
- Count what you have in each Hide it Pro album.
- Unhide each album back to your phone's gallery, which the listing describes. For a computer copy, use its one-tap USB export.
- Check them in Photos: counts match, videos play, GIFs still move, photos open at full size.
- Import into Noxium with Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos on, then empty Recently Deleted in Photos.
- Check the backup in Noxium's Settings › iCloud backup .
- Only then delete from Hide it Pro and its cloud storage, and cancel any subscription in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions .
Watch out
Unhidden photos sit unencrypted in your Photos library until the new vault imports them. Do the move in one sitting, on a phone only you are using.
Encrypted, with a backup only you can open
Noxium encrypts everything on your iPhone and backs up only encrypted data to your own iCloud. Free for 150 photos and 10 videos.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Is Hide it Pro safe?
It hides photos behind a lock screen and reports no tracking. Its listing doesn't name any encryption, so it's best against people picking up your phone, not against anyone who gets at the files another way. See are photo vault apps safe?
Is Hide it Pro free?
Yes. On the US App Store, Cloud Storage costs $9.99 and Password Reset $4.99; unlimited cloud space is a monthly subscription.
What is Hide it Pro's escape code?
A separate unlock code that opens the app looking empty, so someone who makes you open it sees nothing.
What if I forget my Hide it Pro code?
Its listing sells a Password Reset for $4.99. Don't delete the app before you've tried it, or you may lose what's inside. See forgot your vault password .
How do I get my photos out of Hide it Pro?
Unhide them back to your gallery from inside the app, or use its one-tap USB export to copy everything to a computer.

## Secret Photo Vault review: how it compares with Noxium

Secret Photo Vault (Lock Photos) is an all-in-one file locker with folders, many file types, decoy accounts, Wi-Fi and USB transfer, a $6.99 one-time Pro and a Data Not Collected privacy label. It keeps everything on the device with no backup, names no encryption, and hasn't been updated since April 2025. Pick it for documents and decoy users; pick Noxium for named encryption and an encrypted iCloud backup.
Several apps are called "Secret Photo Vault". This review is about Secret Photo Vault Lock Photos , which has been on the App Store since July 2011 and has 27,396 US ratings at 4.6 stars. It isn't Keepsafe, whose App Store name also starts with "Secret Photo Vault" (see our Keepsafe review ), or SPV . Everything here comes from its App Store listing, checked on 15 November 2026, compared with Noxium. We make Noxium, so weigh what we say about our own app accordingly.

### What does Secret Photo Vault do well, and where does it fall short?
It's a capable file manager with a lock, cheap to buy outright and private by its label. Its gaps are encryption, backup and updates.
#### What Secret Photo Vault does well

- One low price. Pro is $6.99 once, with no subscription.

- Decoy accounts. A decoy password opens a separate, harmless set of files, and you can set up several users with their own passwords.

#### Where Secret Photo Vault falls short
- No backup. Everything stays on the phone. If it's lost, broken or reset, the vault goes with it, unless you've copied files off yourself.

- Not updated since 25 April 2025 , more than 18 months before we checked.
- Security-question reset. An optional question can reset your password. Answers to such questions are often easy to guess or find.

Secret Photo Vault offers an optional security question. Noxium has no reset by anyone; you write down a recovery phrase at setup, and it opens your vault on this iPhone or a new one.

Secret Photo Vault is built for mixed files: it opens PDFs, Office and iWork documents, plays audio, and lets you create text notes and voice recordings. Noxium is built for photos and videos, with encrypted notes alongside, and imports HEIC, ProRAW and Live Photos and exports them in full quality with original dates. If most of what you protect is documents, Secret Photo Vault's viewers are more useful; if it's photos, Noxium keeps them closer to the originals.
#### Price
Secret Photo Vault Pro is $6.99 once. Noxium's free plan includes 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes and full backup; Pro is $39.99 once or $17.99 a year.

# Calculator vault apps: how they work and what they hide

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/calculator-vault-apps
Last updated: 2026-11-16

Guide · Choosing a vault
## Calculator vault apps: how they work and what they hide
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 16 November 2026
Short answer
A calculator vault app looks and works like a calculator, but typing a secret code and = opens a hidden store of photos and videos. The disguise stops a quick glance at your Home Screen. It doesn't stop someone who checks Settings, and many of these apps name no encryption, show ads or track you, so read the listing before you trust one.
Calculator vaults are some of the most common photo hiders on the App Store. This guide explains how the disguise works, what it protects and what it doesn't, and what three calculator vaults say about themselves on their App Store listings, checked on 16 November 2026. We make Noxium, a photo vault with an optional calculator lookalike icon, so we say where it fits and where it doesn't.
### How does a calculator vault app work?
It opens as a working calculator. A code you choose, typed on the keypad and followed by =, opens the vault instead of showing a result.
- The icon and first screen look like a calculator. Anyone who opens it sees sums work as normal.
- Your code is the key. At setup you pick a number, such as a PIN. Typing it and pressing = opens the hidden part.
- Inside is a gallery. You import photos and videos from Photos, and many apps offer to delete the originals for you.
- Extras vary. Some add decoy codes, a panic switch, notes, passwords, contacts or cloud backup.
The disguise is a social tool: it makes the app look boring to someone scrolling through your phone. Whether the photos are encrypted is a separate question, and the calculator screen says nothing about it. For the difference between hiding and encrypting, see how encrypted photo vaults work .
### What do popular calculator vaults say about themselves?
Here is what three calculator vaults state on their US App Store listings. None of their listings names an encryption method.
Source: each app's US App Store listing, checked 16 November 2026.
App Ratings Last update Privacy label Backup Paid options
Calculator# Hide Photos Videos 28,955 · 4.4★ 30 Oct 2026 Data Used to Track You iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive $4.99 yearly; $4.99 pack
Calculator Lock - Secure Vault 6,629 · 4.6★ 20 Dec 2024 Data Used to Track You Not in listing $1.99 a week to $29.99 lifetime; Remove Ads $3.99
Private Photos (Calculator%) 457 · 4.1★ 24 Jun 2021 Data Not Collected None; "stored locally on your device" $0.99 to lift the photo limit
- Calculator# is the busiest: photos, videos, documents, a password manager, contacts, notes and to-dos, Wi-Fi transfer, cloud backup, and a "Panic Switch, Disguise Mode & Hack Monitoring". It unlocks with a calculator code, PIN, password, pattern, Touch ID or Face ID. Our Calculator# review goes through it point by point.
- Calculator Lock hides photos and videos, contacts, notes and passwords. Its in-app purchases include "Remove Ads", which suggests the free version shows ads, and it hasn't been updated since December 2024.
- Private Photos (Calculator%) is simple and collects no data, but it was last updated in June 2021. Its listing says photos you import must be deleted from the Photos app by hand.
### What does the calculator disguise protect against?
It protects against a casual look. Someone swiping through your Home Screen, or opening the app, sees a calculator.
- A partner, child or friend holding your phone for a minute is unlikely to try a code on a calculator.
- A photo popping up in the wrong place. Once you delete the originals from the Photos app, they no longer show up in Memories, widgets or Photos search.
### What doesn't a calculator vault protect against?
Anyone who looks at the phone's lists of apps, or at the files themselves. The disguise lives only on the Home Screen.
- The App Store. Your list of purchased apps shows each app by its full store name, and a name like "Calculator Lock - Secure Vault" gives the game away.
- iPhone Storage. Settings › General › iPhone Storage lists every app and how much space it uses. A "calculator" holding gigabytes of videos stands out.
- Someone who knows the trick. Calculator vaults are well known. A second calculator next to Apple's own is a hint.
- A copy of the phone's storage. If the files aren't encrypted, anyone who can read the app's storage can see them. None of the three listings above names any encryption.
- A lost phone. An app with no backup loses everything with the phone. Private Photos (Calculator%) says its data stays only on the device.
- The app itself. Two of the three apps above carry the "Data Used to Track You" privacy label. A vault that tracks you is an odd place for private photos. See are photo vault apps safe? for what each label means.
### How do you check a calculator vault before you trust it?
Read four things on its App Store page: encryption, privacy label, backup and last update. It takes two minutes.
- Search the description for "encrypt". Look for a named method, such as AES-256. "Secure" and "protected" alone don't say how.
- Scroll to App Privacy . "Data Not Collected" is best. "Data Used to Track You" means the app shares data for tracking.
- Find out where backups go. Your own iCloud, the developer's cloud, or nowhere. If it's the developer's cloud, look for whether it's encrypted before upload.
- Check Version History . An app not updated in over a year may not keep up with new iOS versions.
- Test before you move everything. Add a few photos, close the app, and open it again with your code. Only then delete originals from Photos, and empty Recently Deleted .
### What are the alternatives to a calculator vault?
Pick by what you're hiding from. For a quick glance, iPhone's own tools may be enough. For anyone who might dig, you want encryption.
- iPhone's Hidden album. Free and built in, locked with Face ID or your passcode. Anyone who knows your passcode can open it. See Hidden album vs a photo vault app .
- Lock the Photos app. On iOS 18 and later, touch and hold the Photos icon and tap Require Face ID . Our guide to locking photos with Face ID has the steps.
- An encrypted vault with a disguise option. Noxium encrypts every photo, video and note with AES-256-GCM, with a key made from a pattern you draw. With Pro, you can change its Home Screen icon to a Calculator, Notes or Weather lookalike; see custom app icons . It opens with a pattern, not a calculator, and the name under the icon still reads "Noxium".
More apps, with and without disguises, are side by side in our full photo vault comparison .
Encryption first, disguise second
Noxium encrypts photos, videos and notes on your iPhone before they're saved. Pro adds plain-looking icons, including a Calculator lookalike.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Are calculator vault apps safe?
They're safe from a quick look, not from a determined one. Check that the listing names encryption, that the privacy label isn't "Data Used to Track You", and that it was updated in the last year.
Can someone find photos hidden in a calculator app?
They can find the app: your App Store purchases list it by its full name, and iPhone Storage shows how much it holds. Seeing the photos still takes your code, or access to the files if they aren't encrypted.
Do calculator vault apps encrypt photos?
Some may, but none of the three we checked says so on its listing. If an app doesn't name an encryption method, assume the photos are only hidden.
What happens if I forget my calculator code?
It depends on the app: some use an email or security question, and some have no way back. Don't delete the app first; read our guide to a forgotten vault password .
Is there a calculator vault without ads?
Yes. Private Photos (Calculator%) lists no ads and collects no data, but it hasn't been updated since 2021. Our list of vaults without subscriptions or ads has more.

# Decoy vault: a second pattern that opens a harmless vault

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/decoy-vault
Last updated: 2026-11-16

Feature
## Decoy vault: a second pattern that opens a harmless vault
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 16 November 2026
Short answer
In Noxium, a second pattern opens a separate, harmless vault that looks like an ordinary Noxium. Nothing on the lock screen or in Settings shows that other vaults exist. The free plan includes 1 decoy vault; Pro adds as many as you like.
Sometimes the threat isn't a hacker. It's a person standing next to you saying "open it". A decoy vault gives you something to open. Noxium, the photo vault we make, builds decoys in from the start: each vault has its own pattern, its own encryption keys and its own contents. This page covers how Noxium's decoy works, how to set one up, and what it can't do. For decoys in general, across apps, read what is a decoy vault?
### How does Noxium's decoy vault work?
Every pattern you set opens exactly one vault. Your main pattern opens your real vault; a decoy pattern opens the decoy.
- One lock screen for all vaults. You draw on the same 5×5 plate of bolts. Noxium tries the pattern and opens whichever vault it belongs to.
- Separate keys. Each vault's key is made from its own pattern through Argon2id, and its files are sealed with AES-256-GCM. The decoy pattern can't open the main vault, and the main pattern can't open the decoy. See pattern lock and on-device encryption .
- No list of vaults. Noxium never shows how many vaults exist. A wrong pattern opens nothing and doesn't hint at what's there.
- It looks ordinary. The decoy is called "Noxium", like the real one. Its Settings look the same, and nothing in it says "decoy".
- Counts stay separate. Backup status only shows items from the vault that's open, so the decoy never gives away that a bigger vault exists.
### How do you set up a decoy vault?
Open your main vault, go to Settings › Vaults › Add a decoy vault , and draw a new pattern.
- Open your main vault and tap Settings .
- Under Vaults , tap Add a decoy vault .
- Draw the decoy pattern across at least 6 bolts. It has to be different from every pattern you already use. Noxium confirms: "Decoy vault ready. Draw its pattern on the lock screen to open it."
- Lock Noxium and draw the decoy pattern on the lock screen. The decoy opens, empty.
- Fill it with harmless things. Screenshots, receipts, food, a few notes. A believable decoy has some photos in it.
- Practise both patterns so that, under pressure, you draw the one you mean.
A decoy can have its own recovery phrase too: open the decoy and use Settings › Recovery phrase , as described on the recovery phrase page.
### When does a decoy vault help?
When someone knows you have Noxium and asks you to open it.
- A partner, parent or friend who saw the app and wants to look inside.
- Someone who takes your phone and demands that you unlock it.
- Showing photos to someone without opening your real vault in front of them.
If you need more than a decoy, Pro adds an emergency erase pattern : drawing it opens a harmless vault and erases the others.
### What doesn't a decoy vault protect?
A decoy only works if the other person believes it. It can't stop someone who knows more than you'd like.
- Someone who watches you draw your real pattern. They can draw it too. Draw with your hand covering the screen.
- Face ID. Face ID opens your main vault, never a decoy. If someone could hold your phone up to your face, leave Face ID off.
- Someone who knows decoys exist. Noxium's decoy feature is public, including on this page. A person who knows may ask for "the other pattern".
- Storage totals. Settings › General › iPhone Storage shows how much space Noxium uses in all. A decoy with 20 photos in an app using 8 GB invites questions.
- Photos still in your camera roll. The decoy protects what's inside Noxium. Delete the originals from Photos, then empty Recently Deleted .
- The law. Some countries require you to unlock devices for police or at a border. A decoy is not a way around a legal order, and this page isn't legal advice.
### Is it free or Pro?
The free plan includes 1 decoy vault. Pro removes the limit, so you can add as many decoys as you like.
The free plan also includes 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, and full iCloud backup and restore. Pro adds unlimited items, emergency erase, iPhone and iPad sync , custom icons, album patterns and shared vaults . See pricing .
Something harmless to open
A second pattern opens a separate, ordinary-looking vault. Nothing shows that the real one exists. Free plan included.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
What is a decoy vault in a photo vault app?
A second, harmless vault that opens with a different code or pattern. You show it instead of your real vault when someone asks you to open the app.
Can someone tell that a Noxium vault is a decoy?
Not from inside Noxium. The decoy has the same name and the same Settings, and nothing lists other vaults. They could still guess from how much storage Noxium uses, or because they know decoys exist.
Is the decoy vault encrypted too?
Yes. Each vault has its own key, made from its own pattern, and every photo, video and note in it is encrypted with AES-256-GCM.
Can I use the same pattern for two vaults?
No. Noxium refuses a pattern that already opens another vault, so each pattern always opens exactly one.
Does Face ID open the decoy?
No. Face ID only ever opens the main vault. To open the decoy, draw its pattern.

# Emergency erase: a pattern that wipes your vaults

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/emergency-erase
Last updated: 2026-11-16

Feature
## Emergency erase: a pattern that wipes your vaults
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 16 November 2026
Short answer
Emergency erase is a separate pattern you set in Noxium Pro. If someone forces you to open the app, draw it instead of your real pattern: Noxium opens a new, empty vault and quietly erases every other vault on the iPhone. You choose at setup whether your iCloud backups are kept. It can't be undone.
Most photo vaults call this a panic button or duress mode. In Noxium, the photo vault we make, it's a pattern, so using it looks exactly like opening the app. This page explains what it erases, how to set it up safely, and when not to use it. It's a last resort, and it's built to be one: there's no undo, no recycle bin and no confirmation screen.
### What happens when you draw the emergency erase pattern?
Noxium opens an empty vault that looks ordinary, and erases every other vault on the iPhone at the same moment.
- You draw it on the normal lock screen. It's a pattern on the same 5×5 plate, so nobody watching sees a special button or a warning.
- A new, empty vault opens. It looks like an ordinary Noxium, with nothing to say it was an erase pattern.
- Every other vault is erased. Your main vault and every decoy vault on the iPhone: their files, their records in Noxium's database, and the Face ID key for the main vault. Noxium's own tests check that no trace of the erased vaults is left in its files.
- Old patterns stop working. Afterwards, your main pattern opens nothing.
- iCloud follows your setup choice. By default your iCloud backups are kept; if you chose to, they're deleted too.
Because the vaults are encrypted, the files that were erased were also unreadable without your pattern. Erasing removes them altogether. See on-device encryption for how that works.
### How do you set up emergency erase?
Open your main vault, go to Settings › Vaults › Emergency erase pattern , choose what gets erased, and draw a new pattern.
- Open your main vault and tap Settings . Under Vaults , tap Emergency erase pattern . It needs Pro.
- Choose what gets erased:
- This iPhone only , marked recommended. Your iCloud backups stay, so you can restore later with your normal pattern.
- This iPhone and iCloud backups . Also deletes the other vaults' iCloud backups. Nothing can bring them back.
- Confirm that you understand the pattern permanently deletes your other vaults, then tap Draw emergency erase pattern .
- Draw a pattern across at least 6 bolts that you don't use for any other vault.
- Don't test it. Drawing it erases your vaults for real. Practise drawing the shape somewhere else, such as on paper.
Make sure your iCloud backup is up to date in Settings › iCloud backup if you chose "This iPhone only". That backup is how you get your photos back later.
### Can you get your photos back afterwards?
Only if you chose "This iPhone only" and your backup was up to date. Then your vaults are still in your iCloud, and your normal pattern restores them.
If you chose "This iPhone and iCloud backups", nothing can bring them back: not us, not Apple. That's the point of that option, and the reason Noxium shows a warning and asks you to confirm before you set it.
### What doesn't emergency erase protect?
It erases what's in Noxium on this iPhone. It can't reach anything else, and it can't change what someone already knows.
- Copies outside Noxium. Photos still in your camera roll, in Recently Deleted, in iCloud Photos, in a computer backup or in a chat app aren't touched.
- iCloud backups, by default. With "This iPhone only", encrypted backups stay in your iCloud. They're unreadable without your pattern, but they exist.
- An empty vault can look odd. Someone who expected to see photos may not believe an empty Noxium. A decoy vault filled with harmless photos is often the better first answer.
- Someone who knows the feature. Noxium's emergency erase is public, including on this page.
- Anything already copied. If someone copied files or photographed your screen before, erasing now doesn't undo that.
- The law. In many countries, deleting data after police or border officers ask for it can be a crime in itself. Emergency erase is for coercion by people with no right to your photos, not for defying a legal order. This page is general information, not legal advice.
### Is it free or Pro?
Emergency erase is part of Noxium Pro. The free plan includes 1 decoy vault, which helps in many of the same situations.
Pro also adds unlimited items, iPhone and iPad sync, custom icons, album patterns and shared vaults . See pricing .
A last resort you hope never to use
One pattern opens an empty vault and erases the rest. You choose whether your iCloud backups stay.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
What is a panic erase in a photo vault?
A code or pattern that deletes the vault's contents instead of opening them. In Noxium it opens an empty vault and erases every other vault on the iPhone.
Does emergency erase delete my iCloud backup?
Only if you chose "This iPhone and iCloud backups" at setup. The recommended choice, "This iPhone only", keeps your backups so you can restore later.
Does Noxium show anything when the erase pattern is drawn?
No. It opens an ordinary-looking empty vault, with no message, countdown or confirmation.
Can I undo an emergency erase?
Not on the iPhone. If your iCloud backups were kept and up to date, your normal pattern restores them; if not, the vaults are gone for good.
Should I use it at a border?
Be careful. In many countries deleting data after officers ask for it can be an offence. Read the rules for where you're going before you travel, and consider leaving sensitive photos off the phone instead.

# Custom app icons: make your photo vault look ordinary

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/custom-app-icons
Last updated: 2026-11-16

Feature
## Custom app icons: make your photo vault look ordinary
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 16 November 2026
Short answer
With Noxium Pro, you can swap the app's icon for a Calculator, Notes or Weather lookalike in Settings › App settings › Change app icon . Every icon still opens Noxium's lock screen. The name under the icon stays "Noxium"; for any name and picture, make a Home Screen shortcut with the "Open Noxium" action.
A photo vault's icon tells everyone what it is. A plain one doesn't. Noxium, the photo vault we make, offers three plain-looking icons, plus a Shortcuts action for a fully custom one. This page shows how to change the icon, what else Noxium hides on screen, and where the disguise ends. A disguise is the outer layer; the protection is the encryption and the pattern behind it.
### Which icons can you choose?
Four: Noxium's own icon and three lookalikes.
The icons in Settings › App settings › Change app icon, Noxium Pro.
Name in the picker Looks like
Noxium Noxium's own icon (the default)
Numbers A calculator
Memo A notes app
Sunrise A weather app
Whichever you pick, tapping it opens Noxium's lock screen, and the vault still needs your pattern. Unlike a calculator vault app , the lookalike isn't a working calculator: it changes how Noxium looks on the Home Screen, not how it opens.
### How do you change Noxium's icon?
Open the vault, go to Settings › App settings › Change app icon , and tap an icon.
- Open your vault and tap Settings .
- Tap App settings , then Change app icon under Privacy . It shows a Pro badge on the free plan.
- Tap the icon you want. iOS shows a short message confirming that the icon changed.
- To switch back, come back and tap Noxium .
### How do you give Noxium any name and picture?
Use the Shortcuts app. Noxium adds an "Open Noxium" action that opens the lock screen and never unlocks anything.
- Open the Shortcuts app and create a new shortcut.
- Add the "Open Noxium" action.
- Add it to your Home Screen with the name and picture you like, from the shortcut's share or details options.
- Move the real Noxium icon off your Home Screen into the App Library, so only your shortcut shows.
Noxium also adds a "Close Noxium" action that locks it at once. You can put it on the Action button on iPhone models that have one.
### What else does Noxium hide on screen?
Your photos stay off the screen whenever the screen could be seen by someone else's device.
- The app switcher. Swipe up and you see a plain panel with the word "Noxium", not your photos.
- Screen recording and mirroring. While the screen is recorded, mirrored or shared, Noxium shows a notice instead of vault content.
- Lock when face down. In Settings › App settings , turn on Lock when face down to lock Noxium when you put the phone down on its face.
### What doesn't a custom icon hide?
The icon only changes the picture on your Home Screen. Everywhere iOS lists apps by name, it still says Noxium.
- The name under the icon. iOS keeps the app's name, "Noxium", under any icon. Only a Shortcuts icon can carry a different name.
- Settings, search and the App Library. Searching for "Noxium" finds it, and iOS lists it by name in Settings and in Settings › General › iPhone Storage .
- Your App Store purchases, which list Noxium by its store name.
- Someone who taps it. They see Noxium's lock screen. They still need your pattern, but they'll know it's a vault. A decoy vault gives you something to open.
- Photos still in your camera roll. Delete the originals after importing, then empty Recently Deleted .
### Is it free or Pro?
Custom icons are part of Noxium Pro. The Shortcuts actions, app switcher cover and screen-recording protection work on every plan.
The free plan includes 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, 1 decoy vault, and full iCloud backup and restore. See pricing .

Several vault apps can change their icon to look like something else. Noxium Pro offers Calculator, Notes and Weather lookalikes. No app can remove its name from Settings or the App Store.
Does the Calculator icon work as a calculator?
No. In Noxium, every icon opens the lock screen, where you draw your pattern.
Can I change the name under the icon?
Not for the app itself: iOS always shows "Noxium". Make a Home Screen shortcut with the "Open Noxium" action and give it any name you like.

No. The app switcher shows a plain panel with the word "Noxium". This works on the free plan too.

# Album patterns: lock one album with its own pattern

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/album-patterns
Last updated: 2026-11-17

Feature
## Album patterns: lock one album with its own pattern
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 17 November 2026
Short answer
iPhone's Photos app can't lock a single album; it only locks the Hidden and Recently Deleted albums. In Noxium Pro, you can give any album its own pattern. The album stays locked inside the open vault until that pattern is drawn, and its photos are sealed with a key of their own.
Sometimes one vault isn't enough separation. You might hand your phone over with Noxium open to show holiday photos, but keep one album shut. Noxium, the photo vault we make, lets you put a second lock on a single album. This page covers how it works, how to set it up, and what it doesn't do. If you only need Apple's built-in options, see how to lock photos on iPhone with Face ID .
### How does an album pattern work?
The album gets its own encryption key, and only its pattern unlocks that key. Opening the vault isn't enough.
- A key of its own. When you set an album pattern, Noxium makes a new random key for the album and re-encrypts the album's photos, videos and notes with it.
- Sealed by the pattern. That key is sealed with a key made from the album pattern through Argon2id, the same slow function that protects your vault pattern. See on-device encryption .
- Locked inside the vault. In the album list, a locked album shows a lock, the words "Locked album" and no cover photo, because its photos stay encrypted until you draw its pattern.
- Albums inside it are covered too. An album nested inside a locked album uses the nearest locked album's key.
- It locks again with the vault. Once you draw the album pattern, the album stays open until Noxium locks. The next time you open the vault, it's locked again.
### How do you lock an album with its own pattern?
Touch and hold the album, tap Give it its own pattern , and draw a new pattern.
- Open your vault and go to Albums . To make a new album first, tap New album .
- Touch and hold the album you want to lock.
- Tap Give it its own pattern . On the free plan, this opens the Pro screen.
- Draw the album pattern across at least 6 bolts. Noxium explains: "This album stays locked inside the open vault until this pattern is drawn."
- To open it, tap the album and draw its pattern on the Album locked screen.
- To remove the pattern, open the album, then touch and hold it in the list and tap Remove album pattern .
Use a pattern you don't use for any vault, and practise it. Noxium can't reset an album pattern any more than a vault pattern.
### How is this different from a decoy vault?
An album pattern hides one album inside a vault you've opened. A decoy vault is a whole separate vault with its own pattern.
- Use an album pattern when you're happy to open Noxium in front of someone but want one album to stay shut.
- Use a decoy vault when someone asks you to open Noxium and you don't want them to see anything real.
### What doesn't an album pattern protect?
It keeps an album shut; it doesn't hide that the album exists.
- The album is visible. Anyone in the vault sees its name and the lock, and may ask you to open it. Choose a dull name, or use a decoy vault instead.
- Someone who watches you draw it. As with any pattern, cover the screen with your hand.
- A forgotten album pattern. Nobody can reset it: not us, not Apple. The vault's recovery phrase opens the vault, not a locked album inside it.
- Copies outside Noxium. Photos still in your camera roll or in Recently Deleted in Photos aren't covered.
### Is it free or Pro?
Album patterns are part of Noxium Pro. Albums, albums inside albums, encrypted notes and a 30-day Recently Deleted come with every plan.
The free plan includes 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, 1 decoy vault, and full iCloud backup and restore. See pricing .
One album, its own lock
Give any album its own pattern and its own key. It stays locked inside the open vault until you draw it.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Can you lock individual albums on iPhone?
Not in the Photos app. iOS locks only the Hidden and Recently Deleted albums, with Face ID or your passcode. To lock one album of your choice, you need a vault app with per-album locks.
Is a locked album encrypted separately?
Yes. In Noxium, a locked album has its own key, sealed by its pattern, so opening the vault doesn't decrypt it.
Can Face ID open a locked album?
No. Face ID can open your main vault, but a locked album always needs its own pattern.
What happens if I forget an album pattern?
The album stays locked. Nobody can reset it, and the vault's recovery phrase doesn't open it, so practise the pattern before you rely on it.

# iPhone and iPad sync: one encrypted vault on both

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/iphone-ipad-sync
Last updated: 2026-11-17

Feature
## iPhone and iPad sync: one encrypted vault on both
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 17 November 2026
Short answer
With Noxium Pro, the same vault stays in step on your iPhone and iPad through your own private iCloud. Only encrypted data travels between them. To add a device, sign in to the same Apple Account, open Noxium and draw your pattern; every plan backs up, but only Pro applies changes made on another device.
A photo vault that lives on one phone is a vault you can't open on the bigger screen. Noxium, the photo vault we make, uses the same encrypted iCloud backup to keep an iPhone and an iPad in step. This page explains what syncs, how to set it up, and what stays on each device. For the backup itself, read encrypted iCloud backup .
### How does Noxium sync between iPhone and iPad?
Each device encrypts changes before they leave it and sends them to your private iCloud. The other device downloads them and decrypts them with the vault key from your pattern.
- Encrypted on the device. Photos, videos, notes, and their names, dates and places, are encrypted before upload. See on-device encryption .
- Stored in your iCloud. Noxium runs no servers. The encrypted data sits in your private iCloud database (CloudKit) and counts toward your iCloud storage.
- Applied on the other device. With Pro, changes from another device are merged into the vault. On the free plan, each device still backs up, but changes made elsewhere aren't applied.
- Only the vault you open. Each vault syncs on its own. A decoy vault doesn't show anything from your main vault.
### How do you set up sync on an iPad?
Install Noxium on the iPad, sign in to the same Apple Account, and restore your vault by drawing its pattern.
- On your iPhone, check that the backup is current in Settings › iCloud backup . Tap Back up now if items are waiting.
- On the iPad, sign in to the same Apple Account with iCloud turned on, and install Noxium. It needs iPadOS 17 or later.
- Open Noxium. On Restore your vault , draw the pattern you use on your iPhone, or tap Use recovery phrase .
- Choose whether to download full-size photos now or later.
- Open your other vaults later. Noxium says: "Any other vaults stay safe in iCloud. Draw their patterns later to open them."
- Pro on both devices. App Store purchases follow your Apple Account, so one Pro purchase can cover both.
If Noxium is already set up on the iPad, use Settings › iCloud backup › Restore from iCloud instead. It brings a backed-up vault onto the device next to the vaults already there.
### How do you save space on the iPad?
Keep full-size copies in iCloud and small previews on the device.
- Free up space in Settings › iCloud backup removes full-size copies from the device and keeps them in iCloud.
- Download all full-size copies brings them back, for example before you travel.
- Wi-Fi only for videos makes large videos wait for Wi-Fi.
### What doesn't sync, and what doesn't it protect?
Your vaults sync. Some settings and keys stay on each device on purpose.
- Face ID. The Face ID key is kept in each device's Keychain and never syncs to iCloud. Turn it on separately on each device, or leave it off.
- Other Apple Accounts. Sync only works between devices signed in to the same Apple Account. To share a vault with another person, use a shared vault .
- Mac, Android and the web. Noxium runs on iPhone and iPad only.
- A pattern someone has seen. Every synced device opens with the same pattern. If someone saw it, change it in Settings › Change pattern .
- iCloud storage. Backups count toward your iCloud plan. If iCloud is full, backup pauses and Noxium says roughly how much more space it needs.
### Is it free or Pro?
Encrypted iCloud backup and restore are free. iPhone and iPad sync, which keeps both devices up to date with each other, is part of Noxium Pro.
The free plan includes 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, 1 decoy vault, and full iCloud backup and restore. See pricing .
The same vault on iPhone and iPad
Encrypted on each device, synced through your own iCloud. Draw your pattern on the iPad and your vault is there.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Can a photo vault app sync between iPhone and iPad?
Some can. Noxium Pro syncs the same encrypted vault through your private iCloud, so both devices show the same photos, videos and notes.
Can Apple see my synced photos?
Noxium encrypts everything on the device before upload, so iCloud holds only encrypted data. Without your pattern or recovery phrase, it can't be read.
Do I need Pro on the iPad too?
Pro is tied to your Apple Account through the App Store, so a purchase made on one device can be used on the other.
What happens to sync if Pro ends?
Each device keeps backing up, and you keep full access to view and export everything already in the vault. Changes made on one device stop appearing on the other.

# Shared vaults: one encrypted vault for you and one other person

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/shared-vaults
Last updated: 2026-11-17

Feature
## Shared vaults: one encrypted vault for you and one other person
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 17 November 2026
Short answer
A shared vault in Noxium Pro is a separate encrypted vault you share with one person through iCloud. It opens with a password of 10 or more characters that you give them in person, never with your pattern, and it never touches your other vaults.
Couples, families and friends sometimes need a private place for photos they both keep: documents, a child's medical photos, or pictures meant for just the two of you. Sending them over a chat app leaves copies everywhere. Noxium, the photo vault we make, lets you share one vault instead. This page covers how it works, how to set it up, and the risks of sharing anything private.
### How does a shared vault work?
It's a vault of its own, stored in your iCloud and shared through Apple's iCloud sharing. A password opens it, not a pattern.
- Its own key. The shared vault's key is made from the password and a salt of its own, through Argon2id. Your pattern and your other vaults play no part.
- Encrypted before upload. Like every Noxium vault, its photos, videos and notes are encrypted on the device with AES-256-GCM, so iCloud only holds encrypted data. See on-device encryption .
- Shared through iCloud. Noxium uses Apple's iCloud sharing to invite the other person. They need Noxium and an Apple Account with iCloud.
- The password is the key. An invitation alone doesn't open anything. The other person also needs the password, which you give them face to face.
- Separate from everything else. Joining your shared vault doesn't give the other person any way into your main vault, your decoy vault or your pattern.
### How do you create and share a vault?
Go to Settings › Vaults › Shared vault , set a name and password, then tap Create and invite .
- Open your main vault and tap Settings . Under Vaults , tap Shared vault . It needs Pro.
- Name the vault and type a password of at least 10 characters, twice. It can't be one that already opens another vault.
- Tap Create and invite . Apple's iCloud sharing screen opens. Choose how to send the invitation.
- Tell the other person the password in person. Don't send it in the same message as the invitation.
- The other person opens the invitation. Noxium shows "Someone shared a Noxium vault with you." They tap Enter password .
- Either of you opens it later from the lock screen, with Open a shared vault .
### When is a shared vault a good idea?
When two people you trust both need the same private photos, and both of you have an iPhone or iPad.
- Partners who keep photos meant only for each other.
- Family documents: passports, insurance cards, medical photos for a child.
- A carer or relative who needs a few documents in an emergency.
### What doesn't a shared vault protect?
Encryption protects the vault from outsiders. It can't control what the other person does once they've opened it.
- The other person's choices. Anyone who can open the vault can view, export or screenshot what's in it. Only share with someone you trust with those photos.
- A relationship that ends. Stopping sharing later doesn't remove copies someone already saved. Think about this before you add intimate photos.
- A weak or leaked password. Use a long password you haven't used anywhere else, and never send it with the invitation.
- Someone who has both. A person with the invitation link and the password can open the vault. Treat them like a key and the address together.
If photos of you have been shared without your consent, StopNCII.org can help stop them spreading on participating platforms.
### Is it free or Pro?
Creating a shared vault is part of Noxium Pro. Noxium Pro also adds unlimited items, emergency erase, iPhone and iPad sync, custom icons and album patterns. See pricing .
Share one vault, keep the rest yours
A separate encrypted vault for you and one other person, opened with a password you give them in person.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Is there a shared photo vault app for couples?
Yes. Noxium Pro can share one encrypted vault with one other person through iCloud. It opens with a password you give them in person, and your other vaults stay private.
Can the other person see my main vault?
No. The shared vault has its own key, made from its own password. It gives no way into your pattern or your other vaults.
Does the other person need Noxium?
Yes, on an iPhone or iPad with iCloud turned on. They open your invitation in Noxium and enter the password you gave them.
Is a shared vault safer than sending photos in a chat app?
It keeps the photos in one encrypted place instead of in chat history and backups on both phones. It can't stop the other person saving copies. See are photo vault apps safe?

# Import and export: full quality in, full quality out

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/import-export
Last updated: 2026-11-17

Feature
## Import and export: full quality in, full quality out
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 17 November 2026
Short answer
Noxium imports from Photos, Files, its own camera and the share sheet, including HEIC, ProRAW and Live Photos. It exports to Photos or Files in full quality with the original date taken. Exported copies are no longer encrypted, so move them only when you need them out of the vault.
A vault is only useful if photos go in without losing anything and come out the same way. Some vault apps shrink photos to save space , or strip the date. Noxium, the photo vault we make, keeps the original file and its date. This page covers every way in and out, and how to move photos without leaving copies behind. If you're switching from another app, see moving a vault to a new iPhone and photo vault lost photos .
### How do you add photos to Noxium?
Tap the add button in your vault and choose From Photos , From Files or Camera , or send items from any app's share sheet.
- From Photos. HEIC, ProRAW and Live Photos come in as they are. With Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos on, Noxium offers to delete the originals afterwards.
- From Files. Photos and videos saved in Files, iCloud Drive or on a USB drive.
- Camera. Photos and videos taken in Noxium's camera go straight into the vault. Nothing is saved to Photos.
- "Send to Noxium". In any app's share sheet. Items are encrypted at once, even while Noxium is locked, and move into the vault you open next.
- Notes. Write encrypted notes inside the vault.
Every item is encrypted with AES-256-GCM on the iPhone before it's saved, with its name, date and place. See on-device encryption .
### How do you move photos in without leaving copies?
Add them, check them, then delete the originals and empty Recently Deleted. The full checklist, including where stray copies hide, is in moving photos into a vault app .
- Turn on Offer to delete from Photos in Settings › App settings .
- Add the photos from Photos and wait until Noxium has finished adding them.
- Check them in the vault: counts match, videos play, Live Photos move.
- Let Noxium delete the originals, and confirm iOS's prompt.
- Empty Recently Deleted in Photos. Otherwise iOS keeps the originals there for up to 30 days.
"Send to Noxium" items go into whichever vault you open next, so open your main vault, not a decoy, after sending.
### How do you export photos in full quality?
Select the items, tap Export , and choose Save to Photos , Save to Files or Share… . To leave another vault app, see how to export photos from a vault app .
- Save to Photos keeps full quality and the date the photo was taken, so it lands in the right place in your library.
- Save to Files saves the original files to Files, iCloud Drive or an external drive.
- Share… opens the iOS share sheet for AirDrop, Mail or another app.
Noxium decrypts a temporary copy to export it and deletes that copy afterwards. If a photo's full-size copy is only in iCloud, use Settings › iCloud backup › Download all full-size copies first.
### What doesn't import and export protect?
Inside Noxium, items are encrypted. Outside, they're ordinary files again.
- Exported copies. They're no longer encrypted. Anything you save to Photos or Files, or share, is outside the vault's protection.
- Originals you forget to delete. Importing copies a photo. The original stays in Photos and Recently Deleted until you remove it.
- Copies elsewhere. iCloud Photos, a computer backup or a chat app may still hold the photo.
- Someone using your unlocked vault. If you don't want export to be possible, turn on Settings › App settings › Turn off sharing . It hides export and share, and stops "Send to Noxium".
### Is it free or Pro?
Import and export work on every plan. The free plan holds 150 photos, 10 videos and unlimited notes; Pro removes the limits.
If Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up everything already in your vault, so nothing is ever held hostage. See pricing .
Your originals, kept as they were
HEIC, ProRAW and Live Photos in; full quality and the original date out. Encrypted the whole time they're inside.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Do photo vault apps reduce photo quality?
Some do, to save space. Noxium keeps the original file, including HEIC, ProRAW and Live Photos, and exports it in full quality.
Will exported photos keep their original date?
Yes. Save to Photos keeps the date the photo was taken, so it appears in the right place in your library.
Can I export everything if I stop using Noxium?
Yes. Exporting works on every plan, and if Pro ends you keep full access to export what's in your vault.
Does importing delete photos from my camera roll?
Only if you let it. With Offer to delete from Photos on, Noxium asks after adding; then empty Recently Deleted in Photos.
